Chapter Notes

“Do you yield?” Mydei asks, his knee pressed tightly against Phainon’s neck.

“I yield,” Phainon replies, breathless.

Even after getting his ass thoroughly kicked, Phainon remains energetic as ever, all wide smiles and brilliant blue eyes. Laid flat on the floor with his arms up and chest rapidly rising and falling, he watches Mydei with squinted eyes and a loopy grin.

Like a lush meadow during springtime, the air is sweet with notes of fragrant citrus and smooth vanilla, cut with freshly picked lavender. It’s cloyingly strong like a thick perfume and brings with it the beginnings of a headache. Mydei is half tempted to cover his nose, but he resists. There’s little use in doing so.

It’s been this way as of late—a new sensitivity to scents when only a month ago he failed to detect any.

Customary as he always does after winning a spar, Mydei pulls himself off Phainon and offers his hand to the alpha. Phainon takes it with grace, his scent softening as blue eyes glimmer.

Their palms connect. A snap of electricity rushes down Mydei’s spine and seizes his throat. He yanks his hand back, his heart drumming fast against his chest.

“Mydei?” Phainon questions.

What the…

His entire body tingles uncomfortably. That singular touch reverberates through his core and lights a flame he never knew existed. The world around him seems to blur in a swirl of muted color.

“Earth to Mydeimos.” Phainon waves a hand in front of Mydei’s face. “I didn’t punch you that hard, did I?”

“Fine,” Mydei manages to say. With a slightly shaky hand, he wipes at his brow. “I’m fine. Worry about yourself first, Deliverer.”

Phainon’s expression dips for a second, and his scent shifts, once bright now slightly charred, but thankfully, he doesn’t press on any further. Instead, he says, “Since you won, I guess I owe you a meal. There’s this new restaurant that opened recently that apparently serves the best stuffed grape leaves in all of Okhema. Are you good with that for dinner?”

“Sure,” Mydei responds. He doesn’t have much of an appetite, hasn’t for a few days now, but if Phainon’s footing the bill, then who is he to refuse?

Dust covers the crevices and dips of his clothing and his cape is a little torn from where it caught onto Phainon’s fist, all remnants of a friendly yet aggressive spar. He brushes himself off and places a hand to his nape where a strange sensation has taken afoot. It feels as if he’s being pricked by a thousand tiny needles all at once, chilling yet blistering hot all at once. He tries massaging the area but a wave of dizziness rushes over, like the high tide overtaking dry rock on a summer day.

“Mydei?” Phainon calls out, turning around. “You coming?”

He blinks. The sensation subsides. “Yes,” he says. “I’m coming.”

ོ༘₊⁺☀︎₊⁺⋆.˚

It only gets worse. Whenever he’s near Phainon, which is most of the time now that he thinks about it, the symptoms flare up. Where words and expressions fail to communicate, Phainon’s scent spills out unrestrained and Mydei, for reasons unknown, can detect even the most miniscule changes, how it brightens into floral notes when he sees chimeras chirping and bouncing around and the slight char when he realizes he bought yet another fake antique.

He finds himself watching Phainon’s every movement, a subconscious want in his chest to keep the alpha happy and content. When Phainon’s scent dips and flattens, it makes him feel deeply unsettled as if his heart is being squeezed and pulled. The desire to bring the smile back onto the alpha’s face becomes overwhelming, fiercely intense as if he’s staring right into Kephale’s never-ending dawn.

… Huh? He almost wants to hit himself.

What is wrong with him? Seriously, what the hell?

At night, he can barely sleep, tossing and turning as the burning in his nape ebbs and flows. His entire body feels hot, the heat blistering even against the chilled air of his bedroom. It’s a miracle he isn’t emitting steam because he feels like he’s being broiled in an oven. Shrugging off his red silk tunic, he pushes it to the side of his bed and lays there in only a pair of thin boxers.

His world is off-center. He doesn’t feel right anymore. There’s no pain, only a strange feeling of dizziness that punctuates his every movement and a weird aversion to the outside world. His head spins, vision a blurry mix of colors and shapes as his surroundings cave in on him, trapping and suffocating him as the walls close in. His sense of smell seems to have also sharpened, much to his dismay, and he can barely leave his room without being inundated with a new bout of dizziness and nausea.

Though he desperately tries to remain unaffected, it’s rather obvious he’s not alright. His fellow Kremnoans, particularly the soldiers he trains with, have begun to question his health, worry present in their voices as they speak to him. He waves them off as he always does.

For once in his life, he’s glad that he’s the crown prince. For better or worse, no one tries to question or argue against him.

Is this some sort of sickness? He ponders to himself but there’s been no reports of such an ailment. It seems only he’s affected. Maybe a visit to Hyacine is in order, but he’s leaving for a rescue mission soon. For now, he feels okay enough. He shouldn’t be so severely affected that he’s unable to complete the mission. Years of physical and mental strain have given him the foresight to know his limits. He’s been through far worse, and in comparison this is nothing. He should be fine. At least, that’s what he tells himself, even as he rubs his arms to abate the chills.

He can’t waste time. There are people who need to be rescued.

The destination is a day's travel away in a far and remote corner of the Amphoreus, assumed to have been abandoned long ago. For most who live in these treacherous lands, Okhema is a safe haven. Displaced out of their homes because of the Black Tide, many have been brought over as refugees, but there are a few villages and small cities dotted all over that refuse to bend down and leave their homes behind, abandoning their culture and history.

Moving over to Okhema means assimilation. Stubbornly clinging onto the last vestiges of their home, many resist until the very end, claimed by the Black Tide before there’s any hope of rescue. This particular village has recently been recently overrun, their pleas for help reaching Aglaea who has requested his assistance.

In the calm of his bedroom, Mydei runs through his cabinets. There’s not much to bring on this mission, but he still wants a few changes of clothing and some basic toiletries. Phainon sits at the edge of his bed, wiping away at his greatsword.

“When are you leaving?” Phainon asks.

“In a few hours,” Mydei replies, distracted. He can’t remember where he put his teleslate. He thought he had it on him, but it seems to have disappeared. It’s not in his pocket or anywhere nearby.

Phainon regards him, doesn’t say anything, only places his sword down and stands up. Mydei is acutely aware of the other moving closer but he doesn’t expect Phainon to place his hand on his forehead. Meant only as a show of concern, it brings yet another shock of electricity, igniting the fire in his body. His breathing hitches and he finds he wants to nuzzle into that touch, wants to bare his neck and—

Mydei pulls away as if scalded.

Phainon stares in mute surprise, his gloved hand frozen in place. He brings it down and blows a stray strand of hair out of his face. “You know, I didn’t want to mention it again but you’ve been acting really strange lately.”

“Have I?” Mydei says flatly. His ears burn as another bout of dizziness makes its way over. Stubbornly, he blinks it away and steels himself, forcing away the vertigo with sheer will. It works a little, if he can ignore the way the reds and blacks of his bedroom seem to meld together.

Phainon laughs. “I’ve been winning more recently and it’s definitely not because I’m improving at such a fast rate, though it would be nice if that were the case…”

“You’re not one to speak like this,” Mydei notes. “Perhaps you should go see Hyacine.”

“I could say the same to you,” Phainon shoots back. “You look paler than usual and have none of the bravado you normally do.”

“Tch.”

Phainon shrugs. “Nothing to say to that, hm?”

“I’m fine.”

“Are you sure you’re up for that solo mission?” Phainon says. “It looks more like you should go rest. I can take it instead.”

“I will go on the mission.” He’s getting a little sick of being constantly asked if he’s alright, looked at as if he can’t take care of himself.

“You don’t seem—”

“Deliverer, I will throw you off my balcony right this moment if you do not stop with your incessant prodding,” Mydei hisses. “I. Am. Fine.”

Phainon puts his hands up. “Okay, okay. No need to get so defensive. I worry for you sometimes, y’know…”

His scent shifts, dulled down. Immediately, Mydei wants to placate him, wants to tell him it’s okay and that he doesn’t mean it, but he shakes away the feeling. The silent wish stays nuzzled tightly against his chest, regardless of how much he tries to pull his thoughts away. He doesn’t even want to begin to think about why he feels like this.

The buzzing and the prickling in his neck worsens by the second, but, still, he wants Phainon here. This will be the last time they’ll see each other for a week or longer. Even a mission as routine as this one can be a cause for disaster.

Mydei lays down on his bed, enjoying the feeling of soft cotton against his bare back. “There’s no need to worry, Deliverer. If I can’t handle it, I will tell you or alert Aglaea before I leave.”

“If you say so…” Phainon says. His attention turns to the device left haphazardly on the nightstand. “Your teleslate is right there, by the way.”

Mydei turns over. “Hmph.”

ོ༘₊⁺☀︎₊⁺⋆.˚

It seems leaving Okhema is the best option to deal with the strange ailments that have been plaguing him. The further away he is from the hustle and bustle of the city, the better he feels. Or atleast, that’s what he thinks at first.

The prickling sensation in the back of his neck subsides for the first few days only to exponentially worsen the longer he’s away. Sometimes he even finds his thoughts flitting to Phainon, wondering what the other man is up to and if he’s taking care of himself. He wonders if Phainon is eating properly and if he’s gotten himself scammed once more. Against all rational thought, he also wonders if Phainon misses him the same way he misses Phainon.

He might be going crazy. This is insanity.

Yes, he does care for Phainon, but never have his thoughts wandered in such an inappropriate manner. And yes, he can begrudgingly admit he misses the other man’s warm presence, his non-stop talking and overly bright smiles, but that doesn’t mean all his thoughts have to center on him. Mr. Sunshine, Phainon’s been called by many an Okheman, and Mydei can’t argue against it because it’s true. There’s a sweetness in the way those brilliant blue eyes curve and crinkle at the edges, and Mydei finds himself wanting to hoard Phainon’s smiles all for himself.

Damn it. He’s slipping again. Shaking away the embarrassing thoughts, he continues to his destination.

Thankfully, the mission goes smoothly. Black Tide monsters eradicated, villagers rescued. No casualties though many buildings have been levelled and the area is almost unlivable with corruption crawling in every corner. The stench of destruction blankets the area, dust from scorched debris and the wailing pheromones emitting from the scraps of monsters etched out of metal and decay.

Mydei runs a hand through his hair as he silently watches the villagers debate about their future. His body feels hot, and his head aches constantly, a pressure behind his temples that doesn’t abate no matter how much he rubs. His chest also aches, sore in a way that makes him feel empty yet full at the same time. The burning in his nape, once a thousand needles, now feels like fire ants crawling and biting all over. There’s even a strange and unwelcome wetness between his thighs that he refuses to even consider. It’s not sweat, that much he knows. Sweat is not that thick.

When they make it back to the city and the villagers are all settled, he meets with Aglaea in the privacy of the Hero’s Bath and recounts the mission, going over any pertinent information and findings. There’s nothing much to speak about aside from the Black Tide continuing to mutate with the corrupted titankin becoming a little stronger and faster than before.

As she always does, Aglaea nods and regards him with those crystalline gold eyes, but somehow, this time it feels different. It’s as if she’s looking through him with the way she stares, unblinking as her expression takes one of deep contemplation.

Her scent remains a careful neutral, instead of overbearing and suffocating. Aglaea, the picture of grace and beauty, is an alpha yet she never presents herself as such, never one to intimidate through pheromones or signs of aggression. Instead, she remains calm and collected regardless of whether she’s on the battlefield or speaking casually with a fellow heir.

“You should go rest,” she tells him. “I recommend taking a bath in your own room and not at the communal bath house. If you wish, you can also bathe in the Chrysos Heir private bath.”

Confused, Mydei asks, “Did something happen while I was away?” His muscles ache from exertion and a hot bath would do wonders to release the tension in his back and the burning in his nape. The public baths have always held a soft spot in his heart and brings back memories of when he first arrived in Okhema years ago.

“It’s the more suitable option,” she says. Her tone leaves little room for argument. “That is all.”

ོ༘₊⁺☀︎₊⁺⋆.˚

The next few days are spent in complete recuperation. Mydei doesn’t go outside at all and instead shuts himself in his room while he tries to figure out what’s going on with his body. It feels like he’s burning from the inside out, and he wakes up in cold sweat every couple of hours.

When he finally feels okay enough to brave the dawn, he finds himself at a complete loss. It doesn’t happen often that he finds himself feeling such, but it’s been a common occurrence as of late. Is he cursed? Did he inadvertently walk into a hex and didn’t even notice?

That would explain the strange symptoms and bouts of bad luck, but never is the answer so simple.

As he strolls down Marmoreal Market for the first time since his return, he instantly knows something is wrong. All eyes are on him, watching, prying. It’s as if a spotlight has been cast down, illuminating and bringing forth all attention.

Then comes the whispers. If they could even be called such. Far too loud and overly excited, almost like they’re egging him on for a response. He does not take the bait.

“Haven’t you heard? The crown prince of Castrum Kremnos has found an omega lover! Seems like it’s true…” one woman says as she watches him walk by.

To which her friend giggles and responds, “Really now? First I’ve heard of that… Well, what are you waiting for?! Spill the details!”

“It’s said she’s a recent rescue from a nearby deserted village. No one has ever seen her face. Seems like the prince is intent on keeping her hidden, you know typical possessive alpha behavior…”

He has absolutely no clue where these baseless rumors originate from and why they seem to be so widespread. His stroll through Kephale Plaza also resulted in the same scrutiny. Yes, it’s true, he had recently been out on a mission and did indeed rescue some civilians trapped within the grasp of unstable titankin, but that’s the entirety of what happened.

Unfortunately, it seems whenever he walks by, no matter what part of the city, whether it's the markets or the baths or the residential areas, he sees groups of people huddling together, whispering and staring at him like he’s some kind of interesting specimen for them to gawk at. The air is heavy with a plethora of scents, mixing together into a strange concoction that makes his throat itch. His symptoms have mostly abated, aside from the heaviness in his chest, but he finds he’s starting to regret leaving the safety of his bedroom.

He’s even had a few of his own countrymen approach him to congratulate him for finding a suitable mate. One soldier, a little drunk, even proclaims the royal lineage to be saved.

“About time, Lord Mydeimos! A beautiful omega she must be to be worthy to bear your pups,” the man says, face red from the alcohol sloshing in his glass. Some of it spills onto his already stained chiton. “The royal lineage is saved! Glory to Castrum Kremnos!”

Mydei has no clue how to react. What is he even supposed to say? All he does is stand there, watching as the man bows and hobbles off.

It seems like the best way to get over ideological and cultural differences is gossip. He’s never seen the people of Okhema so united, all over a frankly idiotic and unfounded rumor no less. Maybe it’s a good thing? He reminds himself to tell Aglaea about this new tactic, camaraderie through gossip, though she probably already knows.

“What do you think she looks like?”

“She must be a catch to strike the fancy of the crown prince.”

“Her scent is so sweet and inviting. Any alpha would fall on their knees—Hey! What was that for?!”

“Careful! You know how the Kremnoans are. You don’t want to earn his ire.”

It’s rather difficult trying to eat when the restaurant's patrons keep eyeing him. All he wants is some peace and quiet, but instead, he’s getting loud whispers, pointing fingers, and hushed giggles. Though mildly annoying, it’s still not enough to deter him from leaving the establishment. When he first arrived in Okhema, he and the rest of the Kremnoans weren't exactly met with the best reception, so he’s learned to ignore unwanted attention.

Doesn’t mean he enjoys it though.

He can handle the cityfolk, but, of course, his tumultuous day wouldn’t be complete without a visit from Phainon who waltzes in like he owns the place. Truly, a surefire coincidence for him to be at this specific restaurant at this specific hour.

“Mydei!” Phainon exclaims. “Fancy seeing you here! You’ve been ignoring my texts again.”

“Deliverer,” Mydei greets gruffly.

Phainon sits down beside him and calls for a menu. Like always, he’s grinning widely, a blinding ray of sunshine, but there’s a tightness at the corner of his lips that Mydei notices right away.

“I heard the news circulating,” Phainon begins. “Seems like it’s accurate.”

Oh titans, not him too. This better not be what Mydei thinks its about.

“Your entire body is covered in her scent,” Phainon laughs. “I heard you rescued her from some corrupted titankin. Must have been love at first sight!”

Mydei fights the urge to sigh. There it is. His worst fears are confirmed. For even Phainon to believe in such a dumb rumor… He only hopes the other heirs aren’t daft enough to believe these baseless words.

And what does he mean by his entire body covered in omega scent? He doesn’t smell anything. At least, nothing out of the ordinary.

Mydei takes a bite of his pomegranate honeycakes. The warm, cloudlike sweetness melts in his mouth eliciting a small quirk of his lips. He twirls his fork around as he indulges himself.

“So…” Phainon says as he places his menu down.  “What is she like?”

Instead of responding, Mydei takes another piece of honeycake and ensures it’s suitably doused in warm honey syrup, whipped cream, and pomegranate seeds to create the most ideal bite. He’s still aware of all the pairs of eyes on him, but it’s not that big of a deal. He does not, however, appreciate Phainon’s brilliant blues burning a hole through his skull.

Said simply, Phainon is different from the rest of the curious crowd. Mydei almost wants to punch him for believing such rumors. He hasn’t seen the other heir for nearly two weeks and this is his first greeting? Unbelievable.

Though he tries, it seems he can’t hide the slight scrunch of his features. Under Phainon’s watchful eye, nothing goes undetected.

“Mydei,” he says, scooting closer.

“None of your business, Deliverer,” Mydei settles on saying. Really, what is he to say? Especially with so many people around. Anything he says has the potential to set off a new chain of rumors. For now, he has to figure out exactly what caused this weird turn of events.

He comes up with nothing. After meeting with Aglaea, he returned to his residence and stayed there, delirious, until he finally collected enough wits to go outside. Where did these rumors even come from?

Lost in thought, he’s unaware of the hand that reaches out to wipe the side of his lip.

Instinctively, Mydei jerks back.

Phainon smiles. His blinding blue eyes, at first glance, seem innocent, but Mydei can see the deception hiding within.

“You have some cream here,” Phainon says like it's oh so simple. He shows the dollop on his finger. “See?”

The prickling sensation returns once more. Mydei already feels a headache building, just when he thinks he’s feeling better. Great.

“It would be uncouth for the crown prince of Castrum Kremnos to walk around with cream smeared on his lip,” Phainon continues, acting blissfully unaware of Mydei’s inner turmoil. His tongue peaks out to taste the sweetness on his finger, whilst maintaining eye contact.

Brilliant blue clashes against molten amber. Mydei fights the urge to look away, unwilling to concede defeat. It’s strange really. What has gotten into Phainon? Rather inappropriate behavior, if he has anything to say about it.

“Deliverer, you…” Mydei trails off. The stinging in his nape only increases with each passing second. Once more, a thousand burning needles repeatedly jab into his skin. His thighs also begin to ache, the beginnings of familiar wetness.

He’s going crazy. This is some kind of weird fever dream. He’s still asleep in his room, dealing with yet another bout of strange dreams. It has to be, because Phainon would never do something so uncouth and in public no less.

Shocked beyond belief, Mydei settles on what he knows best. He reaches out and yanks Phainon by the collar, pulling him across the table in a clatter of tableware. “Battle me. Now.”

Immediately, the bustle of the restaurant quiets down. All watch with bated breath as the two Chrysos Heirs clash.

“Of course. It would be my pleasure,” Phainon grins, all white teeth and bright eyes. His citrusy scent intensifies, and Mydei feels like he’s about to choke.

The air in the restaurant is stale with little circulation. A cozy establishment with good ambience, but Phainon’s scent suffocates him, wraps around his throat and floods his senses, and he can’t handle it anymore. Mourning the loss of his delicious honey cakes, he throws money onto the table and storms out of the place with Phainon clamoring after him.

He has no clue where he’s going, only a conviction to get as far away as possible as he can from all the nosy onlookers.

“Weapons or no weapons?” Phainon asks as he catches up.

“No weapons.”

Mydei throws the first hit. All the pent up energy and frustration he’s been feeling coalesces into brutal punches and kicks, leaving Phainon on the defensive as he blocks blow after blow.

His control begins to slip and the frustration grows. His attacks, once precise and aimed, become more and more uncoordinated, vicious and almost animalistic in the way he swipes and snarls. Phainon dodges with ease, his eyebrows raising as he watches Mydei slowly lose himself.

“Woah,” Phainon says, dodging a punch that would have landed him straight into Hyacine’s office had he been a millisecond slower. “Pent up, aren’t you?”

“Shut up,” Mydei hisses.

As the fight draws on and more curious cityfolk gather, hiding beneath the shade of the marble pillars, the more his body barely responds to his commands anymore. He swings wildly and without much purpose. The heat brews, and his mind grows hazy.

The battle ends with Mydei pinned flat onto the floor. His vision swims as sweat drips down his temple and stings his eyes.

“I win,” Phainon says, his face a mere centimeter away from Mydei’s. They both breathe heavily, sharing the same air. Each inhale brings a flood of bright citrus and the promise of spring, lush meadows and petals fluttering in the wind.

He’s acutely aware of Phainon on top of him. What is he doing…? Moonlight hair tickles his chin as Phainon presses down and sniffs him.

“All you smell like is her,” Phainon mutters. “Where is your scent?”

I don’t have a scent, Mydei wants to say, but he can’t. His body stays frozen in place, unable to move even as Phainon presses his face into the crook of his neck and nuzzles him.

At once, his face flushes hot red and his pupils constrict into pinpricks. Breaking out of his self-induced stupor, Mydei yanks Phainon by his hair and tugs his head up. “What the hell do you think you’re doing?” he hisses, eyes flitting to the onlookers who have begun to whisper and giggle.

“Nothing,” Phainon says, his blue eyes darkening. He pulls himself off and says, “It’s nothing.”

“Deliverer,” Mydei says, getting to his feet. “You won. I’ll treat you to dinner this time.”

Phainon’s back is turned to him. Like a burning meadow, the air grows thick with the smell of ash and burnt flora. He’s upset, that much rings true.

“No need,” Phainon says. He pauses then turns to regard Mydei with pursed lips and drawn eyebrows. “It’s getting late. I’ll be heading back home.”

Maybe he should say something, but the words are stuck in his throat. All he does is watch as Phainon stomps away. The whispering of the crowd only grows louder but he can’t bring himself to care, not when Phainon is upset with him.

When he returns back to his room, Mydei immediately slumps onto his bed. His neck itches where Phainon so inappropriately made contact and his scent sticks onto him like second skin. He quickly sheds his armor, leaving himself bare with only his undergarments on before shucking off his wet boxers and sliding a hand down his legs to the unbearable ache and the slick wetness pooling down there . The urge to shove his fingers inside to abate the emptiness grows almost unbearable, but he stops himself and buries his face in his pillows instead.

He has to go see Hyacine. This is getting to be too much. What the hell is going on with his body?

And he knows, dear titans help him, Phainon has something to do with this. As much as he wishes to deny it, he can’t. It’s obvious.

Chapter Notes

i want to thank everyone for a great first chapter! 💕 i was a lil nervous abt posting but now i'm super hyped up hehe

Deep breath in, deep breath out, Phainon tells himself as he adjusts his grip on his box of honeycakes—an offering meant to appease. His palms feel gross, sticky with sweat regardless of how hard he’s attempting (and failing) to keep cool.

He stands quietly outside the stairway to Mydei’s private residence, a single-story white stone house bordered by a small but quaint courtyard. Mydei sighs, and types up a quick response asking to meet up for dinner, but his finger hesitates as he hovers over the send button.

No, not yet. He hasn’t even taken the medications yet, and there’s no telling if they’ll even work considering his altered biology. He deletes the original message and instead replies with a simple, “Busy. Will explain later when I’m free. Stay out of trouble.”

Hyacine texted him alerting that she spoke with Aglaea about his need for rest, promising she didn’t spill a single detail about his omega presentation. He’s almost certain the goldweaver already knows, but it’s still a nice gesture nonetheless.

He holds the two bottles in his hand, unassuming in appearance yet housing the very medications that dictate his future. He downs one of each pill with a glass of water then sits at the edge of his bed.

His windows are strewn shut and the lamps are turned off as he throws the covers over himself. He’s tired yet he can’t sleep, his mind a blur of images that coalesce into everything yet nothing simultaneously. He feels like he’s drowning, pulled under by monsters ten times his size. They grab him and submerge him over and over as he struggles and screams.

When he wakes up from the fitful sleep, he’s groggy, but he feels much better. No longer does his skin prickle incessantly. He feels at peace without any annoying buzzing in his head or fogginess in his mind.

The pills seem to work. His symptoms have abated until almost nothing, and it’s no longer overwhelming to step outside. He’s no longer inundated with dizziness and his body feels looser than before, his muscles relaxed instead of tensed.

And thank the titans. Oh, how he could weep. The sticky wetness between his thighs is gone and so is the overwhelming desire to plug his fingers inside to abate the empty ache.

He visits Hyacine again, once more sneaking out during the middle of curtain-fall hour and spending about half an hour navigating through alleyways to avoid even the chance of being seen. He thinks he might go mad if he has to continue such a route and even debates moving closer.

The Chrysos Heir villa is right beside her office, and as far as Mydei knows, only Castorice resides there as a semi-permanent tenant. Maybe he’ll move there, if only temporarily, and find himself a room at the very back of the villa.

With a thumbs up, Hyacine confirms he’s in the clear, a bounce in her step as she regards him with a bright smile. His scent signature is gone, and he’s back to how he was before.

In the calm of his kitchen, he sits at the dining table and stares out the window at the chirping birds and fluttering branches. The sweet tang of pomegranate juice coats his tongue as he takes slow sips. His appetite hasn’t fully recovered, but he feels hungrier than he has in ages.

Everything is fine now. Issue solved. He can pretend to be how he was before.

His gauntleted hand tightens on his chalice. He never envisioned being an omega. Even now, a part of him still denies it. Him? An omega? It’s preposterous.

But how else could he plausibly explain the scent, the wetness, the dizziness, the tingling in his neck? And most regrettably, the overwhelming desire to be plugged up and filled?

Not even for a moment can he allow himself to slip. He has his duty. The flame-chase journey comes first. Amphoreus comes first. His people come first.

Even if he has to hide his true self from view, he will gladly do it. There’s no reason to reveal the truth, not when it’ll complicate the already precarious circumstances. Besides, he’s lived his entire life this way in this strange state of limbo. It’ll be like nothing has changed.

It’s for the best. No one will know. Especially not Phainon.

Chapter End Notes

chapters.title: Chapter 3
chapters.html:
Chapter Notes

The scents catch in his lungs, thick and overwhelming, a heavy, oppressive aura that weighs down the surroundings. Pheromones permeate the trapped air, blending with the sharp tang of sweat and the flame of heightened emotion. He can practically taste the aggression, the loud shouts and clashing of fists.

He almost wants to leave. Backtrack and never come back. The medications have dulled his sense of smell, but it’s still leagues more sensitive than what it was before. His nose burns.

“Your highness,” a soldier greets and the others follow. In an instant, all combat ceases and all eyes are on him. His countrymen straighten, standing at attention, waiting for his call. A customary sign of respect for the general and prince, he should be used to it, but instead, he’s unsettled under such high focus.

It’s risky to be here, he knows, surrounded, caged in by a legion of alphas who are all staring at him with intent. Though it’s not predatory in nature, even if it feels like so, he can’t help the chills that crawl down his spine. If Hyacine were beside him, she would no doubt admonish him for his impulsiveness and try her best to drag him away from here. He silently apologizes to her.

Unfortunately, there’s no better place to test his theories than at the Kremnoan training hall.

Mydei clears his throat and announces, “You may proceed.” Immediately, the soldiers relax and resume their activities.

Even if the medications hide the outward features, he’s still an omega. Being near large groups of alphas, especially those entrenched in a frenzy of combat, is far from the brightest idea, but he rather rip off the bandages than let the wound fester beneath. Whether he wants the title of crown prince or not, he’s the de facto leader of the Kremnoans. If he can’t stand to be near his men, then how could he hope to lead his people?

If the medications pull their weight, then he should have no issues. Hyacine had told him that he could resume as he normally did but to keep an eye out for anything abnormal. Though the flood of scents in the air isn’t pleasant, he’ll get used to it. Probably.

Most embarrassingly, he has to see if he reacts to another alpha. It pains him to admit, but Phainon’s pheromones caused this entire mess. If another alpha could somehow breach his defenses, break through the carefully constructed barrier of the medications, and cause a similar reaction, then Mydei thinks he might be screwed. He should find out now before later.

Krateros steadily roams the premises, arms behind his back as he surveys the trainees. He makes his way towards Mydei with forceful, yet calculated steps, customary of the Kremnoan elite. With a stern nod of acknowledgement, he says, “Welcome back.”

Mydei returns the nod and responds, “Apologies for my absence, Krateros. How has training been?”

His old mentor looks him over, head to toe. “Well. They’ve been asking for you.”

Mydei’s gaze trails the expanse of the hall, the familiar metal domed structure housing hundreds of soldiers at once. New recruits, many of whom he’s never met before, work through structured training drills whilst veterans take training into their own hands either through sparring with one another or fighting enchanted training dummies and simulations of titankin.

Majority of the men here are alphas with only a sliver of beta. Krateros, firmly rooted in traditional values, only recruits those that fit within the narrow range. Female alphas are welcome to join as well, but there are few that go through the doors and stay. He’s tried to argue for the inclusion of all others, even those not Kremnoan, but Krateros holds his ideals steady. Absolutely no omegas and no outsiders.

It’s a danger, he’s been told repeatedly, to house omegas who may go into heat at any time, surrounded by so many hormonal alphas. How ironic.

As they stroll around the periphery, he’s brought back to memories of the time he’s spent here. He had overseen the building of this hall and practically used to live here and the surrounding courtyard. This was the space where he could let loose and fall into the familiar drum of combat without the need to think about the other issues plaguing him. Training consumed half of his life, the other battle. He would spar with his fellow soldiers, any of those who had the confidence to face the undefeated crown prince, though none could even hope to match his tenacity. Not even Krateros himself could land a singular blow.

Kremnoan men were born to be soldiers. Castrum Kremnos thrived off strife—a military city-state that stood only to conquer and expand. Glory in blood, to die in combat was the greatest honor. Thus, male omegas were the antithesis of everything Castrum Kremnos stood for. Men were soldiers, living and breathing the battlefield. Omegas were the homemakers, child bearers meant to create the new generation of fighters.

Incompatible, the idea of being a soldier and a child bearer. Secondary gender manifests late, and there’s little telling what a boy would become, but if the signs were there, then he would be seen as a disgrace. Many male omegas end up in brothels, living in servitude, used as playthings or stress relief by cruel patrons, other soldiers. Male omegas are far less desired, far less fertile than their female counterparts and have difficulty giving birth due to narrower hips and unpredictable heats.

Mydei is well aware of his rapidly declining reputation. If the truth were to come out about his omegan nature, it would only exacerbate tensions and slice through the already precarious peace until near unsalvageable. Half of his countrymen already find him a disgrace to traditional Kremnoan ideals. Even if they would never dare say it to his face, though many have come close, he’s heard the whisperings. He’s been called a slacker, living as a “dishonorable” Okheman, a prince that has betrayed his home.

They pass by a few veteran soldiers, men that he’s fought with, bled with. The very same ones that followed him from Castrum Kremnos to Okhema. These alphas have families and are fathers to the first generation of Okheman-born Kremnoans. He’s greeted with a few nods of acknowledgement, while others regard him with narrowed eyes.

“Your highness, welcome back. It’s been awhile,” one man says. Mydei recalls he married an Okheman, much to the dismay of his comrades, and has a daughter, a young female omega with bright eyes and a passion for the arts. The man’s prowess on the battlefield is second to none, thus his reputation has taken far less of a hit than if he were a lesser warrior.

His words have Mydei pausing in his step. He hasn’t been around, that much is true.

Most of his time is spent either lounging around or with Phainon. Or both. Lounging around with Phainon, enjoying each other’s company. He has his fair share of missions, and he does train everyday in some form or another, mostly by attempting to punch the Deliverer’s face in, but his life is far more peaceful. It's a good change.

“We have a group of new recruits over there,” Krateros says, pointing to the group in the back corner of the hall. “There’s one that insists on joining our ranks. He spent days begging outside even after being repeatedly turned away. I need you to decide whether or not we allow him to stay.”

There’s a teenage boy crumpled in the corner. The rest of his group have moved on without him, working on coordinating spear strikes while he trembles and attempts to catch his breath.

A softer, sweeter scent cuts through the dense fog. For a moment, Mydei thinks he’s hallucinating. He turns to Krateros and finds the man watching him, his gaze steady. There’s no betrayal of emotion in those eyes.

Is this a test?

“Your highness!” The boy looks up, his eyes wide as he tries to compose himself in front of the approaching prince. He’s scrawny, soaked in sweat, and struggling to even keep himself upright.

“I apologize for my unruly appearance. Please forgive this lowly one,” the boy scrambles to save. His cheeks burn red as he scrambles to get off the floor.

Mydei stops him and leans down. The boy trembles, but the fire in his eyes burns bright.

“You are new, yes?” Mydei asks. “What is your name?”

“T-This one is named Iavokos.”

A young male omega. The only one amidst a group of alphas and betas. It’s dangerous, yet…

“I ask of you, Iavokos, why are you here? Be warned, there is no glory in battle. Do not mistake violence for honor. If that is why you are here, then you best leave,” Mydei says, causing the boy to stare up at him with wide eyes and a complicated expression. He pushes down the urge to reach out and pat the boy on the head. This isn’t the right place or time.

“I’m not here for glory,” the boy says. He grapples with himself, pheromones waving wildly until it steadies. “I wish to grow stronger to provide for my little sister. It’s not battle I yearn for, only a desire to make sure she is safe and happy.”

Selfless. Children like him will get eaten alive in this type of cutthroat environment, but the stubbornness in the boy's gaze tells him there's not much he can do other than warn. He wants to support the boy, but the road ahead is treacherous.

“I cannot stop you from pursuing this if you so wish, but I want you to understand what dangers lie ahead. It is not an easy path to take.”

The boy nods. “I understand, your highness. It won't be easy, but I will not give up.”

“You are brave,” Mydei murmurs. His golden eyes soften as he says, “Keep your chin up, child. Do not allow anyone to talk down on you.”

Iavokos forces himself upright. There's a obvious stumble in his step, but this time, he manages to get to his feet and stay with little to no issue. With a deep bow, he exclaims, “Yes, of course, your highness! Thank you for your support!”

Krateros looms over, his arms crossed tight against his chest. “Very well. I will pay extra attention to this trainee.” He turns to the boy and says, “The crown prince has given you his blessings. Do not disappoint.”

As they walk a good distance away, Mydei narrows his eyes and says, “You accepted a male omega into the ranks. Why?”

“So I did,” Krateros responds, his gravelly timbre taking a tone of deep contemplation as he strokes his beard. “The boy was relentless. I saw a spark in him I have not seen in years. Maybe it’s time for a little change.”

Mydei almost wants to argue. It sounds preposterous. For a man as steadfast as Krateros to change his mind, there must be a deeper reason, and with the manner Krateros stares at him, it almost feels like he’s being pushed towards a certain response. The crawl of unease nestles itself in his chest.

ོ༘₊⁺☀︎₊⁺⋆.˚

Now that the sweet scent that covered his skin has dissipated, the rumors have shifted from the crown prince of Castrum Kremnos finding his mate and spending all his waking hours with her to abandoning her because she wasn’t to his standards.

“Poor omega she must be! The prince is no longer enamored with her!”

“How unfortunate… She smelled so sweet. Surely, she’s a prize and will bear strong pups. If he doesn’t want her, I’ll take a gander and say she’s not lacking other choices.”

“Do you reckon he’s found another?”

His eye twitches. When surrounded by these loud and tactless gossipers, he knows he has another headache incoming. He’s to meet with Aglaea soon and yet, he has to deal with this. Stepping outside the confines of the Kremnoan neighborhood would inevitably subject him to this nonsense but he didn’t expect to have to hear it until he reached areas of high traffic like Kephale plaza. No, it's everywhere. He almost wishes he had asked to meet via online instead of in person.

Are they not bored? Do they not have other gossip? Can they talk about something else?

Calm down, he tells himself. There’s no use in lashing out. The omega scent that once permeated his body is gone and will not return for as long as he takes his suppressants and scent blockers. Now, all he has to do is weather the storm. They’ll grow bored eventually.

For all the cityfolk wish, they can believe him promiscuous alpha scum for breaking a young maiden’s fragile heart after using her body for days on end. He’s dealt with similar yet outlandish rumors in the past. As the crown prince of the city-state that many call “brutish”, he’s had his fair share of strange allegations. This is no real issue. He rather they believe in that story than find out the truth.

There are consequences to the truth.

And he knows it’s very much irrational. Castorice holds herself in such grace and has no care of her omegan nature whilst he’s hiding from it, attempting to act as if it doesn’t exist. But he’s also very much aware that her curse of death stops many from attempting to harm her. He’s heard passing alphas whispering about her, speaking of the things they would do to her if given the chance. On more than one occasion, he had been tempted to crack their heads against the sidewalk, but Aglaea would never approve.

Keep the peace, she would say. Okhema does not need more internal turmoil. The Council of Elders is watching, waiting for a chance to strike. He knows they are, even if they posture otherwise.

The whisperings only grow louder when he steps foot in the baths to the immediate attention of a large crowd of chattering Okhemans. The bulk of pheromones is muted by the medications, thankfully, but it exists, stronger here than in the rest of the city due to the greater exposure of skin, the lack of fresh air, and the lax mannerisms of the bathgoers. It vaguely registers that this is the first time he's set foot in the public baths since the end of his mission.

A group of omegas giggle at him as their gazes roam up and down. He ignores them and continues on, his boots clanging against the marble flooring with a little too much force in his step. Aglaea is awaiting his arrival. There's no time for this. Strolling through the long hallways, he keeps his gaze trained steadily forward, each stride confident with no wavering to be had.

The curse of death protects Castorice from the touch of scummy alphas, but he doesn’t have the same luxury. He can easily dominate in a fight so long as he’s not bogged down by the fog of heat, but therein lies the issue. He can’t predict his body.

Running from a battle is a coward’s game, but this time, he’s given up before it’s even begun. It’s for the best. An unmated omega, especially one of his age, is a prime target. Under no circumstances does he want to deal with an alpha getting close enough to bite him. He knows what mating bonds are and how difficult it is for a mated omega—whether willing or not—to fight against what’s essentially a permanent brand of ownership.

A bite mark on his neck. He absentmindedly rubs at his nape. The skin there is smooth, untainted. It will stay that way.

When he finally arrives at the Hero’s Bath, he finds Aglaea standing in front of the golden fountain, a deep look of contemplation paints her lovely features as she gazes calmly at the glimmering water.

“Mydei,” Aglaea greets. “How have you been? You seem well.”

He lands beside her and says, “Good. Feeling much better. My apologies if I’ve missed anything important these past few days.”

“I trust you have the situation under control.” She pauses for a few moments, her crystalline eyes looking into him instead of at him. She's picking him apart, wordlessly, in that serene manner she always does.

“I do indeed have some news to share," Aglaea continues. The gold laurel in her hair shines with each graceful, practiced movement. "The villagers you rescued have settled in quite nicely to their new lodgings, and as per your instruction, I have made the arrangements for the chief’s daughter. She has since met with me to privately say her thanks and wishes to extend them to you as well.”

“I hope she has found herself happy and free of obligation.”

“Indeed, she has,” Aglaea says, her eyes softening. “It is rather unfortunate for ones born in such circumstances to be held back from their potential. Secondary gender should not matter in assessing the worth of an individual.”

Mydei wants to agree, but the words catch in his throat. If only it were that easy.

Aglaea stares at him with a knowing expression, patiently awaiting response. When she gets none, she turns back towards the streaming fountain and places her hand into the water, allowing the gold to fall between her fingers.

“I’m planning a get together, a reunion of the heirs,” Aglaea says lightly. Her crystalline gold eyes seem to glow brighter and her expression takes a wistful note. Her voice sounds almost reminiscent as she says, “Cifera will be visiting Okhema and has agreed to join.”

Cifera? He’s heard of her, her trickery and her stealth. And he knows she avoids Okhema for reasons unknown to him and most of the other heirs.

“The demigod of trickery,” Mydei replies.

Aglaea nods. “You two have not yet met. It will be a great time to introduce yourself.”

“Very well." The prospect of meeting the legendary cat thief does spark his attention. "Let me know of the plans when they’re finalized, and I’ll make sure to clear my schedule.”

“I will alert you therein.”

The rest of the conversation is lax, falling to recent developments in recovering the missing coreflames. Aglaea even asks about how his people are doing and if there's anything she can do for him. She's a born leader, and he appreciates her support. Had it not been for her, his people would have never thrived within these walls.

“Do take care,” Aglaea says as she slowly walks him down the steps, the clack of her heels rhythmic against the marble flooring. “And stay close in case of an emergency. If anything should happen, you can always speak with me. I am here for you as are all the other heirs.” She pauses in contemplation then adds, “Besides Anaxagoras.”

“Thank you, Aglaea. May the flamechase bear fruit.” He turns to leave only to be stopped by a gentle hand on his shoulder.

“It will do you good to speak with Phainon,” Aglaea says, her lips slightly pursed. “He has not been at his best recently.”

“I plan to,” Mydei responds. His heart twists in his chest. “There is much to discuss.”

ོ༘₊⁺☀︎₊⁺⋆.˚

Marmoreal Market is as bustling as he remembers to be with crowds of smiling cityfolk strolling around, vendors shouting their wares, and lively patrons enjoying Okheman cuisine whilst lounging around. The aroma of freshly cooked food fills the midday air.

There’s never a quiet day in Okhema.

A smile pulls at the corner of his lips, threatening to spill over only to dim when he once again feels the stares. Really, what did he expect?

He strides through the market, honing in on his destination and ignoring all else. As he makes his way up the stone steps, he spots a familiar shock of moonlight hair. As he had predicted, Phainon is once again appraising antiques, a concentrated frown on his face as he repeatedly flips the object in his hand.

“It’s been awhile, Deliverer,” Mydei greets.

The very picture of grace, Phainon jerks and nearly drops the rusted mirror he’s holding. Eyes wide like he’s been caught red-handed, he turns and gives an awkward laugh, “Mydei! Didn’t think I would see you here.”

Mydei takes a peek at the artifact. It looks to be Kremnoan by the razor sharp designs, but the uncertainty in the carvings and the obviously flimsy, crumbling material gives its identity away as an obvious fake. Kremnoan craftsmen were renowned for their ability to forge. Never would they allow such poor quality to exist. “Don’t buy that.”

“Fake?” Phainon asks. When Mydei nods, he laughs again and places the mirror back. “Right, right. I knew that...”

“You’re not looking at the amphora ?” Mydei asks, raising an eyebrow. “There’s many this time, of all different colors too... Are they not your favorite? You’ve been stating you wish to increase your collection. Repeatedly, if I may add.”

Phainon turns red. He coughs and says, “Nah, I’m not too into those nowadays…” When Theodoros gives him a look of exasperation, he straightens and says, “Anyways, it’s been awhile. How have you been?”

“Fine.” Terrible.

The medications have done their job. He feels almost normal again if not for the newfound knowledge of his nature. He can pretend all he wants, outwardly act as if he’s still genderless and continue to posture as such, but he’ll never be able to erase the truth.

Phainon tries to act natural, unbothered. If Mydei didn’t know him so well, he would almost be fooled, but the strain of his muscles and his rapidly charring scent gives him away. What Mydei could barely detect before is obvious now.

“Good. That’s good… Love the one word answers. Truly. Glad to know that you’re still mad at me.” Phainon gestures towards the nearby corridors and says, “Let’s discuss somewhere with fewer people.” With a quick and quipped farewell to Theodoros, he stalks off.

“I’m not mad at you,” Mydei states as he follows behind Phainon. Normally, they would stride side-by-side, arms brushing against each other every few steps, but Mydei doesn’t think he can stand to see the expression darkening Phainon’s usually friendly features. And though he feels normal, he’s still apprehensive of steeping himself in Phainon’s scent. It’s better to stay a little distance away until he’s sure his body will no longer react, even if a small part of him wishes so dearly to grab onto Phainon and never let go.

“You ignored me,” Phainon says as they pass the Verax Leo. He leans against the stone railing overlooking the waterfall and says, “For four full days, might I add.”

Ah. “My teleslate died, and I didn’t have the chance to charge it,” Mydei explains as he tentatively settles by Phainon’s side. “I didn’t see your messages until the day I replied.”

Phainon pauses, his blue eyes narrow as he forces a grin, “Busy, huh?”

“I said I would explain when I saw you in person,” Mydei says. “I intend to do just that.”

“There’s not much to explain. Everyone knows what you were doing. Was a fun time, I’ll bet,” Phainon shrugs, attempting an air of nonchalance, but Mydei can easily see the pinch of his eyebrows and the strain in his voice.

And this entire time, Phainon’s scent has been devolving, a sweet spring meadow starting to dry out and burn beneath the sun’s unrelenting rays.

Oh, how badly Mydei wants to grab Phainon by his two unruly hair strands and chuck him across the room. His hand twitches, yet his restraint holds.

“I fell sick,” Mydei explains as he stares down at the crystalline water. Swirling patterns of purple and turquoise spot the clear surface. “I wasn’t feeling well.”

“Oh.” Phainon raises an eyebrow in obvious disbelief. “You… get sick? Aren’t you immortal?”

Mydei leans in and flicks him on the forehead. Hard. Better that than a punch to the gut.

“Ow?” Phainon responds, his eyes wide as he rubs at the rapidly reddening indent.

With a huff and a glare, Mydei says, “Yes, I indeed get sick. My body is stronger, but I’m still not immune. Are you daft?”

He felt like he was going to die during his pre-heat. Death is not a foreign concept to him. He’s lost count of how many times he’s fallen, yet, somehow, going through pre-heat is worse. Much worse. At least in death, he’s not drowning in a pool of his own slick.

“I’m not daft, only disbelieving,” Phainon says as he continues to absentmindedly rub at his forehead. “What kind of sickness would dispatch you for that long? You’re not talking about your rut, are you? That’s not sickness, my dear Mydeimos.”

For a moment, he debates saying it was rut. He’d get Phainon teasing him for mistaking it as sickness, but it would be far easier to explain. Only he finds posturing as an alpha to be sickening. He is not willing to overstep that boundary. Not now, not ever.

“It’s not rut,” Mydei says. I wish it was rut. I’d much prefer that actually, is what he wants to say.

At this moment, this singular perfect moment, a little boy scampers towards them, his eyes wide as he exclaims, “Your highness! Is it true? You’ve found yourself a princess?”

Phainon turns away.

The boy’s mother runs in and grabs her child, pulling him behind her. She bows frantically, a little out of breath. “My apologies, Lord Mydeimos. Please excuse us.” She pushes her child away as her footsteps clack down the corridor.

The air begins to thicken with burnt flora. Phainon continues to stare blankly at the waterfall, his eyebrows pinching. The urge to placate him is overbearing, and Mydei finds himself scrambling to say, “Don’t believe everything you hear, Deliverer. Truly, the cityfolks’ imaginations know no bounds.”

“So there’s no omega?” Phainon prods. He leans down to pick up a stray strone and tosses it haphazardly into the water. His eyes trail the alternating ripple patterns. “But you smelled like one and I visited you too. I could detect the scent even from outside. Strong, almost overwhelming. It gave me a headache.”

Mydei freezes. “Why were you at my house?”

Phainon shrugs. “I wanted to speak to you in person. You’ve been ignoring me, and I wished to clear up any misconceptions before they festered. It seems only one of us is interested in that endeavor.”

Once a small, controlled bushfire, now a destructive, blazing wildfire.  He wants to scream at Phainon to control his pheromones, but instead, he yanks the alpha by his wrist and says, “We’re going outside. There’s little airflow here.”

“Why are you so resistant?” Phainon asks as he allows himself to be pulled along. “Embarrassed?”

Mydei has to bite his lip from lashing out. Infuriating. Stubborn. Idiotic. He’s not sure if he’s talking about himself or Phainon. His palm burns from the contact.

“It’s none of your business,” Mydei says flatly.

They stride through Kephale Plaza. Mydei ignores the numerous pairs of prodding eyes that turn in their direction. He almost wants to yell at them to get back to business and to stop being nosy, but he knows he’s already causing a scene by showing up whilst dragging along a bumbling idiot.

“Contrary, I think it is my business,” Phainon shoots back.

“It is not. What I do in my spare time has nothing to do with you.” Liar.

“You spend most of your spare time with me,” Phainon says as he pulls up his fingers to count. “Like eighty percent.”

Mydei’s head spins in a whirl of contradiction. A little voice in the back of his head tells him to apologize to the alpha. It wants so badly to placate Phainon, wants to tell him, it’s me, I’m the omega. Please don’t be angry at me. But he shakes away those thoughts, slams them onto the ground and eviscerates them until they cease to exist, and allows the indignation to overtake the shame.

“I will not entertain this conversation any longer.” Stop. Please. I can’t tell you the truth. Not now.

His words have the opposite effect. Phainon shows off his sharp canines and says, “Are you ashamed of her? Is that why? Was this some sort of mistake? You don’t smell like her any longer. Did you toss her aside?”

The charred scent overwhelms him, and anger brews hot, spilling over in a tidal wave of hurt. He almost can’t handle it anymore, but he manages to stop himself from lashing out. He stills in his step only for Phainon to say, “You seem ashamed.”

The restraint Mydei so desperately holds onto snaps. With a frustrated growl, he yanks Phainon by the leather strap crossing his chest and roughly slams him against the nearest wall. His voice lowers, “ Deliverer. Cease this at once.”

Unfazed, Phainon smiles, devious and lopsided as if he’s entertained by Mydei’s outburst. He even has the audacity to laugh when Mydei pushes him further into the white stone. Their faces are mere centimeters apart, breaths intermingling, eyes locked in a heated battle.

Without missing a beat, Phainon leans closer and murmurs hot in his ear, “Mydeimos, there’s no need to be so defensive. I’m only asking honest questions here. Her sickly sweet scent once covered your entire body…” He wrinkles his nose, revisiting the unpleasant sensation. “And now, it's completely gone. What else am I supposed to think? Was she a fling? I didn’t think Kremnoans were the type, but I’ve seen the way your men look at and speak about omegas.”

Sickly sweet. Mydei’s grip trembles.

He thinks your scent is sickly sweet. He doesn’t like it. He said it gave him a headache. He will never—

Shut up. Shut up. Shut up.

The pangs in his chest grow unbearable, yet he claws away the upset and snarls, “Drop it.”

Phainon twirls blonde strands, lets it fall in between his fingers. His blue eyes shine glint in dark amusement as he says, “Why so defensive? Are you hiding something, hm?”

His heart skips a beat, yet he scoffs, “I have nothing to hide. Why are you so insistent? It’s bordering on inappropriate.”

“I’m only curious to see who could have caught the eye of the famous crown prince of Castrum Kremnos, that’s all,” Phainon replies airily. “Surely, she must have been something special, but I guess not if you’ve dropped her that easily.”

Mydei’s eyes darken, shadows cast over the gold by the curve of his eyelashes. “Deliverer, do you sincerely believe me as that sort? The type to toss those aside?”

Brilliant blue clashes with molten amber. A voice in the back of his head, once quiet and negligible, now screams at him to submit, to look away, that he shouldn’t be challenging his alpha like this, that he should bow down and apologize—

But he holds on. His gauntlets claw into the leather. The world narrows.

It’s only the two of them. All else melts away.

The first to turn away is Phainon. The fire dims, and his scent flattens. He looks lost, upset, a swirl of emotion darkening his vibrant blue eyes. His head bows down in defeat. “No, I don’t. I… I misspoke.” The tension leaves his shoulders, and he slumps in Mydei’s grip, seeming much like a scolded puppy.

Mydei releases his hold. The anger melts into upset, and he turns away to hide the twisting of his features. “Let’s agree to not discuss this further.”

“I agree,” Phainon says softly as he dusts himself off. “My apologies, Mydei. I let my emotions get the better of me.”

Mydei surveys their surroundings, relieved to find there’s no eavesdropping passersby. “Control your pheromones, Deliverer. I do believe Aglaea has told you already.”

A sheepish laugh falls from Phainon’s lips. He runs a shaky hand through his moonlight hair. “I’m trying. Aglaea has actually been giving me lessons! Not sure if they’re working though.... I don’t know what’s wrong with me since I’ve never had this type of trouble before. Seems like it’s only been this… past week…” He coughs. “Yeah… So, uh—”

“I still owe you dinner from our last spar,” Mydei interrupts, sparing Phainon the embarrassment of rambling on and on. He turns to meet the other’s gaze and says, “Shall we?”

Phainon nods and attempts a smile. It doesn’t quite reach his eyes.

ོ༘₊⁺☀︎₊⁺⋆.˚

Dinner goes on well enough, far less awkward than he expects. Phainon acts as if their previous fight hadn’t happened at all. No mention of anything related to scents or rumors.

He’s glad for it. Truthfully, he doesn’t think he can handle having Phainon angry at him. His own rage has long since dissipated, leaving only a forlorn emptiness that has him struggling with every breath he takes.

Lashing out was a mistake. Phainon didn’t deserve it. After all, it’s only natural for him to be curious. His responses were rather flimsy, but he doesn’t have much else to lean on without revealing too much.

They grab some fresh gyros from a nearby stand, one that Phainon has pestered him to try for the past few months. It's good, he can admit. The meat is tender, bursting with savory flavor, and meshes well with the soft of the flatbread and the creaminess of the yogurt sauce. The two of them leisurely stroll around the city, snaking through narrow alleyways and taking the paths with the least amount of people.

Phainon chats away as he always does, gesturing rapidly as he speaks about what he’s been up to these past few weeks. Mydei finds his lips quirking up on their own as he slowly closes the distance between their bodies.

With a sheepish laugh, Phainon tells Mydei how he wandered out of Okhema to kill some titankin only to step into some strange ruins that turned out to be enchanted on a loop. He spent hours walking around only to realize he had been stuck in the same place, the door bringing him back to his starting point.

Mydei nearly smacks him for that. Phainon waves him off with a pout, and says he’s fine. No wounds, nothing. It was a good learning experience.

The cityfolk stare at them as they pass by. No doubt, many have heard about what had transpired in Kephale plaza only hours prior, but he pays them no mind.

Phainon wraps a tentative arm around his shoulder, and Mydei finds himself reacting immediately, pushing into the touch instead of pulling away. Maybe he shouldn’t. The smartest choice would be to keep distance, but it feels nice, and he doesn’t want to let go.

It’s as if all is normal again, like everything that’s happened in the past few weeks has only been a dream. Naturally friendly, Phainon has always been more on the touchy side, jumping at the chance for physical contact and never shying away. He’s like this with everyone, and though Mydei shouldn’t, he always indulges. The extra warmth is nice, and he’s missed it dearly.

But there’s that tinge of bitterness, the slight char in Phainon’s scent that doesn’t abate. He’s still a little upset, even if it doesn’t show on his face.

Mydei knows he shouldn’t be so weak as to fall to his emotions that easily but anything regarding Phainon has him acting off . The medications are working as they should. His scent is gone. He no longer has any symptoms, no heat burning beneath his skin, no prickling in his nape, no wetness between his thighs, yet he still feels strange as if he isn’t in full control of his body anymore.

“It’s nearing curtain fall hour. I’ll walk you back to your home,” Phainon says. “I rather enjoy when the Kremnoans glare at me.”

“They won’t if I’m around."

“Nah, they do,” Phainon laughs. “You just don’t see it. For such straightforward people, they can be very sneaky.”

Boots clack on stone. Kephale’s dawn beams down, lighting Phainon in a brilliant halo. His smiles grow wide, brighter. It's almost blinding.

“Deliverer,” Mydei says.

“Hm?”

“I’m sorry,” he says, “for my previous behavior. It was uncouth. I shouldn’t have lashed out.”

Phainon’s expression takes one of shock. He shakes his head fervently and says, “It’s fine. Don’t worry about it.” His blue eyes soften. “I shouldn’t have pushed you so hard. It’s true, what you do is none of my business. I just…” He turns away. “I wanted to know who caught your attention. It’s rare for you… I mean—I just thought, y’know, you weren’t—uh… interested in dating? Though, you are a prince… and it’s your duty to find your future queen, so maybe I’m wrong…”

“There’s no one,” Mydei says. “Believe me.” He can’t tell the truth, but he still wishes to reassure the other as best as he can. Desire blooms in his chest.

Phainon deflates, his eyes downcast. His voice comes out soft. “Alright, I trust you. Besides, I still never apologized for scenting you—”

“Scent me.”

They both freeze.

Phainon chokes, wrestling with words. Mydei turns away, his cheeks beginning to burn.

“I’m only asking this once,” Mydei says. The horror on his face is tangible. “I won’t repeat myself.”

He almost wants to say they’re friends and friends scent each other to show camaraderie, but no, that singular term doesn’t encapsulate the depth of their relationship. It feels almost a disservice to call them that. There’s more weight to what they have than a simple friendship.

“I don’t have a scent I can give you, but I’ll gladly take yours,” Mydei says. His heart thumps in his chest. “I’m not angry over you scenting me. It was unexpected, but not terrible...”

He shouldn’t be doing this, playing with fire. Phainon scenting him had worsened his pre-heat to levels almost unbearable. He’s walking on coals, yet he can’t help but enjoy the burn. The thought of Phainon marking him… it sparks a storm in his chest.

A gesture of possession. That hungry part of him that has reared its head, and it won’t leave until it’s satisfied. It hasn’t even been a few hours, yet he’s already falling back to old habits.

Telling Phainon the truth flashes across his mind. It’s tempting, but he knows if he does, their relationship will change. It’s not that he doesn’t trust Phainon, he does, but his desire to keep his status hidden is priority. Only Hyacine and Aglaea know, and he wants to keep it that way.

“I’m assuming you do indeed take scent blockers and suppressants,” Phainon finally says. He wrings his hands.

Mydei nods. “I do.”

“Why?” Phainon asks.

“Easier this way,” Mydei says. “For everyone.”

“Ah, yeah. An alpha like you would surely dominate the room. Leave some for the rest of us,” Phainon laughs only for it to fizzle out when he finds that Mydei hasn’t taken to the joke. “Ahem. You know, I’d love to know what you smell like.”

Mydei can spot the pink dusting his cheeks. His lips quirk up, “You will continue to wonder, Deliverer.”

Phainon pouts. “Okay, okay. It was worth a shot.”

His real scent is too sweet, sickly sweet as Phainon so nicely put it. The alpha practically admitted point blank that he doesn’t like it, and it makes Mydei feel unworthy. He shakes off the irrational feelings. Maybe when the time is right, he’ll find the courage to reveal the truth, but for now, he will lock that part of him and throw away the key.

Phainon is his equal on all fronts, but if he admits himself to be an omega, reveals the secrets hidden within, will they still be running on equal ground?

“Here?” Phainon whispers, leaning close. His eyes flick around. They’re currently passing down a side street, empty but still open to any passersby. They round the corner and enter a courtyard lined with lilies and wisteria.

“Might as well,” Mydei replies gruffly. “We’re soon to reach my neighborhood. Do you want to do it in front of my countrymen? I’m sure they’ll be pleased.”

“Do you wish for my demise?” Phainon says, the corner of his eyes crinkling. He presses his face into the side of Mydei’s neck as his fingers trace Mydei’s chin. His voice lowers into a breathy murmur, “My dear Mydei, you can be so cruel. Though, I can’t say I’m not tempted… Your people can no longer ignore my importance if I shamelessly scent their prince in front of them.”

“You overestimate yourself,” Mydei says as he wraps his arms around Phainon’s upper back. He feels Phainon’s nose and cheek drag around his neck. Warm lips press softly against rapidly flushing skin. It’s almost tortuous how slow Phainon is going, as if he’s purposefully drawing this out for a reaction. Mydei bites his lip to stop a moan from inadvertently slipping out.

Phainon hums. His arms, once wrapped around Mydei’s waist, have moved upwards to his nape. His fingers gently part the reddish strands. “You always let me get away with it.”

A breath catches in Mydei’s throat when Phainon’s wrists begin to rub slow circles into his untouched mating gland. For a moment, he panics at the prospect of having anything near his nape, but the gentle motions are soothing, and he finds himself melting against Phainon’s sweet touch. There’s no prickling sensation, no thousand needles driving into his skin, only a soft, fuzzy warmth that has his features flushing in content.

This is nice. It feels good. Phainon’s springtime scent is mellower now, sweeter and more crisp. No longer is it cloying and aggressive. He likes it.

Another soft press of warm lips as moonlight hair tickles the bottom of Mydei’s chin. “Mine,” Phainon mutters under his breath, long eyelashes fluttering as they press against feverish skin.

Mydei isn’t quite sure he’s heard correctly. His eyelids grow heavy as he slowly strokes Phainon’s back, running his fingers down the smooth leather, as Phainon continues to mouth softly against his neck. He’s missed Phainon. Missed this.

They’ll go back to how they were before. Rivals. Equals. Fellow Chrysos Heirs. Nothing more, nothing less.

Chapter End Notes
