chapters.title: Chapter 4
chapters.html:
Chapter Notes

His relationship with Mydei returns to normal. Kind of. As normal as it can be given the circumstances. Even so, Phainon is relieved. After the disaster that had been the last week of his life, he’s happy to put it all behind him, toss it in the dark recesses of his mind to never again revisit.

The near constant heartache that has pestered him everyday for the past week has resolved itself, and no longer does he have to deal with the incessant butterflies fluttering around in his stomach, leaving him breathless and gasping for air as his mind inevitably wanders off in directions he wouldn’t broach with a ten foot pole. As a bonus, the people of Okhema have returned to kind greetings and smiles, no longer eyeing him with concern whenever they see him strolling down the streets alone.

Where Kephale’s dawn once burned his skin and irritated his eyes, it’s now warm and inviting, a comforting embrace instead of a searing squeeze. No longer does he have to hide in the shade, and his pheromones have steadied substantially, much to Aglaea’s relief.

Once a week, he sits with Tribbie and Aglaea in the Garden of Life amidst blooming wisteria, multicolored anemone, and floating lily pads. There’s no set meeting time, but it’s been a habit for the past few years to show up every Saturday during the third quint of action hour. Towering willow trees cast speckled shadows as they lounge comfortably in the cool shaded grass.

“I’m happy for you, Snowy!” Tribbie exclaims, unbridled joy flashing in her wide blue eyes when he tells her that he’s made up with Mydei.

In his lap, an orange chimera coos softly, content and fast asleep as it nuzzles against his thighs. He’s glad this one doesn’t have any horns because the last one left a nasty bruise that even had Hyacine startled. Hiding his concern behind a veil of disbelief, Mydei asked why he was limping only for Phainon to admit sheepishly that he couldn’t ruse a sleeping chimera from its hearty slumber.

Soft hums leave his lips as he gently runs his fingers through the chimera’s fluffy red collar, delighting in the feel of warm, fuzzy fur. Beside him, Tribbie bounces around, a white and blue chimera chirping in her arms.

“De is not the type to ignore,” she continues on. “He’s very straightforward!”

Aglaea, beautifully elegant as usual, sits across from Phainon while idly petting a golden chimera. Her lips quirk up, “I’m delighted the issue between the two of you is resolved. If such were to arise again—”

“It won’t,” Phainon rushes in to say. Normally he would never cut her off, but this time, he’s eager to clear his mistakes. “I jumped to conclusions too quickly, even when told repeatedly not to. I worried you both for nothing…”

“Awoo…?” The little chimera in his lap snores and rubs against his thighs. It reminds him so much of Mydei, only smaller and far less aggressive. Equally as adorable though, not that he’d ever admit that part out loud.

“No worries, Snowy! It happens to the best of us! As long as you learn from it,” Tribbie smiles, rosy-cheeked. She releases the chimera in her arms and watches as it squeaks a farewell and bounces off to meet its brethren. “Have you confessed to De yet?”

“Teacher,” Aglaea begins, a touch of concern in her melodious voice.

Phainon laughs a little too loudly. A few passing chimeras pause to stare at him, heads tilted in question, and the one in his lap scrunches its nose and gives a small huff.

He’s fixed with Tribbie’s all-knowing, patient gaze. The laughter surges only to fizzle out completely. “No, I haven’t. I can’t. Well, you’ve heard the rumors…”

“They are completely unfound,” Aglaea says firmly.  “There is no truth in them.”

“But—”

“Agy is right!” Tribbie exclaims, crossing her arms in the same manner Mydei does. When she sees his conflicted expression, she pats him on the head and says gently, “Snowy, you should tell him. You’ve been holding onto these feelings for so long now... The heart’s desires cannot be ignored nor suppressed forever.”

A lone wisteria petal floats down and lands on his shoulder. He twirls it around, moonlight eyelashes casting shadows over his normally vibrant eyes. “It’s still too risky. I have to make sure he reciprocates before I do anything rash.” I don’t want to lose him. “When the time is right, I will confess, just not now…”

“Snowy…” Tribbie deflates.

“We shouldn’t rush him, teacher,” Aglaea says.

Regardless of the warm, pleasant weather, a chill runs down Phainon’s spine. Normally, Aglaea would agree with Tribbie and continue to nudge him towards confessing, yet this time…

As if in agreement, the chimera in Phainon’s lap mumbles out another, “Awoo…”

ོ༘₊⁺☀︎₊⁺⋆.˚ Much of his free time is once again spent with Mydei. They spar, hang out around the city, lounge in the baths. The sight of them together is commonplace as they take to idling around, enjoying each other's presence, and of course, trying to one up one another. All manner of normal.

Only now, Mydei allows Phainon to scent him. Publicly too, even if he does try to half-heartedly push back only to inevitably melt at the first press of Phainon’s lips against his bare skin.

It’s later in the day, nearing curtain-fall hour. Kephale’s dawn shines bright as it always does, covering all in its neverending warmth. Many of the cityfolk have retired for the day, so in the broad daylight, Phainon corners Mydei and presses him against the temple wall. It’s inlaid with a mural of Mnestia in all her glorious beauty, her arms raised up, lips curved into a sensual smile as if she’s overlooking and blessing their union.

This might be blasphemy, but given her title as the titan of romance, maybe she’ll let this slide. Or not. Doesn’t matter either way. He’s not about to stop.

Somehow, no one in the city has caught on yet, but the excitement, the potential of rampant whisperings has him all over Mydei. He can’t get enough, intoxicated as he is by the sight of the other alpha, beautiful, all sharp edges and radiant features.

Mydei glances around, golden eyes flitting corner to corner as Phainon presses soft kisses to his bared neck. Oh how badly Phainon wants to move lower, wants to trail his lips down the crimson expanse of markings covering Mydei’s tanned skin, commit the patterns to memory, but he restrains himself. For now, he’s content with rubbing his scent, staking claim, reminding all that Mydei is his and only his.

No one else can get near Mydei. The Kremnoans can glare all they want. It won’t change a thing. They can attack him all they want with sharp words and even sharper weapons, but he won’t be deterred so long as Mydei allows him.

If he were to think about it for longer than a passing moment, Mydei’s sudden and drastic change in behavior makes little to no sense. In the past, he used to slyly scent the prince, never able to scrounge the courage to bring up the topic and ask for overt permission. Mydei never said anything about it, never once stopping to ask why Phainon had been releasing more pheromones than usual during their spars or why he made every excuse to brush their bodies together. Almost like he was unaware.

But that can’t be it.

“Are you trying to draw blood?” Mydei hisses when Phainon nips him with his canines. Sharp metal gauntlets dig into the meat of his arm. A warning to behave.

“My bad,” Phainon smiles as his tongue peaks out to lick at the rapidly reddening mark. He ends with a soft brush of his lips, murmuring, “I didn’t mean to.”

“Be careful next time,” Mydei says gruffly. Pink dusts his cheeks, and Phainon delights in it, delights in the reactions that only he can draw out.

Next time. Those two words reverberate in his head. Mydei wants a next time. And possibly a time after. And after. His brilliant blues shine as he slowly trails his hands down Mydei’s muscled back, the tip of his fingers ghosting down the curve of his spine.

The prince tenses only to relax once more, almost like he’s at war with himself, melting and freezing on repeat, but never once telling Phainon to stop.

Maybe he should know better than to continue steeping Mydei, a fellow alpha, in his scent, rubbing himself all over, covering his mating gland. He’s surprised Mydei lets him, bares his neck out for him in an almost coy manner, and flutters his eyelashes as he tries to hold back small gasps.

What Phainon is doing is an obvious stake for claim, marking someone’s mating gland in such a forthright manner, yet Mydei doesn’t seem to mind or care.

Phainon pulls away first this time much to Mydei’s confusion. Long eyelashes cast shadows over his eyes as he runs a hand through his moonlight locks. His thoughts always stray in this manner, but he can’t help it. Not when he has Mydei in front of him, looking so vulnerable in ways Phainon never thought he would.

Are his affections returned? Does Mydei feel the same way?

No, he can’t jump to conclusions yet. Truth to be told, he didn’t think he would get this far. Never in his wildest dreams did he think Mydei would allow him this… this intimacy.

“I’ll see you tomorrow?” he says, attempting nonchalance. “Same time, same place.”

Mydei nods. He presses a tentative finger to the bruise on his neck, golden eyes glowing beneath the shadows cast by the temple’s pillars. There’s no scent on his body, and it bothers Phainon more than it should.

The stake for claim is one-sided. Mydei will not scent him. And even told him point blank that he will continue to stay scentless, on those medications. If Mydei were to scent him back, it would be confirmation that Mydei returned his affections. Then he could confess.

Why Mydei even takes those pills in the first place is lost on him. There’s little to no reason, especially for a warrior meant to command attention on the battlefield. An alpha’s pheromones are their greatest source of power, capable of controlling and silencing those lesser. The potential to subjugate is a tool many rulers have used to their advantage, and even common foot soldiers are trained to sharpen and hone their pheromones to use against their enemies. As far as he remembers, Kremnoans take it very seriously.

Well, whatever. He'll continue testing the waters before finding the correct time to plunge right in. Phainon isn’t going to look a gift dromas in the mouth. The teeth might not be perfect, but who is he to complain?

ོོ༘༘₊⁺☀︎₊⁺⋆.˚

The days go by in a blur. Okhema, for the most part, is peaceful. No attacks from invading titankin, no huge calamities, no calls for emergency missions or dispatching of the army.

By all means, Phainon should be relaxed, content. Especially today of all days. What he thought was another normal weekday.

Entry hour had been filled—no, flooded—with antique appraisal. A recent excavation had unearthed many never before seen artifacts, overloading Okhema with wares, and Phainon had the first pick due to his status as Chrysos Heir. Much to Aglaea and Mydei’s exponentially increasing exasperation, his home is now stuffed with even more trinkets, glazed vases with curved handles, ceramic plates artfully decorated with mythical scenes, and even shimmering crystalline jewels, his favorite being an amber gem flecked with orange that reminds him of Mydei’s eyes. Some of them might be fake, yes, and his wallet may be completely empty, relieved of its heavy financial burden, but he’s felt more content than he has in a long while. An abuse of power on his end to take first pickings, but Theodoros offered, and he’s not about to say no.

Afternoon had his customary spar with Mydei, this time with weapons. Mydei had chosen a sword, and of course, Phainon kept to his greatsword. The spar stayed even, lasting for hours, only to end with the tip of Mydei’s sword tucked under his chin, both of them glowing beneath the dawn’s rays, breathing heavily but grinning from ear to ear. All in all a good, worthwhile spar, even if Mydei won this time. He won’t next time.

Phainon posits he only lost because Mydei had cheated, distracted him by bearing the purpling bite mark on his neck. For a few precious moments, his mind blanked and when he came to, he had been thrown onto his back with the other alpha asking him to yield. Definitely not fair. Why did Mydei always have to look so perfect? A divine being amongst a sea of normal men.

When he voices his complaints, Mydei scoffs and says, “Stop being a sore loser.”

“Am not!” Phainon argues back. He has little to stand on aside from admitting that he had been staring a little too hard.

Now, they’re relaxing, waiting for the final hours of the day to tick on by. Settled in one of the public courtyards, Mydei lounges beside him. They’re seated comfortably on wooden chairs overlooking a pond full of lotus flowers and elegant luminescent fish, and the air smells softly floral with large stalks of wisteria swaying gently in the spring breeze. Gentle yet melodious chimes of wind bells fill the area.

Only there’s one problem. One tiny, teensy small problem.

It’s not a big deal, really. To think about it is to bring it into existence, so he will ignore it. Continue to play pretend even as he’s surrounded on all sides, boxed in by a city that has an untold favoritism towards a specific fruit . All around him are lush trees dotted with blooming red blossoms—a constant, never-ending reminder.

Relaxation be damned. The hustle and bustle had left him without time to think. Now that he’s lounging around, he’s hit full force.

By far the smartest option is to wipe away all memory of that… that accursed scent. There’s no way he’ll bring it up since he can’t afford to anger Mydei again nor can he disappoint Tribbie and Aglaea with his lack of emotional control. It’s a touchy subject for sure, and the regret from how he lashed out stays palpable, bitter. He acted akin to a heartbroken maiden who had been told her promised lover had left her on the altar for another woman. Only Mydei isn’t his lover. Titans, he’s pathetic.

The sticky omegan scent no longer clings onto Mydei’s skin. Gone. No trace of her left. Disappeared as if it never existed to begin with. Aglaea and Tribbie have confirmed the rumors to be false, but he swears he didn’t hallucinate that scent.

And the itch beneath Phainon’s skin hasn’t abated. No, if anything, it’s gotten worse, the slow crawl, like static electricity, has become millions of red hot needles jabbing deep, drawing rivulets of golden blood. His mind wanders to her , who she is, what she looks like and sounds like, if her voice is as soft and sweet as the scent she exudes and if her body is as warm and inviting. He dare say her scent rivals ambrosia, nectar of the gods.

Maybe he could handle it, toss away all thoughts of honey and pomegranate in his mind, ignore the plethora of trees with their red blossoms soon to become fruit, only there’s one gigantic issue—an issue he can’t ignore in the shape of Mydeimos, fellow alpha, fellow Chrysos Heir, crown prince of Castrum Kremnos.

Phainon glances over and immediately regrets it because Mydei is leisurely swirling his crystal chalice around, taking slow sips from it every so often. The sweet, tart juice has tinted his lips a delicate red, and the small, content smile that softens his striking features only serves to heighten the contradiction blazing in Phainon’s chest. He turns away before Mydei can give him the side eye.

The prince’s love of pomegranates has made itself known—what once barely registered in Phainon’s mind is now very much apparent. Yes, he knows Mydei likes pomegranates, has known since practically the first day they’ve met, but never has it bothered him until now.

Pomegranates. His second greatest enemy. One look at the round shape, the glistening red skin, and the crispy crimson arils has his mind wandering in strange and obscene directions. Even a singular whiff of its juice has his mind buzzing with hot desire, heat curling within his gut.

He’s acting absurd. He knows. Mydei’s eyes flit over to him every so often yet he doesn’t say anything, only continues to bask in the stillness, not quite comfortable yet not quite stifling. They’ve sat here for the past fifteen minutes, resting after the particularly brutal spar that left both of them breathless and aching. While Mydei’s immortal body is more resilient when it comes to taking hits, Phainon doesn’t have that luxury. By tomorrow, he’ll probably be nursing some heavy bruises on his abdomen, but the pain barely registers, not when Mydei is seated beside him, sipping that accursed red drink made from that horrible fruit that seems to populate half of Okhema’s crops.

Stop thinking about pomegranates. Stop it. Stop. Stop.

Silence blankets the surroundings save for the occasional footsteps of passing cityfolk. Phainon stares blankly at the gliding fish and continues to drink his water only to realize his jug is completely empty and has been for awhile now. He’s been chugging away at air.

Mydei glances at him once more as he wipes away a layer of dust on the table and gently places his chalice down. From this angle, Phainon can see the red liquid, can smell its sweet, tantalizing aroma. It threatens to choke him, a shadow of a threat lurking beneath its murky surface. Regardless of all the water he’s drank in the last few minutes, his mouth dries, parched like dried out crops in the sweltering heat of summer.

“Something the matter, Deliverer?” Mydei asks. Sharp golden eyes trace over his form, and Phainon resists the urge to shiver beneath the observant gaze. “The fish can’t be that interesting.”

“They are,” he replies, resting his elbow on the table. With a lazy grin, he waves his hand around and continues, “I rather enjoy watching them swim around. Look at that one on the right, the one that’s wiggling around, trying to bite at the lilypad. It looks more purple than the rest. Isn’t that amazing?”

“Very,” Mydei says dryly.

Phainon’s gaze traces over the crystalline chalice as Mydei steadily strokes the glass, gauntleted fingers running down the body in slow, repeated motions. He holds his expression carefree, resisting the urge to frown and hiss at the crimson liquid. “No milk this time?”

“I ran out,” Mydei replies.

Yeah. Of course. Okay, whatever. If it were pink, maybe it would be more manageable.

Control yourself, Aglaea’s voice reverberates in his head. Deep breaths in and out.

“Did my juice do something to you?” Mydei asks, raising an eyebrow. He pushes his glass towards Phainon, the ornate gold stem glinting beneath the bright sunlight,  “Do you want some?”

What part of my expression makes you think I want some? I don’t. Get that away from me, Phainon wants to say—or scream—only his hand moves on its own, disconnected from his brain. Ok, fine. He’s overreacting. Maybe taking a sip will solve all his problems. The crimson liquid looks a little too much like blood, thick like it too. He brings it up to face, taking care not to inhale, and takes a tentative sip. Sweet and tart, the juice coats his tongue and lands with a slightly bitter aftertaste, lingering in the moments after. It tastes good, complex in flavor, delicious and cold.

Phainon wrinkles his nose. The burning in his gut returns full force.

He shouldn’t have done that. Damn it.

Against his better judgement, Phainon asks, “Why do you like pomegranates so much?” He slides the chalice back to Mydei who catches it, gauntleted fingers curving gracefully around the stem.

With a huff, he rests his back against the stone wall, attempting to act nonchalant. Unbothered. If only that were true. If only his mind weren’t supplying him with a million thoughts at once, and his heart starts to squeeze, compress as if he’s being juiced. Ha. Haha…

He can’t take it anymore.

Before Mydei even has a chance to respond, Phainon starts rattling off transgressions as if the fruit had broken the law and he’s the purveyor of justice, a loyal follower of Talanton ready to pass judgement. “There’s nothing good about these stupid looking fruits! Nothing! First of all, they’re stupidly ugly and bulbous, far too round for absolutely no reason at all, and they’re a giant pain in the ass to peel! And don’t even get me started on the juice—oh titans, the juice—it stains clothing like no tomorrow!“

“…“

“It’s like the fruit knows if you’re wearing white and tries to mess you up on purpose—I can’t tell you how many times I’ve gotten it splattered on me, and I was being extra careful too! Taking extra time to ensure not a single drop got on me and next thing I knew, the entire front of my chiton was splotched red… I even stained some expensive tailored outfits Aglaea gave me and, ugh, let me tell you, she wasn’t happy with me—“

“Deliverer—“

“Don’t even get me started on the pith! It’s thick, way too thick for its own good, and hard to crack open for no reason at all, and then you have to make sure you don’t accidentally eat any of it because it’s super dry, astringent, gross with such a weird spongy, grainy texture that shouldn’t exist because it's an affront to mankind! You also have to pick out the membrane pieces too—which is annoying by the way—because eating that is like eating nasty, bitter wax paper, and there’s a giant seed in the middle of each aril which means you barely get any of the actual fruit and have to deal with spitting out—”

Mydei slams his chalice onto the dusty table. Hard. Gold rattles against aged wood.

Phainon jumps.

A vein ticks on Mydei’s forehead, his patience worn thin. The table cracks, wood splintering where the metal connected. “If you’re splattering juice all over then you’re not opening it correctly. That’s clumsiness on your part, Deliverer. Don’t blame the fruit for your ineptitude. You can swallow the seeds too, they’re edible and good for you.”

Phainon rolls his eyes and waves him off. “I still don’t like them. Grapes taste much better and are far less work for basically the same thing.” He sits back up and clasps his hands together. “And you don’t have to peel them. Just pop 'em in your mouth, and you’re done. Though, I guess you can peel them if you really want to…  My point still stands.”

“What?” Mydei questions, confusion evident in his voice. “I… Okay. No one is forcing you to like anything. Calm down.”

Being told to calm down does nothing to help his mood. His annoyance stews and stews until it boils over in a flood of molten anger, brought forth by Mydei’s irritatingly obvious lack of scent. Mydei is already difficult enough to read, able to keep his expression calm in even the most dire of situations. If only he could smell Mydei, bathe in his scent until his mind is far removed from any thought of pomegranate. He knows Mydei smells good, amazing, the sort of scent that permeates, grips one by the throat and doesn’t let go. After all, there’s no part of Mydei that isn’t perfect.

The red liquid taunts him, mocks him. He needs it gone. Now. Only then can he think straight.

Mydei barely takes another sip before Phainon reaches over, yanks the chalice out of his hands, and downs the rest in one go.

“Here,” Phainon says with a slight wince, wiping at his lip. “I was thirsty, thanks for offering. Make sure to add milk next time. Preferably lots of it.”

Mydei stares at him like he’s grown an extra head or three. Oh how he wishes he had another because maybe one of them would be a voice of reason.

Their fingers brush when Mydei hesitantly takes back his chalice, eyebrows furrowed as he regards Phainon with silent concern. That singular, momentary touch brings shockwaves down his spine, and he’s flooded with the desperate desire to slot their hands together, hold on and never let go.

Tartness covers his tongue and coats his throat in its unrelenting embrace. The itch beneath his skin returns full force, ripping the breath from his lungs. Hot flame burns and burns, his nerves lit ablaze. Desperation grows, and Phainon scrambles to gasp out, “I need water.” His eyes flick over to the fish. “You think the pond water is clean enough to drink?”

The only response he receives is an exasperated grunt. The wisteria flowers cast a shadow over Mydei’s features as he turns his head to the side, away from Phainon’s view.

A short burst of laughter clears through the haze. A brief moment of clarity.

Phainon whines, “Don’t laugh. It’s not funny. It’s not…” He watches as Mydei covers his face in his hands, a slight tremor overtaking his figure.

“I didn’t know you had such a vendetta,” Mydei manages to say, long eyelashes quivering. “Remind me to never bring pomegranate juice in your vicinity ever again.”

Phainon perks up. “Is that a promise? Do you swear on the River of Souls?” He pulls himself off his chair and jumps in front of Mydei, looming over the other alpha.

“Is it that serious, Deliverer? You had no problem before.” When Mydei receives sparkling blue eyes and an overly enthusiastic nod as answer, he sighs and relents, “I swear on the River of Souls, I will not drink pomegranate juice in your presence lest you decide to continue acting like a spoiled, bratty princess.”

There’s a fondness in Mydei’s expression, a shine in his sharp eyes and a soft curve to his lips, that drags the breath out of Phainon’s lungs.

Distracted, Phainon responds, “Good, good…” Only to pause when his brain finally processes Mydei’s words. Indignant, he squawks, “I—What? Seriously? You did not just call me that.”

Mydei stands so they’re nearly pressed chest to chest. He tilts his head, eyes narrowing in amusement as he murmurs, “Princess. ”

Close. They’re so close. He can feel the heat radiating off Mydei’s body. Phainon’s head spins, the taste and smell of pomegranate long forgotten. Before he even realizes, he blurts out, “If I’m the princess, then are you my prince?”

Mydei’s confident expression stalls.

Flustered, Phainon cracks a shaky grin. He even tries to laugh, only it comes out like he’s attempting not to choke and failing miserably.

Oh titans. He did not just say that . Couldn’t he have thought up a better comeback?! Only he didn’t think. Not at all. Not with how close Mydei is, sharing the same air, their body heats mixing.

This close, he can see all of Mydei’s individual lashes, the soft curve of his cheek, and the red flame marking beneath his right eye. The purple bruise on his neck. He’s tempted to take a step back, almost does, but his instinct screams to stay put in place. To step back is to give in.

Though this isn't the first time nor the last, he still acts dangerously off-balance.

Blue eyes flick down to Mydei’s parted lips then back up only to fly back down once more. Oh how badly he wants to kiss Mydei right now. He could. It’d be as easy as leaning in and taking what’s rightfully his. Mydei might fight him, and their relationship might be ruined before it even begins, but the desire clouds his mind. He wonders if Mydei’s lips are as soft as they look.

It’s tempting to fall, to plunge past the point of no return, to claim Mydei’s lips with his... He reaches out and cradles Mydei’s cheek, stroking downwards before settling on his chin.

Mydei freezes. His golden eyes grow wider with each passing moment, pupils constricting as he stares blankly at Phainon, unable to move an inch. There’s little resistance when Phainon gently tilts his chin up.

Slowly, Phainon trails his fingers over Mydei’s parted lips, tenderly tracing the curve with the pad of his thumb. Soft and warm beneath his touch and stained lightly red. Desire burns, and he leans closer.

“You have some juice here,” Phainon mutters as he thumbs at the middle. He’s lying. It’s a stupid excuse if Mydei were to call him out on it. There’s nothing there. He hopes the tremor in his voice doesn’t betray him.

Golden eyes flick down to Phainon’s lips. Phainon continues to close the distance until they’re almost forehead to forehead, white and blonde strands dancing as they brush against each other.

Mydei isn’t pushing him away, and not a single word leaves him. It’d be so easy for Phainon to close the final distance. Only he doesn’t. He can’t. Not now.

He pulls himself away, shattering their shared space. His arm falls slack at his sides, mourning the loss of warmth. “It’s gone now,” he says. “Be more careful next time, my dear prince.”

ོ༘₊⁺☀︎₊⁺⋆.˚

In the dimness of his bedroom, Phainon tosses and turns. All the curtains have been drawn in preparation for the night yet he can’t get even a wink of sleep. For the past few hours, he’s tried every fathomable way to fall asleep including counting chimeras, clearing his mind of all thought—easier said than done, and even playing some boring lecture videos that he saved all those years ago. His time at the Grove may be over, but he knew those videos could come in handy eventually.

Regardless of the stillness in his room, his mind is loud. His heart has thumped erratically for titans know how long. He doesn’t have to grab his teleslate to know it’s nearing the third quint of curtain-fall hour.

Without Mydei around—they parted ways hours ago—his every waking thought is consumed by her . That faceless omega and her stupidly addicting scent. The more he tries not to think about it, the worse it gets. Even his dreams aren’t safe, haunted by the ghost of someone he doesn’t know, has never met or seen or spoken to.

There’s something twisted with how he’s feeling, and he knows the only way to kick away these horrible feelings is to find out who she is. If he sees her, his attraction will abate, he knows it will. All he has to do is speak with her once and realize she’s not Mydei. Simple. Easy.

He only has eyes for Mydei. From the moment he laid eyes on the crown prince of Castrum Kremnos all those years ago, he’s known. It took a lot of time to work through his feelings, a boatload of denial even as he oogled the other alpha to the concern of literally everyone around him. He’s sure half of Okhema is aware of his crush, most of the heirs too.

Mydei said there was no one, but all of Okhema did not hallucinate that scent. He did not hallucinate that scent.

Even with Aglaea and Tribbie confirming that the rumors are false, that scent was very much real, tangible. He could taste it on his tongue as it burned his nose.

She exists out there. Mydei knows who she is but will not tell. He wonders what she did to upset him or if it was only a fling, nothing serious. His heart squeezes uncomfortably.

Never did he think he would find himself victim to his own instincts. Some scents land better than others. Omega scents tend towards saccharine sweet, not his favorite, yet…

Phainon groans and turns to his side. He throws off his covers and flips over his pillow.

Compatibility has never been a worry for him. His pheromones are softer than the traditional alpha, sweet like a floral spring breeze with fragrant petals afloat. Bright citrusy notes with lavender and vanilla. Apparently, he smells like the sun, though he’s not really sure what that means because a ball of light has no smell. The tattoo on his neck seems to agree, and he reaches out to absentmindedly rub at it.

If he were to desire an alpha, his pheromones wouldn’t clash, wouldn’t cause the other alpha to turn aggressive. Omegas desire dominant scents and his, regardless of its floral character, is dominant in its own right. There’s little wonder why Aglaea repeatedly tells him to control his pheromones.

When he's in rut, that's a whole other story that he doesn't wish to get into. Outside of not wanting anyone else but Mydei, there's a reason why he's never taken a rut partner.

Even with the air conditioning turned on to the highest setting, his room stays blistering hot. Wildly, he grabs at the mug on his nightstand and downs the water in one go. It parches the dryness in his throat, but does nothing to stop the incessant, burning itch.

His attraction to Mydei can’t stop his desire for her. He hates it. This shouldn’t be the case at all, and ignoring isn’t an option anymore. He will find her and under no circumstances will Mydei find out. As long as he can see the omega, speak with her, then all of this will resolve.

It has to.

ོ༘₊⁺☀︎₊⁺⋆.˚ Mydei lounges on his living room couch, an arm covering his eyes. Beside him is a chalice of pomegranate juice, untouched, filled to the brim, and taunting him to take a sip. He had poured himself another glass only to push it to the side with a sigh. The thought of drinking it makes his throat close, his mind wandering to Phainon’s disgruntled expression and obvious disgust. He almost wants to dump it in the sink.

It’s irrational to feel this way, but he’ll get over it. It might take a day or two, but he should be fine afterwards.

He can’t sleep. Not at all. Not with the incessant buzzing in his head and the heaviness in his limbs. Absent-mindedly, he runs his tongue over his bottom lip in an attempt to stop the constant tingling, Phainon’s lingering gift.

Given how many years he’s known the other, he should be used to his antics, wild and unrestrained as they are. But Phainon’s behavior today had been overly erratic in a manner that was outside his normal, variable as it was.

One moment, Phainon seemed fine. The day started fine. Their spar went great and ended well, but that was when Mydei noticed the beginning of the shift, but ignored it. They went about their business strolling through the city, content to be in each other’s company.

Only his scent began to waver, flipping back and forth. Unstable then stable then unstable once more. A sweet spring meadow lit ablaze into the burning char of desiccated wheat only to fizzle out and stabilize to relative calm only to return once more to a blaze of destruction.

Mydei couldn’t relax. He couldn’t even enjoy his juice without being hyper aware of the way Phainon’s scent continued to switch and shift, even as the other tried to act normal and unbothered.

It might be a curse. Before, he had been confident in his ability to read the other, but now he’s slammed in the face by the obvious. He doesn’t like it when Phainon is upset, because obviously, he cares for the other, but now…

He thought Phainon liked pomegranates. Never had the other given any hint or indication that he disliked the fruit. They’ve shared plenty of pomegranate honey cakes in the past, and he’s even seen Phainon ordering pomegranate smoothies at the local juicery many times.

It almost felt personal. Did a pomegranate fall off a tree and hit him upside the head or something? Is that why he’s holding a grudge?

And when faced with Phainon’s piercing blue eyes, he froze, his body ignoring his commands. All he could do was watch as Phainon leaned closer, as the scent of spring overwhelmed and clouded his senses.

It almost seemed like… Phainon wanted to kiss him?

No, that can’t be it. He’s seeing things that don’t exist.

These instincts won’t leave, rearing their ugly heads at the worst times possible. Where he was once able to challenge Phainon with no issue, there’s now a twisting in his chest and loud whisperings begging him to submit. He feels like he can’t breathe.

Each time Phainon closes in, touches him, the desire to bare his neck and offer himself on a silver platter burns hot. He’s walking a fine line, and he’s a fool to think he wouldn’t fall.

Fortunately, he’s held in his reactions well enough. At the very least, Phainon hasn’t noticed the change, hasn’t called him out for any changes in behavior.

Mydei sighs, frustrated.

This is idiotic. He shouldn’t be wasting his time like this.

Maybe it’s time to visit Hyacine once more. He grabs his teleslate and quickly texts her asking if she’s available for an impromptu visit. Might as well make use of his restlessness to get a prescription refill, and besides, he could use some fresh air.

Chapter End Notes

As usual, Hyacine greets him with twinkling turquoise eyes and a wide smile, cotton candy pigtails swaying as she bounces over to say her hellos. Only this time, she pauses in her step, her normally jovial expression wiped off her sweet features. She stands frozen, the cogs in her brain seemingly halted.

Mydei stares at her in wait.

“Uh...” Hyacine says, dumbfounded. Her gaze slowly trails down to the bruise on his neck.

The need to explain grows with each passing moment. “Phainon scented me recently. He also bit me by accident.”

Hyacine blinks. Little Ica squeaks softly in concern.

“Ah!” she exclaims, a little too loudly. Her lips curve into yet another wide smile, though this time, it shakes at the corners. “Yes, okay, well. That’s great! Are you two together?”

“Together?” Mydei frowns. “We do spend a lot of time with one another.”

He’s not daft. He knows what she means to say, but he’s not about to open that line of thought.

“Never mind,” Hyacine laughs with a wave of her hands. “Let me grab your prescription. Stay right here.” She bounces off to scour her cabinets.

Mydei watches as she rummages through all sorts of medications, concentration on her features as she hones in on the familiar blue and white bottles. Inevitably, his mind wanders off, following the path it knows best—Phainon. Seems like he’s all Mydei thinks about nowadays. It shouldn’t be the case but it is.

Luckily, Hyacine is quick, grabbing the medications and bouncing in front of him to hand them over. “Here you go! These are another month’s supply.”

“Thank you.”

“My pleasure!” she smiles, peppy as always. Little Ica squeaks excitedly beside her, flying around in a flurry of rainbow sparkles. Mydei reaches out to pet the little plump unicorn, smiling as it squeaks again and nuzzles against his hand.

“Hyacine, are there any medications to stop…” he trails off, unable to finish. Hyacine is his doctor and he trusts her, but admitting his unusual fixation towards Phainon is worse than pulling teeth. “Never mind.”

Hyacine tilts her head.

“What do I smell like?” Mydei asks instead. It’s been stuck on his mind for a while now. The rumors always repeated sweet and fertile, far too vague to make any sort of sense. Being told he smells fertile brings chills rolling down his spine.

“Huh?” Turquoise eyes widen.

“I don’t think it’s possible to scent myself,” Mydei says with a small frown. “The rumors never specified, and asking is out of the question.”

“Got it!” Hyacine nods. “I would say… “ She strokes her chin, a pensive look on her delicate features. “A blend of ripe pomegranates and honey.”

Her words register. Pomegranate.

Oh.

That… That explains everything. His heart squeezes, the breath punched out of his lungs. Phainon hates his natural scent. The dislike for the fruit didn’t appear out of nowhere. He’s the reason why.

“Keep in mind that’s how you smell in pre-heat. Your scent intensifies, becomes sweeter in an attempt to attract a mate. I haven’t had a chance to gauge your usual scent, but it’d probably still smell of pomegranate, only not nearly as strong.”

“I smell like pomegranate,” Mydei states back. His expression falls. “I see…”

“Is something the matter, Lord Mydei?” Hyacine asks. “Are you alright?”

“I’m fine,” he says.

This is idiotic. He shouldn’t care. It doesn’t matter if Phainon doesn’t like his scent. Everyone has their own preferences. It’s not Phainon’s fault he dislikes pomegranates.

Observant like always, Hyacine sees his discomfort, her eyebrows pinching. Mydei quickly stuffs his pill bottles into his pockets before he crushes them in his grip.

“Your scent is quite nice,” she reassures and reaches out to pat him gently on the shoulder.

He appreciates the gesture but it does nothing to abate the crawl of hurt brewing in his chest. Years of experience have allowed him to keep his expression level. “Thank you.”

Hyacine’s office is always lively, a far cry from the rundown tents he used to be patched up in. Cutesy rainbow decor covers the walls and her desk is filled with lots of small trinkets, plush dolls of pink cotton candy chimeras and crocheted flowers.

Even dealing with all the casualties and taking the brunt of responsibility as head physician of Okhema, she remains carefree, all brilliant smiles and twinkling eyes. He admires her resilience in the face of these trying times.

With a soft sigh, Hyacine scoots over to her desk and takes a seat. The next moments are silent in contemplation. Her hands clasp tightly together.

Finally, Hyacine says, “Lord Mydei.”

“Yes?”

She purses her lips. “My apologies if I’m assuming, but I have to say this as your physician. Please be careful about letting Lord Phainon scent you. It’s one thing to be around him and other alphas, but letting them scent you can mess with the efficacy of the medications. His scent on you is very strong, and it seems to me, he’s rubbed against your mating gland. For now, you’re stable with no signs of degradation, but I'm obligated to let you know the risks.”

Mydei braces himself for her next words. He knows what’s coming.

“Beneath the medications, you are still an omega.” Her expression softens. “I do not mean this in a derogatory way, Lord Mydei.”

You cannot hide from your instincts. The meaning is clear, even if she tries to let him down easy.

“I understand… I will be more careful.”

ོ༘₊⁺☀︎₊⁺⋆.˚

Mydei comes to the realization when he’s yet again traversing across the city to return home.

He passes through the fifth marble corridor of the night before he’s had enough. It’s nearing the fourth quint of curtain fall hour, and he wants nothing more than to go back to sleep and try to scrounge as much rest as he can before the day begins. Luckily he doesn’t have much planned so he can afford to relax a little and maybe work on some new chimera animations.

It pains him to admit, but realistically, if he’s spending this much time zipping back and forth, he might as well move closer. That way he wouldn’t have to deal with the treacherous walk and having to wake up in the middle of the night, scurrying around the city corridors and alleyways like some jumpy nocturnal creature, easily spooked by moving shadows and sudden noises.

There’s no word in the Kremnoan language for “I’m tired of having to spend an hour walking across the city for a doctor’s visit”, but he’s about to pen one and stick it in the dictionary.

He rounds the corner only to nearly crash into a warm body.

Who in their right mind is up during this hour? Though it’s not their fault, he almost wants to snarl at them for breaking the peace and quiet.

“Woah, watch out!” said person cries out. “Eh? M-Mydei?”

The familiar scent of spring fills his nose, stronger than usual, bright citrus roasting beneath the sun.

Phainon stands in front of him, dressed lightly in a soft white chiton that both reveals and accentuates his toned chest muscles. Mydei recalls buying it for him after witnessing the atrocity that was his favored bright yellow shirt and deep purple pants. Phainon had pouted and attempted in earnest to defend himself and his eyesore of a getup only to quietly acquiesce when Aglaea passed by and lightly frowned at him.

The black leather choker remains tightly strapped around his throat, digging into his pale skin and covering the etching of the brilliant sun. Crossing his arms against his chest with a little too much force, Mydei tears his gaze away and asks, “Why are you awake at this hour?”

The last person he wishes to see right now is Phainon, but luck isn’t on his side.

“I could say the same to you,” Phainon laughs only to sober up immediately, his expression listless as he says, “Couldn’t sleep… needed some fresh air.”

“Hmph.”

“You look good,” Phainon says. A pink tongue peaks out to lick over dry lips.

“And you look terrible,” Mydei lies.

“Thanks.” Phainon rubs at his eyes. “Nice to know…”

“Go back home, Deliverer,” Mydei says as he turns to leave. He doesn’t have time for this, not when the weight of the pills in his pockets reminds him of his inadequacies.

But Phainon catches his wrist, urgency in his voice, as he says, “Can I sleep with you?”

Caught off guard, Mydei jerks back. “...What?”

Phainon waves his arms around wildly, as if trying to distract. With a stilted laugh, he tries again, “Sorry, tired—Ah, I meant… Can I go home with you?”

“I have pomegranates on my kitchen counter,” Mydei says flatly. “Wouldn’t want you to be uncomfortable. I know how much I disgust you.” He can’t stop the venom that leaches into his voice nor the slipup. Fuck. He only hopes Phainon doesn’t notice.

Phainon expression darkens, lashes casting deep shadows over his eyes. His voice lowers, “Look, I’m sorry about earlier today. I don’t know what came over me. I’m normally not like this…”

“Yes, you are,” Mydei retorts. “Let go of my wrist.”

“Okay, not this bad though,” Phainon says, releasing his hold. In an instant, his tired expression warms and he stares at Mydei with wide, glimmering blue eyes and his bottom lip jutted out, trembling ever so slightly. “Please?” He inches closer. “Mydei… Please?”

He doesn’t have time for this. Already, he’s threatened by a headache, a faint pulse in his temples. Kephale’s dawn is too bright for this deep in the day. He almost wishes for the evernight.

Tell Phainon no. Tell him to go back home and leave him alone. He has no desire to be near the alpha. Not right now. Not when he knows Phainon can’t stand who he really is, hidden beneath the layers of medication.

But one look at those sparkling eyes has his resolve wavering, the stone walls he’s built crumbling beneath the heat of the burning sun.

“Fine,” Mydei bites out. “Only for tonight.”

The grin that Phainon gives is blinding. Mydei feels nothing but regret.

ོ༘₊⁺☀︎₊⁺⋆.˚

This isn’t the first time they’ve shared a bed, far from it. They’ve been through their fair share of missions that resulted in sleeping in a small, cramped tent or even sharing a dingy inn room with only one bed that was for sure not meant for two grown men.

Phainon tosses and turns in his sleep. He also likes to starfish and cling onto the nearest object, whether it be a pillow, a pile of blankets, or a person, hoarding all warmth for himself.

After all, Phainon’s appearance is striking, radiant. Moonlight hair artfully tousled and wide blue eyes framed by thick lashes. Trained body of a warrior, strong beyond mortal comprehension.

Mydei learned the hard way when Phainon easily hoisted him up with one arm, a wide grin on his face as Mydei scrambled to steady himself.

Phainon is Okhema’s proud jewel. Everyone loves him. A rare alpha that naturally commands attention when he walks into the room.

Mydei has always known that. He’s had to bear witness to the many people that have either confessed or attempted to confess to Phainon. And at the baths, with Phainon’s body out on display, it’s always a free for all for the bathgoers and workers on who can get his attention first. Thankfully, he’s fully clothed right now, so the attention is less, but still very much present.

Disgruntled, Mydei steps aside to lounge on a nearby kline . The omega didn’t seem too keen on speaking with him, only offered him a polite look before honing her attention on her target. It’s better to wait for them to finish.

It’s not a big deal. Many Okhemans still have their prejudices against Kremnoans. Though tensions are lesser nowadays, they’re still very much present. His reputation has shot down given the rumors, though he hasn’t heard much whisperings lately.

He rests his head against the pillow and closes his eyes, scrounging a moment's rest and blocking out all noise. Never has it bothered him this much until now. He almost wishes he had refused Phainon’s request to bathe together. They always request a private room, even in the public baths.

“Mydei!” Phainon jogs up to him, the clack of his leather boots against tile. “Don’t fall asleep on me again.”

He cracks open an eye to see Phainon looming over him, looking much like an excited puppy. If he had a tail, it’d be wagging. Though the omega is gone, he can smell her on him. He doesn’t like it. Something burns inside him. A desire to claim.

“She’s interested in you,” Mydei says, sitting up and watching as the woman gives Phainon one last wistful glance before hurrying off to do her worker duties.

Phainon tilts his head. “Who?”

“The omega you were speaking to,” Mydei says, pushing himself off the kline . He stretches out his back muscles before swinging his towel over his shoulders.

“Oh. She’s a friend. I met her a few weeks ago when you were on your mission. Had to come to the bathhouse alone.”

“Hmph.”

“Why?” Phainon presses. His voice grows tight, though his expression remains light. “Are you interested in her? You’ve been eyeing her. Found more prey to sink your fangs into?”

“Why would I be interested in her?” Mydei stares at Phainon with obvious disbelief. “She rubbed against you, and you let her.”

“Oh? Hm…” Phainon tilts his head, banging falling over his eyes. He pauses, in deep contemplation, before he’s leaning forwards, lips curving into a wide grin as he effortlessly invades Mydei’s personal space. His face is only millimeters away from Mydei’s. “Are you jealous?” he jests, blue eyes glinting.

“I’m not,” Mydei scoffs. He grabs Phainon’s wrist and pulls him towards the changing room. “Let’s go.”

“No way!” Phainon laughs. “Mydei, my dearest, you know I only have eyes for you.” He says it a bit too loud, unabashed in his tone. Almost as if he wants others to hear.

A few heads turn their way. Mydei even hears a gasp in the background and the clattering of a fruit plate onto the floor, plump grapes rolling away in all different directions.

“Stop talking,” Mydei hisses. Already, his ears begin to burn red, and Phainon, observant as always, notices right away. Blue eyes glimmer, crinkling at the edges, a wide smile decorating handsome features. Any wider, and it’s sure to fall off.

Phainon looks far too pleased. It makes Mydei turn away and focus on their destination. They make it through the doorway into the changing rooms. Without another word, Mydei starts pulling off his clothing and stuffing it into an open locker, ignoring Phainon whose gaze is burning a hole in his back. He wraps a towel around his hips as he shrugs off his pants.

“I like alphas, you know,” Phainon says, his hand moving to wrap around Mydei’s bare waist, stroking away at the tanned skin. “Can’t see myself with an omega. I thought you knew that.”

“I know now,” Mydei says, pulling himself away. The touch burns. Bitterness floods his mouth. “Shut up and take your clothes off. ”

“Not going to buy me dinner first?” Phainon pouts as he pulls off his high-collared compression shirt, sculpted muscles flexing. His pectorals are firm, pure muscle, complete with carved washboard abs. No matter how often he’s seen Phainon shirtless, he still can’t get used to the sight.

He sounds a little like a teenage girl. Castorice would be delighted if she could hear his internal dialogue.

“What’s that on your neck?” Mydei asks, staring at what looks to be a square piece of gauze covering Phainon’s nape. He even has matching ones on both his wrists. “Have you been injured?”

Phainon slaps his hand over the patch on his nape and raises an eyebrow. He searches Mydei’s expression for any signs of a joke. “It’s a scent patch.”

Oh . A scent patch. That makes infinitely more sense. He’s heard of those. Many Okhemans run around with gauze on their necks and wrists, and it always struck him as odd.

Okhemans treat secondary gender differently it seems. Kremnoans parade their scents around, wearing it as a badge of honor. Scent patches don’t exist where he’s from because it’s seen as a disgrace to hide one’s scent, almost on par with refusing to battle.

Closing the mahogany doors, they slide into the warm water. Their own private bath, away from the loud crowds and curious eyes. Steam blankets the room, giving it a hazy, euphoric feeling. With a soft groan, Mydei melts into the water, eyes fluttering shut. Phainon lounges beside him.

Now that the patch is gone, Phainon’s familiar scent begins to fill the space, overpowering the soft scents of chamomile and sandalwood from the scented bath oils. The hairs on Mydei’s neck stick up, and he breathes deeply. He’s missed the scent more than he’d like to admit, but it’s tinged with the omega from earlier. Their scents mesh together, and he’s unable to tell where Phainon starts and where she ends.

Mydei bites his lip. He can’t relax, not like this. His eyes snap open, and he crawls onto Phainon’s lap, burying his face into the crook of Phainon’s neck. He breathes in the familiar citrus scent while rubbing his cheek against the bare skin, desperately trying to get rid of the other scent that sticks onto the alpha. His bare ass rubs against the wet towel tied tightly around Phainon’s waist.

Maybe he should drag Phainon underwater to wash away her scent. He won’t be too happy about it, but Mydei will take his chances.

He pauses, breath fanning over pale skin.

No. Probably not worth it.

“Mydei…” Phainon shifts beneath him. His voice comes out rough, almost ragged, “What do you think you’re doing?”

He pulls away and presses a finger to Phainon’s lips. “Shush.”

If only he could scent Phainon too… then he could get rid of her scent on his body. He tries again and again, but he has no scent. The haziness of the steamy room mixes with the haziness of his mind. He nearly cries out in frustration.

It’s good that Phainon can’t smell him. He’s sure the alpha would pull away and not allow any of this had Mydei outed himself as an omega. Some alphas and omegas aren’t compatible. While he likes Phainon’s scent, Phainon doesn’t like his.

“What’s going on with you?” Phainon murmurs as wraps his arms around Mydei’s waist to stabilize him. Fingers thread into his hair as Mydei clings onto Phainon’s broad shoulders.

A soft knock on the door. An attendant slides in to bring new towels and refresh the soaps and fragrant oils. It’s the same girl as before. Of course it is. Seasoned bathhouse workers know better than to go into their private room unannounced.

Phainon’s back is turned to her. Mydei runs his hands up his spine, eliciting a shiver from the alpha while he gives the omega the darkest glare he can muster. A warning to leave. A warning that she’s not welcome here, that Phainon isn’t hers for the taking.

The message is clear.

She squeaks out an apology, dropping the towels and bottles on the bench before bowing and making her way out.

Okay. If that’s how Mydei wants to play, then Phainon has no choice other than retreat and lick his wounds. It’s a strange turn of events, especially since Mydei was the one who initiated that entire public scenting ordeal. Can’t really fault him for being a little confused. It definitely puts a wrench in his plans.

He won’t confess. Not yet. Not until he gets a clearer picture of what’s going on.

Regardless of the itch in his throat and the pressure in his chest, he carries on. Smiles and laughs. Acts as if he’s okay. Mydei is cautious of him now, and he doesn’t know how to close that distance.

Phainon peels off the scent patches on his nape and wrists and tosses them into the trash. He sighs, frustrated, as he rubs slow circles in the inflamed area on his neck. The corners of the patch had dug incessantly into his skin, leaving it red and irritated. He doesn’t miss this feeling. Rather, he wishes he didn’t have to deal with this at all.

With a scornful smile, he yanks open the cabinet where he usually stores his scent patches, expecting to find his stash. Only there’s nothing in there. It’s empty.

“What? I thought I had more…” Phainon mutters to himself, confused.

He checks his closet. Nothing. His bathroom. Nothing. Maybe he left some in his living room? Also nothing. He swore he had more, but it’s also been years since he’s had to use them. Is his memory growing hazy?

Once again, he checks the cabinet. Opens it then slams it close only to open it once more as if the patches would magically appear if he repeated it enough times.

Phainon groans as he stares into his trash, eyeing the wrinkled remnants of the last three patches he had so haphazardly thrown away. Should he fish them out and reuse them? Objectively it’s gross and he rather not, but he’s sort of in a pinch.

Damn it. If he wants more that means he has to visit Hyacine.

It’s times like these where he realizes how little it takes to push the needle. Years he spent stable and in control only to fall back to old patterns, unable to regulate his scent even with Aglaea’s teachings branded into him. None of her lessons work as they used to.

Frustrated, Phainon flops onto his bed, wincing at the sting where his chafed skin hits the rumpled mattress. He turns to his side and stares blankly at himself in the mirror.

He hates wearing those accursed patches. The amount of upkeep and the constant paranoia of them falling off makes them a less than stellar option at keeping pheromones at bay. Not to mention, he also has to pair them with thick, scent-neutralizing lotions that suffocate his pores. There’s no other choice. Not when his body rejects the medications meant for this very purpose.

Since the end of his rut, he hasn’t been able to properly control his pheromones. It’s as if he had been transported to when he first arrived in Okhema, back when he was in a constant state of wild, unmanageable pre-rut.

He remembers those days. Whispers everywhere he went. A bad omen foretold. The Chrysos Heir who arrived in Okhema smelling of decay and destruction. The young alpha, the sole survivor of the black masked spectre that destroyed a small farming village. He had been young then, barely a child past fifteen.

Phainon pulls out his teleslate to check the time. It’s the third quint of parting hour—not too late in the day. He could go for a quick run to the nearby store and purchase some over the counter. It’d save him a trip to Hyacine’s, but then he remembers how terrible those cheap ones are and how little they work for someone like him.

On second note, it’s probably not worth it. The ones Hyacine gives him are reinforced, made to subdue even the strongest of pheromones. The ones sold at the store barely function, not meant for Chrysos Heirs who have different inner workings due to golden blood.

Instead, he decides to take a quick shower to scrub off the remnants of lotion coating his scent glands. Dressed in only a pair of boxers, he sits at the edge of his bed while he towels his moonlight hair dry. He debates his options, few as they are.

Maybe he can try meditation—a simple yet effective tactic that has helped him much in the past. He closes his eyes and tries to focus, hone in on his senses. Aglaea taught him to clear his mind and release the tension coiled deep inside.

Only the moment he closes his eyes, he’s met with memories of sweet pomegranate and honey. The beginnings of nausea pull at the pit of his stomach. He wants to hurl. That omegan scent haunts him. He can’t escape it. Even his attraction to Mydei can’t lessen the desire he has for that omega. It’s insane to be thinking of another when his heart has always been for Mydei.

Even if Mydei doesn’t return his feelings, Phainon will continue to hold on. No matter how much it hurts.

There is no way he will ever be with an omega. Even if he did like her— he doesn’t —and she liked him back, he can’t be with her. A damaged alpha like him can’t be with an omega.

He’s the captain steering a sinking ship. There’s nowhere to go but down.
