As Phainon steps up the winding steps into the lush greenery surrounding Hyacine’s clinic, he can’t help but feel a strange sense of deja vu. In front of him is the familiar sight of large, yellow sunflowers that border the periphery of the clinic. Spiralling green vines wrap around the aged stone walls, contrasting with the cutesy handwritten sign that reads ‘Hyacine’s Office Here!! ♡’.

He rarely visits Hyacine. The last time he came here, he had been forcefully dragged over by an angry Mydei who demanded he get that purpling bruise on his ribs checked out. Sure, it hurt when he breathed and maybe he couldn’t walk as upright as he used to, but it was no big deal. It would heal with enough time, and he could still fight even if it hurt to hold his greatsword. There was no reason to waste Hyacine’s precious time or resources.

She’s already dealt with him in the past, spending hours upon hours, sacrificing precious sleep and resources, in an attempt to help him adjust to Okhema. He rather not revisit that era of his life.

Her space is as he remembers. Cozy and warm. Very much lived in, covered in pastel colors, cutesy designs, and many soft plushies. Little Ica hangs out on a waiting chair in the corner of the room, chomping away at a tower of bright red apples.

“Lord Phainon!” Hyacine exclaims, spinning around in her plush pink office chair to face him, her fluffy pigtails bouncing. If her wide eyes are any indication, she’s caught off guard by his sudden and unannounced appearance. “What brings you here?”

“Hey, Hyacine,” Phainon greets, giving her his signature wide grin. “My apologies for coming up unannounced.”

“No worries!” Hyacine places her pen down. She had been in the middle of penning prescriptions, a deep look of concentration on her sweet features before he so rudely broke her out of her trance. He feels bad for wasting her time like this. She has better things to deal with than him, but he’s desperate. Without those patches, he can’t leave the confines of his room without terrorizing the public with what he can no longer control.

“Do you have more of those reinforced scent patches?” he casually asks her. Or tries. He can’t help the slight pause of his words or the small hitch of his breath. His heart thunders in his chest, bracing for the next question to leave his lips. “Also… uhm, can I get some suppressants and scent blockers?”

Hyacine pauses as she takes in his request. Hesitant, she asks, “You’re using the patches again?”

“For now,” Phainon responds, rubbing at his naked nape. His fingers come back gross and oily from the plethora of lotion he had slapped on earlier. “I sort of ran out.”

In an instant, she’s off her chair and beside him. Turquoise eyes scan his face, and she carefully sniffs the air before placing a gentle hand on his nape. Her expression pinches as she murmurs, “Your scent is stronger than usual, even with the scent neutralization. It seems unstable too…” She looks up at him with abject concern, causing a chill to run down Phainon’s spine. “Oh, dear. What caused this?”

“My rut came earlier than I expected,” Phainon tells her. “Last week. A month early.”

For years, his ruts have been normal. Once every three months on the dot. He can predict the beginning of his pre-rut with striking accuracy. Never has he reacted so strongly to the scent of another to thrust him into an early cycle. It’s concerning to be thrown back to how he used to be—a reminder of the truth he’s run from for so long. The illusion has shattered, and he’s left to pick up the remnants.

Hyacine’s expression flickers. She opens her mouth to say something only to pause in her step. Phainon has known her for years, practically since the day he entered the city, and has spent much of his time with her when they were students at the Grove. It’s obvious she knows more than she lets on. Cheerful and enthusiastic as she is, she’s also easy to read when troubled, even if she tries to hide it behind a veil of sweet smiles.

As lead physician, half of her job is keeping positive even when the situation seems a downward spiral. He wishes he had her tenacity.

“Do you know why your rut arrived earlier?” Hyacine settles on asking. “Any reason you can think of? Maybe a scent that caused it? Or an emotional reaction?” In an instant, her somber expression brightens. She stares at him with wide expectant eyes, lips curved up into a knowing smile. It’s like she’s seeing through him, waiting for a specific response.

Little Ica zooms over, also watching with waiting eyes.

Pomegranate. Honey. Omega.

Quickly, Phainon responds, “No, none I can think of.” He wipes those estranged thoughts out of his mind. “Maybe it’s the heat. It’s been hotter recently…”

It may be his imagination but he thinks he sees Little Ica roll its eyes. Hyacine sighs, shaking her head as she plants her palm against her forehead. All things considered, he’s a little offended.

“Has Lord Mydei spoken to you about anything recently?” Hyacine prods. “How has your relationship been with him?”

“Eh? Mydei? We’ve been doing good…” A tight smile pulling at the corners of his lip. Or at least, they were. He’s not sure what to think nowadays, not with how weird Mydei has been acting. It’s hard to tell what Mydei thinks of him, if he’s being honest.

Mydei never tells him no. If he has an idea, no matter how preposterous, Mydei always supports him, even if he does have some scathing words to say. But now, Mydei is refusing him, keeping away as if he’s afraid. Only that can’t be it because Mydei does not know fear. There’s no word for it in the Kremnoan dictionary, he’s been told many times.

“Did he mention anything new?” Hyacine asks as she grabs a pack of scent patches from one of her many stocked shelves.

Little Ica makes a loud trilling noise, and Hyacine gestures for the little pegasus to shush.

“Uh, I remember he did tell me that he uses suppressants and scent blockers. I’m surprised there’s no reaction yet, but he is more responsible than I am...”

Hyacine tilts her head, and so does Little Ica.

“I mean all of Okhema pretty much knew,” Phainon laughs. “An alpha without a scent is the biggest giveaway. He’s not Aglaea.”

Hyacine laughs, a pinch nervous, while Little Ica gives up and flies back to its original resting spot to take a nap. Seems like the poor pegasus has had enough.

With a shake of her head, Hyacine lowers her voice and says, “Lord Phainon, this is serious. If you can recall any recent changes or any reasons for this sudden early rut then it will be very helpful. I say this as your physician and as your friend. I worry about you and my goal is to help you. This hasn’t happened in years…”

Phainon brushes his bangs away from his eyes. Hyacine is aware of his preference for alphas, and his rather embarrassing crush on Mydei. But there’s little use in hiding what needs to be said.

“I think an omega triggered it. You must have heard the rumors a few weeks back,” Phainon, somehow, manages to say. His heart twists. It’s a betrayal of his rational mind against the irrational.

“The rumors regarding Lord Mydeimos?”

Phainon nods. “The omega that Mydei had been with. Her scent is what triggered this early reaction.”

He expects her to react with shock. After all, she knows his history, his refusal to be with an omega. He’s half right. Her eyes do widen, but what he doesn’t expect is for her to look like she’s been vindicated.

“...” The corners of Hyacine’s lips tremble. She tries to remain straight-faced as she shoves the pack of scent patches into Phainon’s hands and turns her head away.

“Hyacine? You okay?”

Hyacine glances back at him and immediately falls into a fit of giggles. She covers her mouth with her hands, but the giggles don’t abate. If anything, they grow stronger, louder. Turquoise eyes become hazy with tears as she tries and fails to calm herself down.

“Sorry—” she gasps out. “Sorry… Lord Phainon—Forgive me…” She clutches her stomach, trembling as a loud snort falls from her lips. Even Little Ica jumps at the noise.

Awkwardly, Phainon stands there, holding onto his pack of scent patches. Should he join in? Maybe he should laugh too. The situation would be quite funny if it weren’t so horrifying.

“Perhaps, you should speak with Lord Mydei about your affliction,” Hyacine says in between fits of laughter. She wipes at the edge of her eyes. “It would do you both some good to communicate… Also, stop scenting him. For both your sakes.”

“How do you know about that?”

“Lord Phainon, the question you should be asking is who doesn’t know?”

“...” Ah, he supposes that makes sense. It’s not like he was trying to hide it. Half of the thrill was in the potential of getting caught.

“Tell Lord Mydeimos your rut was triggered by the omega that smells like pomegranate and honey,” Hyacine continues. She slams her hands onto her desk. “Please…” Another giggle. “It’s for your own good that he knows…”

Phainon tries a smile, though it doesn’t quite reach his eyes. Thankfully, Hyacine doesn’t seem to notice, given how she’s busy trying to calm herself down.

Yeah, okay, so he’s going to go up to Mydei, who pointedly told him he didn’t wish to speak about the rumors, and tell him that his early rut was caused by the faceless omega who smells like a particular fruit that Phainon had so gracefully ranted on about. It’s like he’s asking to be punched.

“Can I try the medications again?” Phainon brings up once more. Hyacine easily gave him the patches, but ignored his request for the meds. He understands why, but he wants to try them again. It’s been years. Maybe they’ll work this time.

The effect is immediate. Her laughter falls away and her expression sobers until almost forlorn. “I don’t think it’s worth it, Lord Phainon.”

“ Please .” He needs to try. If he can’t get his pheromones under wraps, then he’s as good as screwed. The medications are his best bet. He doesn’t know how long he can last if he’s forced to stick with the patches and lotions.

Even if his body rejects the medications, even if he has to spend days in pain recuperating, he will try. Because, at the end of the day, he has his duties, and he can’t let Okhema down. He can’t afford weakness because Mydei won’t view him as worthy anymore, and he can’t have Aglaea disappointed in him either.

Hyacine eyes him, alarmed. Phainon scrambles to say, “Sorry! I can’t control it… Let me slap on a patch real quick.” He practically shreds the packaging in his haste, leaving bits and pieces of plastic on the floor. “I’ll pick that up in a second…”

Conflicted, Hyacine stands there quietly, watching as Phainon slaps the patches all over his body. She’s at war with herself, and Phainon feels a little guilty for putting her in this tough situation. In the end, she acquiesces and silently hands him two trial bottles, each containing a week worth of pills. “Try them, but promise me, you will speak to Lord Mydei before taking them.”

“I will,” Phainon says. He can breathe again, the weight lifted off his chest. “Thank you.”

Silence blankets the room. Phainon stares down at the bottles in his hands, turning them over as he reads the fine print and the giant list of potential side effects. Alpha suppressants and alpha scent blockers—a different formulation than the normal ones sold to normal Okheman citizens. These are modified with Chrysos Heirs in mind and thus have a higher chance of adverse reactions.

Hyacine steps back to her desk and begins scribbling notes down on a piece of paper. He’s almost tempted to look over to see what she’s writing, but he decides to take a seat next to Little Ica instead. The rotund pegasus stares at him then shakes its head, almost like it’s trying to scold Phainon for his antics.

Okay. Now, he feels a little self-conscious.

“How are the villagers?” Phainon asks, changing the subject. “The ones Mydei brought back.”

Hyacine blinks. “Oh! They’re doing great! Settling in just fine. Minor injuries, if any at all.”

“It’s a real tragedy what happened to their home,” Phainon continues.

Aedes Elysiae never stood a chance. For these villagers to come out relatively unharmed is a miracle. His friends and family weren’t so lucky.

Patience is a virtue. Hyacine is practically a saint with how she treats him. With a soft hum, she tells him, “They’re doing well and have been moved to the customary temporary apartment complexes. Aglaea is still sorting out the housing situation.”

It’s as he expects. Good. He can start there. Talking to Mydei is the last resort, even if Hyacine thinks otherwise.

He thanks her for spending precious time on him to which she gives him some kindly but cryptic advice about following his feelings and the importance of honesty in a relationship. There’s little reason to think about it too hard, so he doesn’t and only says his farewells before stepping outside.

Distracted and in a haste to leave, he nearly crashes into Castorice who jumps back on instinct. The pill bottles and scent patches fly out of his hands, clattering onto the floor.

Clutching tightly onto her pastel purple tote bag, Castorice bows. “Lord Phainon, my apologies.”

“No worries,” Phainon responds as he bends down to pick up the fallen medications.

Purple eyes shift back and forth. Castorice wrings her hands. “I did not mean to intrude. It was not my intention.”

“Don’t worry about it,” Phainon reassures her with his signature blinding smile. “Hyacine’s in her office right now if you want to see her. Are you here for an appointment?”

Castorice shakes her head. “I simply wished to send my regards to her. She has been working hard and—” She reaches into her bag and pulls out a crocheted plushie, plump, in the shape of a unicorn. “I wanted to give her a gift. It’s not that great because I’m still practicing but…”

“Hyacine will love it!” Phainon reassures, grinning. It doesn’t quite reach his eyes. “The plush looks great! You should give it to her.”

It’ll fit right in with the other colorful plushes Hyacine has. Now, he wonders if Castorice made most of them herself. It looks to be in her style.

Gesturing to the pill bottles in his hands, Castorice asks, “Hyacine gave you those?”

“Maybe they’ll work this time,” Phainon says with a shrug.

“You and I both know your body does not like those.”

In response, Phainon gives a tight smile.

Castorice knows him better than most. She’s witnessed him at his very worst and has never once judged him for it. Likewise, he knows her troubles too. If she had told him that she started taking medications again, he would have flipped out on her, worried for her health and potential adverse reaction to the seemingly innocuous white pills.

Back then he had taken suppressants and scent blockers by the bucketful. Anything to calm the burn inside him, the hatred that had taken route, the physical manifestation of the despair of watching his friends and family reduced to ashes right before his eyes. Only those pills inevitably failed and the backlash had been terrible.

Hyacine is a miracle worker, but even she can’t help him. The medications are risky, prone to failure, but when they work, they work incredibly well. The alternatives do nothing to fight the fire inside him.

“Lord Phainon,” Castorice says, worry tinged in her soft voice. She remains her careful distance away, though she looks as if she wants to reach out and grab him by the shoulder.

“I know my limits,” Phainon responds. “Don’t worry about me.”

As long as he kept his emotions in check, his scent remained pleasant, fragrant like a flourishing spring meadow. An inviting scent he’s been told by many. The years gone by, the days of the old withered away by the tides of time, most of Okhema has no clue of how he used to be.

And of course, Mydei doesn’t know. By the time the Kremnoan detachment arrived, Phainon had perfected his control, his sunny persona. He never planned on deviating from it. If Mydei knew how he was before, pitifully weak and emotional, then he would have never been regarded as equal.

Only now, he’s slipping once more, falling back to old habits. It’s only a matter of time before he devolves into how he was when he first arrived in Okhema. Mydei has already grown suspicious, and even Aglaea can’t help him if this is to continue.

“Why are you looking for the villagers?” Castorice asks, breaking Phainon out of his prison of thoughts.

“I wish to witness their safety and send my regards.” It’s half-true, after all. He knows what it’s like to be thrown into a new place and expected to mesh in with the greater population while struggling to retain the identity of home.

The answer doesn’t sit well with Castorice. Had it been anyone else, they would have believed him. She takes a deep breath and says, “ Lord Phainon . I understand your sentiments, but you are going behind Lord Mydei’s back.”

An orange butterfly buzzes by, landing softly on a nearby sunflower. The carved stone fountain trickles a steady stream of crystalline water. It’s a nice, beautiful day, all things considered, even if Phainon feels like his world is crumbling beneath his feet.

A touch bitter, Phainon replies, “How am I going behind Mydei’s back? I simply wish to speak with the villagers that have been rescued and are now expected to live in Okhema as if their home hadn’t been destroyed.”

Castorice blinks. Her expression flickers between understanding and exasperation, and her mellow, floral scent begins to wilt.

“Sorry,” Phainon quickly says, raising his arms up in surrender. His expression falls, moonlight bangs covering his eyes.  “I didn’t mean to.”

“Lord Phainon, I understand what you’re attempting to do. You will not find it,” she says, resolute. “Speak with Lord Mydei first, I beg of you.”

Hyacine told him that too. That makes the two of them.

Maybe he should, but Mydei made it very clear he doesn’t want to talk about any topic related to the rumors. He only hopes Castorice won’t tell him. She’s not that type of person, so he should be safe in that regard, but still, he can’t help but feel uneasy.

ོ༘₊⁺☀︎₊⁺⋆.˚ The temporary housing complexes are as he remembers—rows of towering white buildings all cut exactly the same. Each complex is stamped with a number, meant to accommodate hundreds of people at a time while Aglaea sorts through finding permanent housing. Situated in the back end of Okhema, there’s not much to do in this area outside of a small park and a rocky hiking trail up to the baths.

Phainon had never been housed here. When he first arrived in Okhema, he had been hidden away from the general public and taken to live under Aglaea’s strict supervision. After all, what good was there in placing a singular teenager in a complex meant to house tens if not hundreds of survivors.

In the weeks following Aedes Elysiae’s destruction, he had wandered aimlessly, cutting down all manner of monsters. Stuck in a trance, he had been consumed by a state of frenzied rut and his body moved on autopilot as he slashed and screamed and fought with all the energy he had left. Aglaea found him in that disheveled, beastly state and brought him to Okhema.

His first few weeks had been under strict lockdown. He remembers his first moments in the eternal holy city, witnessing the giant city-state in all its dawn blessed glory. He had been overwhelmed by the grand marble buildings, the luxurious temples, and cityfolk who held themselves much differently than the humble villagers he grew up with. Emotions still a harrowing mess, he didn’t react so well. Uncontrolled pheromones flourished and flooded the surroundings, an oppressive cloud of destruction, hatred, and decay. He had to be sequestered away before he made too much of a scene.

That’s how it was back then—his first few months of living in Okhema, thrust into a new world and still reeling from his loss of, well, everything . He had no ability to regulate his emotions, not when his every waking and sleeping moment had been consumed by visions of the masked spectre and the blood that dyed his hands red. Adrenaline flooded his system with no signs of reprieve.

In his presence, alphas would grow aggressive, but it was manageable. Betas didn’t like his burning scent, but it was more of a nuisance than anything else. With omegas… it was an entirely different story. They were terrified of him, of the oppressive atmosphere that followed him and smothered them in a haze of burning despair and falling ash. Even Castorice reacted negatively to his presence.

There was little he could do to ease the rampage of his mind. He can’t fault anyone for reacting to him, but it was a lesson learned that he will never forget. Omegas can’t handle him, and it’s best to stay a good distance away. He doesn’t want anyone to fear him, to be afraid of him for something he has no control over. It’s safer this way.

Phainon smiles at the guards, and he’s let into the complex without much hassle. Wherever he goes in Okhema, people recognize him and never question his motives. His reputation speaks for itself. After all, he’s rescued and brought over his fair share of people.

It doesn’t take long to find the village chief, a striking older alpha dressed in ornate, layered robes, who scurries out to greet him. They exchange pleasantries, and Phainon sends his regards. Delighted, the village chief invites him for a cup of specially brewed tea, a village specialty, fragrantly flavored with orange peel and cloves.

It’s here that Phainon finds what he’s looking for. The village chief reveals to him the most pertinent of information, the identity behind the scent that permeated Mydei’s body and lay the basis for the rumors. Bitterness settles in his throat as the chief speaks.

“I promised my daughter to Lord Mydeimos. She has left my side, and I have not seen her since the day we entered Okhema’s gates.”

Confused, Phainon sets his teacup down with a loud clink.

… What?

There’s no way he’s heard correctly.

“Excuse me, to reiterate, you sent your daughter to marry Mydei?”

“Indeed, I have.” The chief strokes his beard in contemplation. His deep brown eyes crinkle with pride. “Lord Mydeimos of Castrum Kremnos is a worthy alpha, and my daughter is an unmated omega of age. As a show of thanks, I offered him her hand. He will protect her well, and she will provide him with bountiful pups.”

Eh? The cogs in his brain spin to a halt. Okay, he’s known that Mydei has had relations with a faceless omega, but for him to agree to marry her?! What in the Kephale is going on?!

No. He’s jumping to conclusions. He needs to calm down.

“Lord Phainon?” the village chief questions. “I hope I did not offend.”

Phainon scrambles for a response. “You did not! I was only in thought. Of course, it is without a doubt true that Mydei is a great warrior and protector of Okhema.” A stilted laugh falls from his lips. “And… uh, Mydei accepted?”

The chief takes a deep sip of his spiced tea. “Indeed he did and laid out some terms of agreement. She is to be housed with the Kremnoans, and I will not be able to visit her or ask about her. It is a worthy sacrifice to secure her future. I have no qualms.” He seems very unbothered for someone that practically sold his daughter off, and it rubs Phainon the wrong way.

Incredulous, he asks, “And you accepted?” Probably not the best thing to say, but it slips out before he can control himself.

Already, he’s heating up, the familiar curl of anger brewing in his stomach. It’s unsightly and immature, but the flames are fanned by his desire to have Mydei as his and only his. The idea of Mydei with someone else doesn’t sit well with him no matter how much he tries to convince himself otherwise.

“Yes,” the chief hums. “My daughter must fulfill her omegan duties as childbearer. It is an honor for her to serve the crown prince.”

This is getting to be too much. Caged in like this, the beige walls of the communal kitchen caving in on him, he can hardly breathe. It feels like he’s been kicked in the crotch and slapped in the face at the same time. And then ran over repeatedly.

He almost wants to ask the chief if his daughter smells of pomegranates and honey when she’s in pre-heat, but he stops himself short. Regardless of Kremnoan mating customs, it’s an invasion of privacy to reveal that he, and the rest of Okhema, has smelled his daughter in such a vulnerable state.

The rest of the conversation happens in a blur. He keeps the confident, lax smile plastered onto his face, regardless of the twitching of his facial muscles, and continues running through pleasantries until it's time to say his farewells. He’s barely touched his tea and decides to down it in one go. The cloying spice helps distract him from the ache in his chest, if only for a little while.

Truly, if this is the case, then Mydei’s been lying to him this entire time. Phainon previously believed he knew Mydei, knew his beliefs, his thoughts, everything. Only now he realizes that he doesn’t because never would he have thought that Mydei would agree to such a ludicrous request. Perhaps he needs to argue with the other alpha over the prospects of opening his worldview and forgoing old tradition. Potentially over a spar. Two birds, one stone.

The day continues on. Phainon feels the energy drained out of him. He’s tired. So very tired.

When he steps once more into Kephale’s dawn, he can finally breathe again. The light spring breeze feels good against his feverish skin as he airs out his stuffy collar. He takes the familiar path home only to find Aglaea waiting beneath the shade of an olive tree, her arms crossed against her chest.

Cloaked head to toe in the purest of gold, Aglaea is blinding to look at head on. Her appearance is striking and has Phainon’s heart skipping a beat. Damn it. He’s been caught.

Before he can get even a word in, Aglaea says, “I heard the commotion. Walk with me to the baths.” She turns and heads off.

Phainon scurries after her, feeling much like a child about to be scolded by his mother. Aglaea calmly strides forward, and Phainon matches her step, nervousness creeping in with each foot forward. They pass through snaking marble corridors, silent save for the clacking of their boots against stone.

The pills rattle in his pockets. His skin chafes against the patch on his nape as it rubs against his tender skin. He had been under the false illusion that this day couldn’t possibly get worse only to be slammed in the head with Mydei agreeing to marry someone who isn’t him.

Phainon deflates.

Who is he kidding… Mydei practically rejected him outright a few days ago.

Together, he and Aglaea enter Marmoreal Palace, amidst the tall domed ceiling, the rushing water of the baths, and the lax gossip of the bathgoers. The change is immediate. All eyes are on the two of them. Aglaea pays them no mind, but chills creep down Phainon’s spine at the unwanted attention.

Once they reach the safety of the Hero’s Bath, Aglaea says, “Phainon, I have already told you the rumors about Mydei are false. For what reason did you want to visit the villagers?”

“I wished to send my regards. And see for myself how the villagers are faring.” An easy, practiced response.

Crystalline eyes regard him. Phainon gulps.

Lying to Aglaea is never a good idea, yet he still tries—and fails—to bend the truth. It’s a terrible habit he needs to break especially because Aglaea knows everything. Her golden threads reach every crevice of Okhema, covering the city in an invisible net of gold.

“I did not hallucinate that omegan scent,” Phainon says, taking a deep breath to calm his nerves. “Even if it’s false, I want to meet the chief’s daughter. To confirm for myself.”

Patient as always, Aglaea effortlessly answers, “She is not the omega in the rumors.” Her heels clack against the marble steps as her gaze trails the stream of shimmering golden water. She turns back to Phainon and softly says, “You don’t believe me.”

“The chief told me he promised her to Mydei and that he agreed to marry her.”

“That is what he told you?” Aglaea asks.

“Yes.” He didn’t hear wrong. Oh how he wishes he did, but the man’s deep, gravelly voice plays on loop. The shimmery water beckons him to jump in, if only to quiet the incessant buzzing in his head.

“From your conversation with the chief, how do you feel about him?”

Phainon’s brows furrow in thought. “Erm… Uh, he’s a traditional man who reflects the values of his village?”

“And what do you know about Mydei?” she asks gently.

“That he, erm, also agrees with those traditional values?” A pause. “No… that’s not right… Uh…”

Aglaea shakes her head. “Let me tell you the truth of the situation. Mydei agreed with the chief as a way to safely send her over to me. She is not living with the Kremnoans and has no further relations with him. Instead of attempting to dig for information behind his back, I implore you to speak with Mydei yourself and have an honest conversation.”

Ouch. That hurts a little. Phainon laughs it off.

It’s a little strange seeing how Hyacine and Castorice both told him to speak with Mydei. Now add Aglaea into the equation. Are they conspiring together?

Okay, so now he’s expected to reveal that he went into rut because of the omega who may or may not be the chief’s daughter and that he went behind Mydei’s back to ask about said omega when he promised to not bring up the topic anymore. Great. How is he even supposed to start that conversation without it derailing completely? He only hopes Mydei doesn’t hate him afterwards.

“I’ll speak to Mydei.” His expression falls, blue eyes downcast. “But I don’t know if he’s open to responding to my questions. He’s been hiding from me…”

It hurts to think that he doesn’t know Mydei as well as he thought he did. These years of camaraderie, have they shown Mydei nothing? That even now, he still can’t be fully trusted? His fists clench at his sides. It’s pathetic really. To think he’s holding onto these feelings, allowing them to consume him.

“Do you like him for him or because he’s an alpha?” Aglaea questions.

Though his heart clenches, his answer is immediate. “I like him because he’s Mydei.”

Aglaea’s lips curl into a soft smile, pleased by his response. For a moment, he’s in shock. He hasn’t seen that type of expression on her face in awhile, not with the heavy burden of the flamechase and her faltering humanity. Her next words come out gentle, reassuring. “Very good. Keep that in mind when you speak with him. Also, don’t take those medications. Hyacine may have given them to you, but they will only hamper you. Speak with Mydei, and all will be clear.”

Phainon sighs. “Alright, I’ll try. If that’s what it comes down to…”

ོ༘₊⁺☀︎₊⁺⋆.˚

The jealousy continues to burn. He tries to push it down. When that doesn’t work, he tries to ignore it by thinking of literally anything else. It’s like putting out a fire with gasoline.

He can barely control his pheromones as is. Any more of this, and he’s probably going to have to hole himself in his house for the rest of time.

Speak with Mydei they all say. What is he supposed to speak to Mydei about? That he agreed to marry an omega and didn’t tell him? If he brings it up, then he’ll have to admit that he went behind Mydei’s back to ask. Oh, boy. That’s not the conversation he wants to have, not when he’s terribly unsure of how Mydei feels about him.

But he has to. He only needs to find the right time for it.

He stalks his way through the city on his path back home, taking the familiar path that cuts through the middle of the city. It’s probably not the best idea, but he wants to return as soon as he can.

The cityfolk pause to stare at him. He’s not leaking any pheromones, or at least he shouldn’t be, but the stomp of his boots and his flat expression isn’t helping him blend into the background.

“Hey, rascal,” Cipher calls out, casually leaning against the stone railing. Her sharp gaze trails up and down his body like she’s attempting to scour for his weak points.

“Cipher,” Phainon greets evenly. He doesn’t even try to smile this time. “You’re back early.”

Cipher grins, showing off her sharp canines. “Couldn’t resist the temptation. Okhema is how I remember. Beautiful. Warm. Nothing like the evernight.” Regardless of how light and airy her tone is, he can detect the bitterness hidden beneath. A touch of wistfulness.

“It’s great. Really nice out here,” Phainon responds. He only needs to pass two more blocks before he’s finally back home.

“Look here, loverboy,” she says, twirling around a familiar golden ring.

Phainon freezes. His blood runs cold.

“Where did you get that?” he asks, stepping forward. The last thing he wants is to deal with this right now.

“Swiped it from Chartonus when he wasn’t looking,” Cipher winks. “He’s been holding onto it for quite some time now… I couldn’t resist. Why, this can sell for a fortune!”

Phainon sighs and stretches his arm out. “Give it.”

A long while ago, he and Chartonus hatched a plan to fish up Queen Gorgo’s ring and had succeeded. He had given the small golden ring to the blacksmith for safe keeping, faltering between wanting Chartonus to hand it over to Mydei or build enough courage to do it himself. In between his busy schedule and the hectic mess that’s been his life for the past few weeks, he’s forgotten entirely.

“Oh, but I went through so much effort to grab this!” Cipher pouts as she fits the ring onto her index finger. Her eyes glint beneath the shade of the stone pillars. “You’re quite the antique collector… Why, this might just be the best piece in your collection!”

“You’ve never seen my collection.” Unless she’s broken into his house. Oh, no—

Cipher grins. Her white tail swishes lazily behind her. “You leave your housekeys in that hideous red vase that you paid way too much money for.”

“...” Mydei did tell him to hide it somewhere else. Maybe he should have listened.

Cipher leans forwards, her kaleidoscope blue eyes curving in amusement as she looks up at Phainon. Soft and low, she murmurs, “You know, I could potentially be persuaded to give it back…”

Phainon sighs. “What do you want?”

“Hm… What do I want?” Cipher tilts her head, grey bangs falling over her eyes, and lifts the ring up high. She rolls it around in her fingers, lips curving into a smirk as she watches it shine in the bright dawn.

The ring is impeccable. Made of the purest of gold and carved by the finest blacksmiths of Castrum Kremnos. It’s a symbol of the Kremnoan empire, a statement of power, of unrelenting will and defying fate.

“It’s for Mydei,” Phainon admits.

“Mmm…” she perks up at the mention. “The little lion.”

Little? Phainon blinks. Lion, yes, but little?

“I have yet to meet him.” Cipher jumps onto the ornate marble railing and lies against the carved pillar with her arms stretched behind her head. “From what I’ve heard, he’s quite the interesting figure. The talk of the town. An alpha like him must be a real catch.” She purrs out the word alpha, lips curving and kaleidoscope eyes glinting as if she’s been told a great joke and is trying not to laugh.

Her gaze is on him, eagerly awaiting response. There’s not much he can say, but the unpleasant feeling in his gut returns full force. She’s only trying to mock him, he knows that much, but any mention of Mydei has him on edge.

A bored sigh falls from Cipher’s lips as she rolls her eyes. She turns her head to the side and mumbles what sounds like another insult. Something regarding the alarming amount of empty space he has in his head?

Phainon fights the urge to growl at her. It’s inappropriate. He’s not that type of alpha.

With a yawn and a wide stretch, Cipher says, “I have some business to take care of… Selling this on the black market sounds like so much work!”

“There’s a black market?” Phainon questions.

“Innocent boy! It’s like you were born yesterday… Of course there is! Lots going on in the black market! It’s extensive too, a whole affair. I could get into the specifics but it’d take me all day, and I really rather not!”

Quick as lightning, she jumps off the railing and appears in front of him. She beckons him closer then whispers, “But… there are lots of priceless, never before seen antiques going around if you know where to look.”

The mention of antiques has him perking up like an attention-starved puppy when its owner returns home after a long day at work. Cipher laughs.

“But… that’s besides the point. I’m not here to dally. I’m busy, after all! Let me cut to the chase, boy. I’ve been hearing what’s been going on. Got cold feet?”

“I have no clue what you’re talking about. Can I get the ring back?”

It’s surprising how empty this part of the city is. Normally, there would be crowds of people passing through. Why are there none today?

“I really didn’t want to intervene but it seems like I have to! The situation is so much more dire than I expected! I better be paid double for my troubles…” she pouts, pressing a finger against her lip as she bends forwards.

“Intervene what?” He’s definitely missing something. Everyone has been acting so cryptic lately. He’s starting to feel a little left out.

“Wow, I thought you were smarter, but I guess I was wrong. No clue what Aglaea sees in you…” Cipher murmurs with a small huff. “My bad! My bad!”

She knows something he doesn’t or it could be another one of her many tricks. Cipher has never liked him, and Phainon can guess why given her history with Aglaea. It makes him wonder why she’s staying so far away from Okhema, but she must have her reasons and he rather not delve too deeply into it. It’s not his business.

“Put aside your biases for a moment and think. Really think.” Phainon opens his mouth to respond but Cipher shushes him and continues, “I wish I could tell it to your face, but it’s all about the journey and not the destination. All you need is that little push and off you go!”

The ring flies through the air, and he catches it.

With a wink, Cipher says, “You know what to do with it, boy.”

Then she’s gone. Disappeared without a single trace.

chapters.html:
Chapter Notes

Mydei’s gaze sweeps yet over another new recruit. This time, it’s a dainty female omega with snow-pale skin and sweet, doe-like features. Her body is willowy and soft, seemingly incapable of wielding a weapon, but looks are deceiving. The fire of determination blazes in her hazel eyes, and she fights furiously, swinging her blade with vengeance—her movements quick like a flash of lightning and merciless like a trained mercenary. She’d be fit as an assassin, hiding away in the dark of the evernight and striking like a viper when the moment calls for it.

But even with her prowess, it doesn't escape Mydei how the other soldiers eye her like she’s a piece of meat they can sink their fangs into and tear apart. He almost wants to shield her from their view, but she regards him as she does the other alpha soldiers, with a type of hesitant respect and wide distance, suspicious towards his every move. Only with Krateros is she honest and open, her eyes glittering as she speaks with loud fervor to the man that has become her mentor. Mydei can’t fault her for her reaction towards him. He’s sure the rumors about him being a heartbreaker and promiscuous alpha must have come into play.

The Kremnoan training hall is no longer populated by only pheromone ridden alphas and silent betas. In the past week, the ranks have ballooned, and now, there are over ten new omega trainees. A rather strange turn of events if Mydei has anything to say about it. He had previously believed Iavokos to be the sole exception to the rule, but Krateros has been steadily recruiting more omegas, both male and female. Even weirder is how Krateros trains them personally, overseeing their progress, while not allowing any of the other instructors to intervene. It almost feels personal, targeted.

The temptation to ask is there, but Mydei refrains. He can’t jump to conclusions, even if his curiosity grows with each passing interaction, especially when Krateros speaks proudly about the young omega soldiers. It’s very strange, and Mydei doesn’t even know how to begin to react to the rapid change of events.

Given his reputation and wisdom from years of hard battle, Krateros is second in command of the Kremnoan army. As such, no one dares to speak up against him or do anything drastic to upset the status quo, though the tension in the hall speaks volumes. Mydei bears witness to fervent whisperings, hungry gazes, and snide comments.

It’s nearing the end of ascent hour. Mydei circles the hall, boots clicking against the stone floor. A few meters away, he spots two soldiers whispering amongst each other as they glance over at the group of omega recruits doing stretches.

“Is Krateros going senile? Recruiting these bitches and ruining the sanctity of Kremnoan tradition…” the first alpha soldier mutters to his companion.

The second one takes a big swig of water and chuckles. “Don’t worry, I’m sure Krateros brought them in as stress relief. After all, Okheman brothels lack the beauty of Kremnoan omegas. I call dibs on the blonde one with the wide hips and fat ass.”

Luckily, the training hall is a ruckus of shouts and the loud clanging of tempered metal against metal. It takes minimal effort to sneak behind the two gossiping soldiers.

Crossing his arms tightly across his chest, Mydei asks, “What are we talking about here?”

Both alphas jump, far too engrossed with their conversation on which omega would cry and moan the loudest to notice the crown prince approaching.

“Your highness! It is an honor,” the first one greets, bowing deeply. His fingers twitch at his sides. “We were merely taking a break and will be back to training soon. Glory to Castrum Kremnos!”

The second one nods along, fingers turning white from how tightly he’s gripping his water jug. “Thank you for checking up on us, your highness.”

Mydei fixes them with a cold, flat expression. “A break is meant to clear the mind, not create greater turmoil. Speak more of your inappropriate nonsense, and I will send you both to Krateros. Do I make myself clear?”

Both soldiers squeak out weak apologies, flimsy excuses that hold no weight. Mydei almost wants to snarl at them and slam them both into the ground. Fortunately, he has self-restraint, even if his fingers curl at his sides. There’s no need to make a scene. He will alert Krateros of the matter, though he’s sure the older alpha already knows.

The bitterness settles and to distract himself, Mydei pulls open his laptop and begins working on his animations. Drawing is a comfort, a small hobby of his that would have the entirety of the Kremnoan detachment laughing if they knew. Sitting beneath the lamplight, he falls into the comforting rhythm, but his imagination stays firmly planted in one direction.

This one he’s not going to post. It’s far too risky. Many people in Okhema theorize who’s behind the popular Fig Stew account, and he rather not out himself in the most embarrassing way possible.

The tension in his body fizzles out as he stares down at his newest animation, still in its rough draft stages. Fig Stew and Beagle Coconut are surrounded by a litter of energetic pups, all grey with round blue eyes. Fig Stew chirps and the pups follow while Beagle Coconut stays nestled tightly beside Fig Stew.

The next scene has Fig Stew curled up on the grass, purring softly as it feeds its little of unruly pups, while Beagle Coconut whimpers, walking in circles, vying for Fig Stew’s undivided attention.

His expression softens, a pull of a smile at the corner of his lips.

Beside him, his teleslate pings. From an unknown source, it reads: “Have you told him yet?”

Ridden with confusion, he places his stylus down and grabs his teleslate. Is this a spam caller? Perhaps, someone who’s gotten the wrong number?

He answers with a simple and clear: “You must have gotten the wrong number.”

The response is instantaneous, almost mocking: “Have you told him yet, crown prince Mydeimos of Castrum Kremnos?”

What in the river of souls? He stares blankly down at his screen, the words clear in their intent. This person is targeting him. Are they attempting to draw out information?

Then comes a knock at his door, snapping him out of his daze.

He ignores it. The knocks continue, and Phainon yells, “Hey, Mydei! I know you’re in there!”

His eye twitches. After what must have been the tenth knock, he yanks the door open, fingernails digging into the white painted wood, and snaps, “Quit making a ruckus.”

Effortlessly charming as ever, Phainon leans against the doorframe and grins, “My dear prince, may I come in?”

“No.” He slams the door in Phainon’s face.

“Mydei! Hey!”

If Phainon truly wanted to, he could easily kick the door in. He’s seen firsthand how strong the alpha is when he isn’t holding back. There's been many times where Phainon pins him down, and he’s unable to do anything but wait for Phainon to get off him—a feather against a boulder.

Aglaea wouldn’t take so kindly to finding the villa’s pristine walls caved in by an overeager Phainon, and he knows how greatly Phainon respects her, so he should be safe in that regard.

Under no circumstances can he have Phainon entering his room. Not when it looks like this. Not when his bedsheets and blankets lay soiled in a corner and his bed piled high with what is evidently an omega’s personal nest. The pill bottles, blue and white, stand proud on his nightstand, and he quickly shoves them into the cabinet.

Maybe he should throw everything into his closet. Pretend the nest never existed. Return to normalcy. A bed with nothing more than a single pillow and a measly blanket.

Only… It feels like he’s ripping a piece of himself away, caging himself once more.

No. He can’t do it. The prospect of losing what little comfort he has and having to return to a cold, barren room has him shaking his head.

And there’s that infuriating part of him that coos to invite Phainon into his nest and have him rub his scent all over his blankets and pillows until every nook and crevice is filled with the scent of spring and sunshine. He wants to cuddle beside Phainon, wants Phainon to praise him for being a good omega, for having a soft nest perfect for mating.

It’s stupid. Irrational. He knows it to be, yet he can’t resist. There’s little it takes for him to crumble. He never used to be this way, never acting so rash.

Back then, he couldn’t afford to. Coming to Okhema has changed him, and he’s not quite sure if it’s for the better or for the worse, but he wouldn’t exchange what he has now, not for anything.

ོ༘₊⁺☀︎₊⁺⋆.˚

Usually, he’s not one to complain. It’s unbefitting of him to raise a ruckus or proclaim his dissatisfaction. As the crown prince of Castrum Kremnos and survivor of the wretched sea of souls, body forged and re-forged thousands of times, he learned young that there’s little use in crying over what cannot change, the rules etched into the core of the earth, the code of the world. It may be unfair and frustrating, but complaining solves nothing.

Now, he feels differently. He’s ready to launch into an avalanche of complaints all because of one infuriating alpha who won’t stop with that blinding grin of his.

Sleep is important. Now that he’s no longer constantly watching behind his shoulder or on guard for the next ambush, safe within the confines of Okhema, Mydei takes his sleep very seriously.

Phainon, on the other hand, does not. He knocks and knocks, yelling for Mydei to wake up, insisting that they have to get ready in the morning together, establish a routine together. With deep-set eyebags and an irritated scowl that would frighten anybody with a functioning brain, Mydei pulls himself out of bed only to be dragged to the communal bathroom by Phainon who refuses to let go, even as Mydei tries to swipe at him.

Now, they’re here. Mydei yawns and rubs at his eyes as he grabs his toothbrush.

“Your toothbrush…” Phainon murmurs, looking at it as if it’s the most fascinating thing in all of Amphoreus, more so than any priceless antique. “Erm, why is it pink?”

Mydei stares at him, eyebrows pinching together, disbelief written all over his sleepy features. “Yes.”

Phainon holds in a laugh. Or attempts to. He fails, a tidal wave of giggles spilling from his lips as he clutches his stomach, tears forming droplets in the corner of his eyes.

What’s so funny?

Mydei’s fingers twitch at his sides. It’s way too early for this. He thought he was an early riser, but it seems Phainon has got him beat. Makes no sense too because he swears Phainon rises later than he does.

Another loud giggle. His eye begins to twitch.

What kind of grown man giggles like that? Even through the exasperation, he can’t help the heat that floods his cheeks. He turns away before Phainon can tease him for it.

“Do you have a problem, Deliverer?” he bites out.

Once more, Phainon tries to hold it in only to snort. He stares down, noticing the pink bunny slippers adorning Mydei’s feet and promptly starts to choke. Mydei frowns. Castorice had bought the slippers for him when she noticed him not so subtly eyeing them at the market, stating that it was a welcome gift.

His ears burn, and he turns to leave only for Phainon to grab his wrist. Blue eyes crinkle, shining with tears. “I think it’s adorable.”

He’s itching to make distance, but his attempts to wretch his wrist free results in his downfall —Phainon giving him the widest of puppy eyes. Sometimes it’s hard to believe Phainon is an alpha with how he acts, nothing at all like the toxic bravado of Kremnoan alphas he’s used to.

From the first quint of entry hour to the last quint of curtain-fall hour, Phainon sticks by his side. His every waking moment is spent with the alpha, and he even has the audacity to begin to whimpering when Mydei insists on taking a midday nap. Alone.

“Why won’t you let me in? We can nap together!” Phainon exclaims, staring at Mydei with those big blue eyes of his. If he had puppy ears, they would be drooping, and he even gives a small, pathetic whine when Mydei refuses him yet again.

Under no circumstances can Phainon enter his room.

It takes a lot of effort to remove himself from Phainon’s side. The alpha insists on staying within five feet at all times, even choosing the room beside his to occupy. He should be complaining, telling Phainon to stop with his antics, but it’s not so bad. He feels warm and fuzzy all over like he’s wrapped up in soft blankets.

When he’s with Phainon, he’s safe, and safe isn’t a word he’s used to.

He doesn’t know what to do with this new information.

ོ༘₊⁺☀︎₊⁺⋆.˚

It’s the middle of the week when Castorice returns. She carries a bag full of goodies, her eyes sparkling in excitement as she skips through the door.

“Lord Mydei!” Castorice smiles. “Ah! Lord Phainon, you’re here too!” The confusion is written all over her face, and her wildflower scent falters.

“I moved in,” Phainon says, lounging on the living room kline as if he owns it. He gives a small frown. “Like two days ago? Right, Mydei?”

“Three days ago,” Mydei replies gruffly. They sit beside each other with Phainon’s legs crossing over Mydei’s lap. He’s told Phainon to get off five times now only to be refused each time. “Welcome back, Castorice.”

“Thank you, Lord Mydei…” Castorice trails off, eyeing the both of them. “Erm, uh, that’s great news! Anything else you two would like to share?”

“Hm?” Phainon tilts his head. “No. Nothing else that I can think of…” He tilts his head, pondering over Castorice’s question. A light bulb goes off in his head, and he continues, “Oh! Actually, I may have borrowed a blanket or two from your room since a certain someone wouldn’t let me borrow any of his. I tried texting you to ask, but I’m not sure if you got my messages.”

“Stop pouting, Deliverer,” Mydei says, somewhat distracted, as he scrolls through his teleslate, ignoring the weight of Phainon’s muscular calves pressing against his thighs. As of late, he’s been into looking at baby clothes and accessories lately—cute little onesies with chimera patterns and pastel bow headbands. It quenches the fire inside him, the desire that’s overtaken his thoughts lately—to be Phainon’s mate and bear his pups.

Not that he’d ever willingly admit it.

His teleslate pings, and he has to bite back a groan. It’s yet another message from that unknown source. The same old “Have you told him yet?” Mydei’s eye twitches and his fingers move on autopilot, blocking the number even knowing that in an hour, they’ll be back with the same damn message.

Whoever the person is, they’re persistent. What do they want from him?

He only hopes they’re not referring to his conversation with Phainon. Unless there’s spy cameras in the villa, there’s no way they could know. He’s tried subtly asking only to receive “You know exactly what I’m referring to” as a response. Cryptic and useless. It reveals nothing.

Phainon turns to give Mydei a miffed look with his lips pouty and nose scrunched. “Can you blame me? You used to let me into your room with no issue! Remember when you gave me keys to your house? And now you won’t even let me borrow a blanket…”

“Get your own, you big baby.”

“Look at him!” Phainon says, indignant, as he jabs a finger towards Mydei. “This is what I have to deal with!”

Castorice giggles. “You did choose to live here, Lord Phainon.”

“Okay, but that doesn’t mean he has free reign to do whatever!”

“Hmph. Quit complaining.” His eyes land on a white baby onesie patterned with pastel blue flowers. It’s adorable and for a decent price too. He should buy it and save it for when he and Phainon—No. That’s never going to happen. Stop.

“He’s a terrible roommate…” Phainon sniffs. “Won’t even cook dinner without burning it on purpose! And why did you put that much sugar into the beef stew? You’re not that dumb! I mean, salt and sugar do look similar, but the jars were clearly labelled. Mydei… Ah, I forget you can’t read…”

Mydei rolls his eyes, ignoring the obvious bait as he continues scrolling through his teleslate. There's a subtle ache that’s settled in his chest but he pays it no mind. “How have you been, Castorice?”

“Good…” Castorice trails off.

“You’re no fun, Mydei,” Phainon pouts. He pulls his legs off of Mydei’s lap and scoots over to sit right beside him. “Eh? Why are you looking at baby clothes?”

Castorice blinks. Mydei’s cheeks burn.

Mortified, Phainon asks, “Did you get someone pregnant?!” A pause and a loud gasp. “Don’t tell me it’s—”

Mydei clamps a hand over Phainon’s mouth, face burning. His eyebrows draw together as he hisses, “Shut up. Stop talking.”

“I brought some gifts,” Castorice quickly interjects, showing off the items in her tote like she’s an experienced saleswoman. “Look! Woven bracelets for everyone. With cute animal charms too! I got myself this bunny with floppy ears. A fluffy white dog for you, Lord Phainon, and an orange cat for Lord Mydei! I got some for the others too! I didn’t forget Lady Cipher either. She’s visiting soon, isn’t she? Haha…”

Later in the day, Mydei finds himself in front of Castorice’s door. Phainon had left the villa on short notice, giving him time to visit her without making it a three-way conversation.

“Lord Mydei!” Castorice exclaims. “How can I help you?”

“Should I tell him?” Mydei asks.

Castorice blinks. The words settle in, and she perks up, grabbing him by the shoulders. Given their height difference, she has to get on her tippy toes to even reach but that doesn’t stop her from shaking him like she means business. “Yes! You should tell Lord Phainon!”

When she realizes her outburst, she pulls away and says, “Sorry, I mean, you should have an honest conversation with Lord Phainon. Really speak with him and understand his point of view. I think you should tell him, but only you can really decide that.”

She lets Mydei into her room, walls colored light lavender and decor cutesy with soft, fairy lights patterning the walls and crocheted dolls covering her desk, colorful yarn strung all over. There’s a wreath made of lavender and lilac flowers at the head of her bed, and a shelf stacked full of books of all genres.

Her bed is pushed to the side, nest artfully arranged, a bouquet of pastels, white and soft purples. While Mydei’s nest is mostly glossy satin pillows with minimal design and the occasional soft plush, Castorice’s nest is exclusively fuzzy textured ones and ones shaped like different creatures. Her collection is vast and what she has out today is not the same as the first time.

Looking over her arrangement, at the adorable purple daisy plush sitting beside the tall chimera hugging pillow, Mydei is tempted to add more to his own collection. He even spots a large pomegranate in the corner of her nest, its deep crimson contrasting against the soft colors of her nest. Castorice perks up, grabbing it and handing it over to Mydei.

“It’s for you,” she beams. “I found it at the market but didn’t have time to give it to you until now. Hope you like it!”

Mydei hugs it to his chest, face heating up. “Thank you.”

Together, they lay side by side in her nest, nestled amongst a sea of warmth.

“Phainon told me my scent sent him into rut,” Mydei tells her. It’s almost embarrassing to admit.

Castorice chokes on air. Her long purple hair fans around her as she grabs a nearby pillow and hugs it. She turns to face him, amethyst eyes glowing. Her sweet voice comes out dire, urgent in a manner he’s never heard before. “You should tell him. Lord Mydei, you have to tell him. He needs to know.”

“I…” Mydei brushes his bangs away from his face. “I told him I would arrange a meeting after the gathering.”

“There’s no rush. Do so when you’re ready, but Lord Mydei, promise me you’ll tell him.”

Mydei stares up at the ceiling, eyes tracing the hanging butterfly lights, glowing purple in the dim light. It’d be nice to decorate his room more and to not have to hide. To have Phainon with him, hanging out in his room like how it used to be.

Regaining a sense of normality. Not having to pretend. He’d like that. Even if revealing the truth would mean Phainon would never desire him the way he wants, what other choice does he have?

“I promise,” he murmurs—a prayer.
