Objectively, it’s nice up here. Warmer than usual—the dawn’s rays burn brighter this high— but there’s a clear view of Okhema and the surrounding waterfall, the rush of crystalline water as it slams against hard rock. Had it been any other day, he wouldn’t be here alone. Mydei would have been nestled right beside him, where he should be.

He recalls the first time they sparred together at this rooftop, the frenzy as they attempted to one up the other, clashing in broad daylight amongst the sea of passing cityfolk below. Hours of combat had resulted in the two of them landing on their backs, side by side as they basked in the bright dawn and the blue skies. Ever since, this rooftop has held a special place in his heart. Call him sentimental, but that’s the truth. When it concerns Mydei, he latches on and never lets go.

His foot taps rhythmically against red, dusty tiles. A soft breeze brings the scent of spring, rustling his moonlight bangs as he gazes upon the city around him, the bright whites contrasting with the deep blues accented with gold. With a soft sigh, he plops down on the rug, one leg bent upwards, and turns his attention to the world-bearing titan carrying the dawn device atop its shoulders, the sole source of light in all of Amphoreus.

When Phainon had gotten a sudden and unwelcome request from Cipher for a casual chat, he had ignored her. He wasn’t in the mood to cater to her whims, not when it was already nearing parting hour, and he was in his nightrobes already.

You don’t want the ring back then? >:3c is how she responded when he left her on read. Phainon had stared down at his teleslate, repeating the words over and over until it clicked.

Embarrassing as it is to admit, he panicked and asked where and when.

Somehow, Cipher had broken into the villa without either him or Mydei noticing and had stolen the ring from where he had kept it tightly locked in his room. Even after all the precautions, she still saw through him and dug the ring out of the deepest corner of his closet. He had planned to keep it hidden—his treacherous secret—until he figured out the best time and method to give it to Mydei—if it were ever to arrive.

Time flies by. No Cipher in sight. He doesn’t even need to check to know it’s nearing the last quint of parting hour. He’s half tempted to leave, sleepiness burgeoning behind his eyelids.

Begrudgingly, he hoists himself up and steps into the shade of the nearby temple balcony. The cool, smooth stone wall feels good against his back, and he lets his eyes flutter shut. A quick reprieve before he has to deal with the inevitable.

Familiar footsteps echo, the harsh clink of metal greaves against white stone. Warmth burgeons in his chest, followed by a shred of unease. The rhythm isn’t correct, faster than usual and not nearly as steady. A body lands firmly in front of him, and Phainon cracks an eye open.

“Deliverer,” Mydei greets, in all his ferocious Kremnoan glory. He’s even dressed in full armor—chest half exposed, golden greaves, gauntlets, heavy jewelry, and all.

Eh? Phainon blinks.

Last he had seen, Mydei, clothed casually in a loose tank top and chimera patterned sweatpants, had retreated into his room for the day. Once again, Phainon had tried to enter only to be pushed away in the same manner as before, the door roughly slammed in his face. It doesn’t escape his attention how red Mydei’s face had turned at even the briefest mention of Phainon entering.

He’s hiding something, that’s for sure. As for what that is, Phainon has little clue.

“Mydei!” Phainon greets, a wide smile blooming on his features despite the confusion. The presence of the other alpha is always a welcome surprise.

Blonde hair dipped in red sways lightly from the afternoon breeze. Mydei stands before him, arms crossed tight against his chest in that manner that has the round of his breast look even rounder, squeezing against the solid muscle of his forearms.

Phainon sucks in a breath. No, he’s not staring. He’s simply making an observation.

“Stop staring,” Mydei says, only to pull his arms closer, pressing his chest tighter together. The motion doesn’t go unnoticed by Phainon who has to forcefully yank his gaze away.

“I’m not,” Phainon argues, though his eyes begin to wander once more. He clears his throat, “What brings you here, my dear prince? Did you miss me that much?”

He’s about to say more, but a glint of gold catches his eye. There on Mydei’s index finger is a ring—the signet ring. It looks good on him, perfect and fit for a king.

How does he have it? Phainon’s stomach drops, and it doesn’t escape his notice how Mydei’s gauntlets have disappeared entirely. They were there only moments ago. When could they have…?

Oh.

Okay, this makes infinitely more sense.

Phainon narrows his eyes. “Cipher.”

“Who?” Mydei questions.

“I know it’s you.” No wonder he felt so uneasy. This isn’t Mydei.

He should have known. The heir of trickery is known for her ability to shapeshift, changing her appearance and even pheromones in less than a blink of an eye. Her accuracy is uncanny, her disguises virtually indistinguishable from the genuine articles. Naturally, she has no scent —yet another alpha who’s able to control her pheromones.

Mydei—Cipher grins. “I have no clue what you’re talking about, Deliverer.”

“Give me the ring back,” Phainon sighs. “And stop with the Mydei disguise. It’s creepy.”

“You’re no fun!” Cipher pouts. Only she’s wearing Mydei’s face, and it has Phainon pausing in his step.

Mydei. Pouting. His plush bottom lip jutted out and trembling ever so slightly, complete with glimmering golden eyes lined with crimson. Oh titans. His head spins.

Cute. Mydei is so cute.

“Stop with the disguise,” Phainon repeats. “Please.”

“Mmm, how about no?” Cipher purrs, eyes curving in amusement. “I quite like it. I’m so tall and imposing… Amazing figure too!” As she speaks, she runs a gauntleted hand down the ridges and hard muscle of Mydei’s bare torso. “It’s no wonder he’s so popular with omegas.”

A snarl brews in Phainon’s throat.

Cipher laughs, “Besides, I can’t exactly take it off now. Everyone would see! It’d ruin the surprise if Aglaea were to hear that I’m back early. Humor me, will you?”

“How are you so sure she doesn’t already know? This is Aglaea we’re talking about.”

“I know my workarounds,” Cipher shrugs, baring sharp canines as she arches her back in a wide stretch and yawns.

Mydei’s canines aren’t nearly that sharp. How odd. Now that he thinks about it, they’re rather flat for an alpha.

“I didn’t think you’d be affected, but I guess I was wrong,” Cipher continues, tilting her head to the side as she places a hand on her chin. “Aren’t you the closest one to the little lion? You should have been the first to figure it out.”

Figure out what?

“He’s my comrade,” Phainon says, hesitant. “And fellow heir, as are you.”

Cipher scoffs, rolling her eyes in the same manner Mydei does when he’s annoyed at Phainon’s ceaseless antics. “You can’t be serious… Considering the gossip that the bathhouse staff like to throw around, I’d expect you to say more than simple comrades.” She turns away and mutters, “But that’s just like you, isn’t it? Tch.”

Phainon can’t help but squawk, his cheeks burning as he remembers what last transpired in the baths, the feel of Mydei on his lap, the warmth of their bodies in the hazy steam. “We’re simply improving our camaraderie by bathing together! What do you mean the bathhouse staff are gossiping about us?! There’s nothing that—”

He’s shushed by the press of a finger against his parted lips. Cipher takes a step forward and leans in, closing their distance. Her voice comes out as a deep purr, “You look up to him. Am I correct?”

If he could, Phainon would have backed away. Unfortunately, the heel of his boot meets stone. “Is that a trick question?”

Cipher presses closer. Had she been in her usual form, he wouldn’t have hesitated to slide out of the way, but his body doesn’t move because Mydei.

Sharp golden eyes flecked with orange glint in the shadow. Her voice pitches lower, “Answer me.”

His body reacts as if it were Mydei in front of him, caging him in, their bodies too close for comfort. He can hardly breathe, and he turns his head to the side to escape Cipher’s piercing gaze.

He knows it’s not Mydei. Rationally, he knows Mydei is probably asleep in the villa, snoring in that soft way he does, sounding too much like a content cat’s purr. He catches his wits and says, “I’m taller than he is, as you can see.” A few wild arm gestures later, he continues with a weak, “If anything, he looks up to me...”

Cipher’s lips split into a predatory smile. She leans in until they’re almost nose to nose, chest to chest, and Phainon fights the urge to shriek. His back is flat against the wall now, and the beginnings of panic brew hot, lighting his nerves.

Mydei radiates warmth, and like a foolish moth to flame, Phainon is drawn to it. He wants to lean in and capture what he hasn’t allowed himself to have. What he doesn’t deserve to have but wants so terribly.

No. Stop. This is Cipher. Even if she carries herself like Mydei does, it’s still Cipher.

Beneath the patches and lotion, his pheromones burn and blister. Cipher grabs him by the chin and yanks his head back. Her nose wrinkles, and fear pierces through Phainon like an arrow.

“I’m being serious here. Doesn’t happen often, but the situation is rather dire…”

“Can you get off me?” Phainon asks—begs. “What if people see? There’s bound to be some misunderstanding…”

“I’ll get off you if you stop with the deflection, boy.”

“I’m not deflecting…”

Cipher slams her free hand beside Phainon’s head and continues to lean forwards.

“Fine! Okay, you got me!” Phainon acquiesces. Laughter bubbles in his throat. “Who doesn’t look up to Mydei? He’s something else. I can hardly describe him! I’ve never met anyone like him, and it’s astounding. He’s a beast on the battlefield—you should watch him fight, it’s inspiring—and he holds himself so effortlessly and fights for what he believes in. He’s a born leader, charismatic and confident—the perfect alpha who inspires awe wherever he goes. He has conviction, and he’s not afraid to be himself. Not to mention, he’s beautiful with a body carved by Mnestia herself. He’s…” Phainon coughs. “He’s everything… He—”

“He’s your equal, so I’m told,” Cipher cuts in. Golden eyes glint like she has him cornered. “But you don’t actually believe that, do you?”

“...” It hits like a slap in the face. To be told so forthrightly by someone he barely knows, it's almost insulting. His shoulders tense.

Mydei considers them equals, believes in it wholeheartedly and mentions it frequently, acting as if it’s effortless fact and not falsities concocted in the passionate throes of battle. Those ten days and nights they spent fighting, basking in each other’s presence, the heat of sweaty bodies clashing and entangling, all coalescing in the formation of their early relationship as equals, yet…

He can’t help but believe it as a joke or Mydei’s sincere attempts to placate him. He’s only a village boy—one thrust into the flamechase after the destruction of his home. Compared to Mydei, the crown prince of a city-state, leader and future king, he’s nothing. It’s day and night.

Mydei holds himself as such, effortlessly confident and commanding as if it were as simple as breathing. They aren’t alike in the slightest and for Mydei to even consider him an equal… it’s a miracle that Phainon, years later, can’t bring himself to fully believe.

He doesn’t need to respond. Cipher sighs and steps away. “Really, it’s no wonder. I miscalculated.”

“Miscalculated what?” Phainon asks. He can finally breathe again, Cipher’s suffocating presence bearing down on him gone.

“Remember what I told you last time?”

“You said many things.”

“The other heirs had no trouble seeing it,” Cipher muses. She looks over at him, eyebrows pinched in what looks to be concern…? Only this is Cipher, so there’s no way—

“There’s a lot going on up there, rascal. You sure you’re okay?” she asks. Her voice is still Mydei’s, and it squeezes Phainon’s heart to hear those words.

“I’m fine.” His response is instant, unyielding.

Cipher shakes her head, hand planted against her forehead. “You’re hopeless.” She twirls her braid around. “And so is he.”

Confused, Phainon responds, “You’ve never met him.”

“I’ve heard enough.”

He almost wants to ask her what she’s heard, if it’s the rumors or something else entirely. He opens his mouth only to lurch back when Cipher lands in front of him once more. There’s a flick of fingers against his forehead, then silence.

Phainon stares on, unblinking, unseeing.

It was gentle, not intended to hurt or impart much of an impact at all, but the change is palpable. He’s not sure what happened, but he feels lighter, like a weight has been pulled off his chest.

Something had shattered. Maybe his skull? He places a hand to his forehead to find the skin intact.

“There,” Cipher smiles, lips stretched wide in glee as if patting herself on the back. She wears Mydei’s appearance like she owns it, brightening his features in that exaggerated manner she prefers, but he finds that Mydei looks good smiling. He only wishes he had the ability to make Mydei smile like that.

“Now, off you go,” Cipher continues, handing Phainon the ring once more. “Go snag that little lion.”

ོ༘₊⁺☀︎₊⁺⋆.˚

Phainon quickly comes to learn that he’s the odd one out. The third wheel so to speak.

His head buzzes—Cipher’s words repeat in his head. She’s seen through him, and it’s terrifying. Not only is she unpredictable, she also doesn’t hide her dislike of him. He’s but an injured mouse caught in the grasp of a crafty cat, sharp claws sunken deep into his soft body. There’s no way she’s not planning something, but she also seems to be rooting for him? He’s a little conflicted there.

He stumbles his way back to the villa, the path a blur. If he trips on a stray rock here and there, that’s only for him to know and the odd cityfolk that walk the streets at this late an hour. The doors to the villa welcome him and he enters, ready to flop onto his bed only to come face to face with Castorice and Mydei cuddling.

Cuddling.

In Castorice’s room. In her nest.

What in the Kephale is going on? Is he losing his mind?

He’s in awe for a moment, unable to compute what’s before him. Castorice’s room is only a small distance away from his, and the door had been slightly ajar, revealing the two entangled together in the comfort of fluffy pillows and soft blankets.

His heart squeezes at the sight of the two of them so close. The full force of knowing that they’re closer than he had previously believed hits him and knocks his breath away.

“He’s asleep,” Castorice whispers, glancing over at Mydei who’s curled up against the cozy purples and whites of Castorice’s nest, looking as if he belongs there. She smiles up at Phainon, and it does nothing to stop the bitter tang in his throat. “How may I help you, Lord Phainon?”

Mydei is clutching a pomegranate pillow to his chest as soft snores, barely audible, fall from his lips. It’s a sight to behold, and Phainon’s leg twitches with the urge to get a better look. He’s still standing outside Castorice’s door, keeping a respectable distance away.

An unmated alpha and an unmated omega nesting together. There’s no mistaking it.

It could be that Castorice and Mydei are only friends, but it seems unlikely given the current situation. This isn’t a matter of familial relations. His mood was already teetering on the edge, and now he feels even worse. This is the worst possible outcome for someone like him —someone so deeply in love with a fellow alpha who, most certainly, doesn’t return the same feelings.

“Do you want to cuddle with him?” Castorice asks. Her voice pitches higher, eyes glimmering in excitement. He knows her and he can’t be mad at her, not for long. She’s a sweet soul. Most of the time that is.

Cuddling with Mydei… Phainon gulps.

His mind works on its own. The answer is obvious.

“It’s your nest…” Phainon croaks out.

“I give you full permission!” Castorice beams.

No matter how much he wants to, he can’t bring himself to cross that boundary.

Entering Castorice’s nest to cuddle with Mydei when he’s not conscious is wrong. Objectively wrong. He can’t take advantage of Mydei like that, and while Castorice’s scent is nice, he would rather not be surrounded by it even if he has Mydei, warm and purring contently, right beside him.

If only Mydei had his own nest, his own carved out space where they could cuddle together and indulge in each other. If only Mydei would allow him in instead of pushing him away. If only…

ོ༘₊⁺☀︎₊⁺⋆.˚

Phainon swears he’s going crazy. He likes Castorice, he really does, but he’d be lying if he didn’t admit that he preferred when she wasn’t here.

It’s horrible of him to feel this way, yet he can’t shrug off the negativity. He's a bad friend but even that admonishment does nothing to abate the bitterness. Why is that?

Because Mydei sticks to her side more than he does with Phainon—the brutal, honest truth.

It’s like the rug has been pulled out from under him and he’s nursing a huge bruise on his ass from where he fell. The hurt threatens to spill over, the twitching of his facial expressions whenever he sees the two of them together. He’s glad the scent patches and lotions are doing their job but now he’s layering on double just in case.

They even giggle over some inside jokes that Phainon has little clue about! He really is an outsider.

Phainon wonders… Does Mydei have a crush on Castorice?

He wouldn’t be surprised if he did. The image of him in her nest is seared into his brain at this point, and considering how close they’ve grown in a matter of weeks, it’s the most reasonable option. Mydei is one of many alphas that have taken to Castorice. He can’t even fault Mydei because of how sweet and kind she is—even with her curse of death—and how honeyed her scent is, irresistible to many alphas. It has Phainon pondering if Mydei moved into the villa to be closer to her. When did these feelings even begin? Probably recently, given their sudden change in relationship.

It’s especially strange how Mydei doesn’t succumb to her curse of death anymore. Phainon recalls the tournament where Mydei and Castorice armwrestled for the title of champion. Mydei had died, drifting over to the River of Souls, the light leaving his eyes for the briefest moments, thus ensuring Castorice’s sound victory. But now, he’s unaffected by her touches.

Could it be that they're compatible and meant to be together? No one else can stand to be within four paces of her, yet he acts as if her curse does not exist.

The thoughts run rampant, and the weight of the signet ring in his pocket continues to grow. There’s no way he can give this to Mydei, not now. He hides it in his closet once more. There’s no use in trying to hide it in a new spot because Cipher can swipe it whenever, but he’s not about to keep it in his pocket when it’s a constant reminder of his one-sided feelings.

Even if Mydei likes her, Castorice isn’t interested, not at all. If anything, she’s weirdly invested in getting them together. Had Phainon not read her very graphic and detailed stories, he would have believed that she simply supported their friendship. Now, he knows better.

There are monstrosities brewing in that innocuous purple notebook of hers, the one decorated with cutesy flower designs and hand-drawn chimera stickers.

Phainon can picture it. Kind of. Some of the positions that Castorice wrote about are nigh impossible to fulfill. One of them had him doing a handstand while Mydei bent down on all fours. He doesn’t even want to think about the logistics of that nor the catastrophe that would ensue if he were to topple over. Though, he is intrigued by the position she calls the mating press. It sounds reasonable enough and the thought of folding Mydei in half is hotter than it should be.

From what he’s had the pleasure—displeasure?—of reading, he’s always the one fucking Mydei. And it begs the question, does Mydei know? Has he read her fantastical stories? What would he think? Would he object to it? Would he even care? Would he be upset that the omega that he’s potentially clamoring over is writing graphic smut about him and his rival? There’s much to think about, and he’s getting wildly off topic. He’s free falling off a ledge, and there’s no ground in sight.

“Lord Phainon, please do me a favor,” Castorice says, sitting at the table with her notebook— that accursed notebook—in front of her. She leans against her elbow and clicks her pen at random as she stares idly at the blank page.

The kitchen smells sweet of whipped cream and shortbread pastry. Mydei is meticulously slicing away at an assortment of colorful fruits, the intensity of his expression unbridled. He always has that look in his eye when he’s focused, the one where the gold of his iris grows darker and his pupils narrow into slits like a lion honing in on prey.

“Yes?” Phainon asks.

“Stand behind Lord Mydei,” she commands like a queen ordering her knight.

Curious, Phainon does as he’s told. Knowing Castorice, he has a pretty good idea of what’s coming next, but he never thought she would be this bold. He eyes Mydei, trying to gauge his reaction, but from this angle, he can only see the alpha bending down slightly as he continues his task.

In the midst of fashioning bunny shapes out of crisp apples and kitty shapes out of strawberries, Mydei remains unbothered by the commotion around him. Even when Castorice asks for Phainon to inch closer until they’re nearly back to chest, he gives little reaction.

Phainon has to hand it to Mydei for his dedication. All of this work in the name of an overly intricate fruit tart that’ll probably be consumed in mere minutes. Earlier, he had tried to sneak an apple slice only to have his hand unceremoniously slapped away. He’s still a little miffed about that one.

“Now, wrap your arms around his waist.”

“Huh?” Phainon squawks.

“Excuse me?” Mydei turns, hand wrapped around the hilt of his knife. The metal glints, strawberry juice drips, a silent threat.

“I need this for research purposes,” Castorice says, nodding to herself. “It’s super important. Now, Lord Phainon, if you will.”

“For your stories?” Phainon can’t help but ask.

“I’m doing a collaboration with Fig Stew. I need inspiration.”

“...” Mydei’s eyelashes quiver.

Phainon gasps. “Fig Stew?! Congrats! That’s wild! Does that mean you know who they are?”

“Uh, huh,” Castorice responds, smug in a way he’s never seen before. “Fig Stew gave me full creative control.”

“You still need to run the ideas through them. They can refuse,” Mydei says. “Deliverer, go make yourself useful and get the grapes out of the fridge.”

Castorice holds an innocent expression, soft amethyst eyes and a sweet smile. She nibbles her pen and says, “Fig Stew is very understanding and can be reasoned with. Now, Lord Phainon, wrap your arms around Lord Mydei’s waist. The grapes can wait.”

Phainon turns to face her.

“Grapes, Deliverer. Now.”

He turns back to look at Mydei.

“No! Wrap your arms around his waist. Don’t be shy. I know what you two get up to in the baths.”

He’s torn. His eyes flit from Castorice to Mydei back to Castorice then to Mydei once more. Mydei’s expression grows stern while the smile on Castorice’s lips stretches wider. He’s a rope pulled taut in a game of tug of war, a puppy being told by his lovely owners to do opposite things at once. He wants to please both of them but—

Mydei’s teleslate pings, and Phainon jumps at the opportunity to swipe it from the kitchen counter. “Got it!” He exclaims, louder than necessary, and squints his eyes to read, “Did you tell him yet?”

The teleslate is snatched out of his hand. With far too much force than necessary, Mydei stuffs it in his pocket before fixing Phainon with a deep glare.

Laughter bubbles in Phainon’s throat. Cute. Had Mydei’s cheeks not been flushed lovely pink, it’d be more menacing. Instead, he looks like a bullied maiden, eyebrows drawn together and long eyelashes quivering as he quickly turns away.

“Tell him what?” Phainon questions, curious. He glances over at Castorice who has begun to scribble wildly in her notebook while not meeting his gaze, purple bangs covering her face from view.

He leans closer, and Mydei snarls like a defensive kitten protecting its territory. He holds his kitchen knife in front of him, and his face has only gotten redder.

Phainon can’t help but grin. He pulls his arms up in mock surrender and says, “Calm down.”

A faint scent of pomegranate saturates the air, fragrant and soft. Only it dissipates as quickly as it came, leaving no trace of its existence.

“Grapes, Deliverer,” Mydei says—commands. His shoulders are squared as he turns back to finish the last of the strawberries. His ears are crimson now, and the giddiness only grows in Phainon’s chest.

Mydei is adorable. Radiant and powerful, yes, terrifying—especially on the battlefield— yes, but simultaneously the cutest person that Phainon has ever had the pleasure of meeting. And with his nape bared, messy red strands pushed away, Phainon finds himself approaching Mydei once more, his legs moving on their own. His fangs have begun to elongate with the anticipation of sheathing themselves into an omega’s neck.

Did he imagine it? The pomegranate that burst forth in the air, sweet and tart, lasting for less than a moment. His entire body tingles. His arms find their way around Mydei’s waist— narrower than what he expects for an alpha like Mydei—and he buries his nose in that pristine nape. Soft  strands tickle his nose, the faint scent of mellow but fruity shampoo filling his senses.

He searches for the scent, lips pressed against the soft skin. Beneath his tight grip, Mydei stiffens, trembling ever so slightly like silent prey caught beneath the grasp of a curious predator.

“Oh, my…” Castorice murmurs, entranced.

Phainon’s tongue peaks out to have a taste, his fangs scratching softly against the smooth, feverish skin. A soft whine falls from Mydei’s lips—music to Phainon’s ears—yet he keeps still, stiff as a board.

“Perfect!” Castorice claps. The sound of pen scratching against paper grows louder, more fervent. “Stay there! Don’t let go, Lord Phainon. Even if Lord Mydei tries to push you away, you have to hold on!”

His fangs ache. The pomegranate scent is gone, but the fire has been lit, the flames stoked by the desire brewing in his chest.

“Mydei…” Phainon murmurs. The temptation to sink his fangs in is paralyzing. He continues to lick softly at the patch of skin as if attempting to ease out the sweet pomegranate that had permeated only moments before, as if Mydei owned that scent.

Only Mydei isn’t an omega so there’s no way that scent came from him… Right?

His body tingles. Did he envision it then? Mydei’s skin is soft and supple. His fangs could pierce through with ease, drawing Mydei’s cries and rivulets of golden blood. Mydei would bear his mark and—

An elbow to the gut has him slammed back to reality.

ོ༘₊⁺☀︎₊⁺⋆.˚

That night, Phainon fucks into his fist until his cock aches and his knot no longer forms. His fangs continue to ache with the need to pierce tender skin, and he bites his bottom lip until blood drips down his chin to stop from groaning out Mydei’s name. They’re separated, a few walls away, but he’s already made a fool of himself too many times.

If Mydei were to hear him chanting his name while rutting into his fist, he would never live it down.

Little does he know, Mydei does the same. Fucks himself on his fingers until his vision whites, and he collapses into a heap of warm pillows and blankets.

ོ༘₊⁺☀︎₊⁺⋆.˚

Hyacine arrives early, little Ica floating beside her. In her hands is a platter of sweet meats, figs, and decadent cheeses.

She exclaims her greetings, her sweet features lit up with excitement as she chats with the three of them. It’s then she notices the tacky antique vases stacked in the corner of the living room. A jarring new addition to the once harmonious decor.

Lounging on the living room kline, Phainon supplies, “I brought them over when I moved in. The best of my collection, and they’re all real! Not a single fake in sight!”

“Right,” Hyacine laughs. Her grip tightens around the platter as she forces a grin. “The living room does look more lively…”

The words process. In an instant, all joy is wiped away and the color drains from her face. Hyacine stares at the antiques as if they have personally offended her.

“...” Hyacine sways. Little Ica makes a loud trilling noise, nudging its face against her cheek.

Alarmed, Mydei starts, “Hyacine—”

“What do you mean you’re living here?!” Hyacine shrieks. Her face cycles between horror, shock, and resignation before returning back to horror. The platter wobbles in her grip, and Mydei quickly grabs ahold of it before she inadvertently drops the entire thing.

“I moved in a week ago,” Phainon recounts.

“Why.” Hyacine’s voice pitches low.

Phainon blinks. “I wanted to live with my friends?”

“Oh, dear. No… Nonononono… This can’t be happening…” Hyacine mutters. She shakes her head fervently as if trying to wake herself from a bad dream, pink pigtails bobbing wildly back and forth. With pleading eyes, she looks over to Castorice who is suddenly very interested in studying her nails.

“Hyacine,” Phainon tests. “Are you okay? Do you need to lie down?”

“Fine!” Hyacine squeaks, giving a forced smile. “Amazing! Thank you for asking!”

The concern on Mydei’s expression grows, and Phainon gives a nervous laugh. Castorice starts whistling, tapping her feet against the plush carpet as she grabs her cup of tea and chugs it in one go.

“Excuse us,” Hyacine says before she stomps up to Mydei and clamps her hand around his wrist. Without another word, she drags him into the hallway.

A door slams, and Phainon is left deeply confused. He almost wants to chase after them, but little Ica blocks his way, shooting loud trilling noises whenever Phainon gets close. Turning to Castorice for help does nothing because all he receives is a shrug.

Defeated, he flops back onto the living room kline.

Okay, then. Left in the dark once more. He can’t help but be a little worried, even if he knows that he’s overreacting. Mydei is fine. Probably.

If that’s the case then why did Hyacine look so scared?

ོ༘₊⁺☀︎₊⁺⋆.˚

Cipher arrives in all her cat-eared glory, ombre tail whipping back and forth as she greets them, a lilt to her voice. A sharp gaze rakes over his figure, and Mydei feels like a spotlight has been dropped on his head. Again.

It’s like she’s picking him apart, pushing against the cracks in his armor and leaving him open to the elements. It’s disconcerting to say the least. Does she do this with everyone?

“Little lion,” Cipher grins, all glinting eyes and bright teeth. She looks at him in amusement as if she knows something he doesn’t. She purrs as her sharp gaze trails him up and down. “You’re bigger than I imagined.”

It doesn’t escape his notice how Phainon rolls his eyes. Cipher’s grin grows wider, her fangs glinting in the bright light.

“This is Cifera,” Aglaea says. “Cifera, this is Mydeimos.” Her crystalline eyes glow brighter, warmer, and her tone of voice is lighter too, the same wistfulness present as when she first announced that Cipher would be visiting.

“Nice to finally meet you. I’ve heard a lot about you,” Cipher purrs before turning to Castorice and winking.

Castorice coughs.

Even Anaxa arrives. It’s the first time Mydei has seen the green-haired scholar, a beta, fellow Chrysos Heir even if he objects to the title and one of the Seven Sages of the Grove of Epiphany. Aglaea mentioned that he was the one who helped the village chief’s daughter gain entry into the Grove.

There’s no denying the odd tension in the air brought forth by his sudden appearance. Aglaea had requested all heirs at the gathering, and Anaxa had indeed followed her orders, only to state that he had visited for the sole purpose of greeting his previous students.

For a moment, Anaxa's gaze settles on Mydei, and Mydei feels like he's been seen through.

“Quite the complicated relationship they have,” Cipher whispers into his ear as she watches the scholar exit the villa much to Aglaea's dissatisfaction.

Mydei nearly jumps. How did she get behind him?

The gathering carries on without a hitch.

Cipher sits beside him instead of next to Aglaea and spends half the time staring at him. When he turns to ask her what’s wrong, she replies with a simple and quick, “Nothing!”

The dining table is grand, set up with dishes, fresh picked fruits, and beverages of all varieties. Aglaea brought drinks, artisan bottles of assyrtiko grape wine and aged honeymead, while Tribbie brought over fresh baked breads and specialties from Januspolis, juicy roasted meats and savory pies. Even Cipher arrived with a grand platter of seafood, and Mydei couldn't help but wrinkle his nose at the grilled octopus with olive oil and lemon. The tentacles, curled and charred to perfection, taunt him.

In the center of the table is the fruit tart that Mydei had so painstakingly crafted, strawberries, apples, and kiwis carved into animal shapes arranged artfully atop sweet vanilla custard and flaky pastry.

For the most part, Mydei stays quiet and lets the others do the talking. He simply observes, taking small bites of his food and offering his opinions every once in awhile. It doesn’t escape him how Cipher, for all her lax attitude and wide cheshire smiles, seems at odds with herself, uncomfortable with Aglaea’s presence but wishing to close the distance. There’s a barrier between them, a separation that Cipher has built up.

If there’s tension, Aglaea ignores it, even if she’s cognizant of it. She’s only happy to have Cipher back, and it has Mydei wondering what happened between them.

And this entire time, Hyacine eyes him like he’s a bomb about to burst.

She had freaked out at him, panicking over Phainon living in such close proximity, and then slapped a scent patch on his nape. Mydei could only stare in shock as she told him point blank that he was definitely fucked. He had never heard her cuss before, didn’t think she could, but she had been deathly serious.

It itches, the corners of the patch rubbing incessantly against his skin every time he moves his head. His fingers twitch with the desire to rip it off, but thankfully, his hair covers it from sight. He didn’t panic then, and he doesn’t panic now.

Maybe he should. Hyacine shifts in her seat, letting out nervous giggles every so often. Even Little Ica is unnerved, wings flicking as the unicorn nibbles on grapes.

Mydei takes a careful sip of his glass and tries not to wrinkle his nose at the astringency. Ugh. He doesn’t take to wine or alcohol, and no matter how expensive or luxurious. It all tastes the same to him.

“Here,” Phainon whispers, handing over a glass of pomegranate juice.

A kind gesture, so much like Phainon. “Thank you,” Mydei whispers back.

Aglaea and Tribbie chat as they do, the conversation inevitably devolving into how to best destroy the Council of Elders and ensure prosperity of the flame-chase. It starts to get violent with Aglaea musing over different methods of using her golden threads to inflict pain and that’s when Cipher cuts in with, “Let’s talk about something different! More light-hearted, yes?”

Castorice’s expression grows grim. She downs her alcohol in one go and reaches over to pour herself more.

“So, I heard some fun rumors going around. Regarding a little lion,” Cipher purrs, swirling her cup of honeymead around as she reclines on her chair.

“Cifera,” Aglaea speaks up, expression stern.

“I can’t help but be a little curious!” Cipher says as she takes a light sip. “It’s the talk of the city. ”

Her kaleidoscope eyes glint, egging him on. Mydei responds with a simple, “They are unfound.”

Phainon scoffs and murmurs, “Yeah, sure. Remember when you told me that you fucked her for days and brought her back to fuck her some more?” Only he says it a bit too loudly, and the entire table quiets.

Mydei glares, cheeks burning, and Cipher chokes on her drink.

Castorice downs another glass, and Hyacine joins her.

ོ༘₊⁺☀︎₊⁺⋆.˚

In the hours following the gathering, Mydei had spent much of his time cleaning. Phainon had been called away once more and left in a hurry, while Castorice had retired early after much coaxing from Mydei’s part.

A peaceful end to a rather hectic night. He had wiped his hands on the kitchen towel before making his way back to his room. The day’s events had worn him out and he couldn’t wait to finally make it to the safety of his bed.

Only he finds his door ajar. At first, he thinks it’s Phainon’s room, but the closer he approaches, the more confused he gets.

His room had been tightly locked before the gathering began. He checked once. Twice. Then checked again. He had even debated throwing all the pillows and blankets into the closet, making his room appear as it had when he first moved in, but stopped himself short. It was the paranoia speaking.

So, how…?

How could his door be open?

Phainon is standing there with back turned. The click of pills hitting plastic echoes in Mydei’s ears.

“Omega suppressants,” Phainon murmurs, rolling the bottle in his hands. He glances at the other bottle. “And omega scent blockers.”

Mydei rushes in. “What are you doing in my room?”

Phainon turns. “Where did you get these?”

The white bottle in his hand. Mydei’s blood runs cold.

“They’re medications. Why do you look so shocked?” Mydei says, voice remaining remarkably even, even with the thundering of his heart against the confines of his chest.

“Omega suppressants from Hyacine,” Phainon responds. Blue eyes glance over to the mountain of pillows and thick crimson blankets. Rumpled, moonlight fabric rests on a golden pillow, contrasting against the deep, dark colors of the surrounding nest.

Mydei can hardly breathe. He wants to scream at Phainon to get out, but the words don’t leave his throat. A million thoughts run through his mind, countless possibilities. None of this makes sense.

His door had been locked. He triple checked it beforehand, ensuring that no one would be able to enter. There’s only one key, the one he keeps in his… It’s gone.

Fuck.

“So, this is what you’ve been hiding…” Phainon’s grip tightens on the bottle, indenting the thin plastic.

Everything, the entire setup, the bottles out on his counter, his nest fluffed up with Phainon’s chiton out on display, it’s all been placed there on purpose. He had hidden the bottles in his nightstand cabinet and the chiton in the confines of his closet. How—How are they out?

“I didn’t hallucinate that scent either,” Phainon murmurs, more to himself than to Mydei. “It’s been growing stronger these past few days… I thought there was no way, since I’ve been by your side this entire time. When could you have snuck off?”

“Deliverer—”

“Mydei.” Phainon takes a step closer, blue eyes flashing beneath the lamplight. “Is there something you’d like to tell me?”

Chapter Notes

hi, i'm back with another chapter! this is a fun one, i promise 🤭

A whirlwind of excuses run through his mind—all weak and none remotely believable.

Phainon is awaiting a response, but what can he feasibly say? Those aren’t my suppressants, they’re for the mysterious, faceless omega I’ve been fucking behind everyone’s back. You know, the one that brought you into rut, the one that you’re so desperate to find even though you proclaim to dislike omegas and want nothing to do with them.

It’s a weak excuse, and he’s already been found out. A part of him wants to run, but where is there to go?

No. He won’t run. He can’t run, not when the truth is staring him in the eye and demanding him to cower. He keeps his feet planted firmly on the floor and lifts his chin up, challenging Phainon’s authority. To submit is the lowliest of actions.

Regardless of how hard he tries, he can’t help the embarrassment that curls in his chest, nor the burning of his ears. He’s glad it hasn’t migrated over to his face, though his lips tremble and his heart rattles.

“This is what you’ve been hiding from me. This entire time…” Phainon’s expression falls. He twirls the bottle of suppressants in his hand. “It’s no wonder why Aglaea was so insistent about the rumors…”

Phainon stares over at Mydei’s nest, impeccably neat and arranged deliberately, inviting any passing alpha to take a good look. Only a proper omega could have created such a beautiful nest, arranged artfully with silken pillows and soft plushes and covered in thick, warm blankets. Phainon’s gaze trails over the nest to its center—the rumpled moonlight chiton laid atop a pillow, the star of the show.

The urge to bolt grows overwhelming. He stays grounded. A warrior doesn’t run, even if his leg twitches and the voice in the back of his head screams about how he’s made a grave mistake. It’s irrational. He can handle Phainon just fine. There’s that other part of him, the lingering shadow, that whispers for a fight.

“Who else knows?” Phainon asks, voice low, almost scratchy in quality.

The air seems to grow thicker with each word. His eyes hurt from the lamplight.

Mydei says nothing, only continues the haughty expression on his face. Phainon can take his silence however he wishes. There’s little else that needs to be said.

After all, Phainon had broken into his room. He doesn’t deserve answers. Anger burgeons in his chest at the thought. How dare he? To be disrespected like this, to have his privacy thrown away, by his closet ally and friend no less.

“Aglaea and Tribbie know, I’m sure of it. Castorice must also know, given you live with her and she lets you into her nest like it's no big deal. Hyacine because she’s the one who gave you these medications and she’s very particular about giving out those specialty medications. Cipher knows because she…” Phainon trails off, turning his head to the side to hide the twist of his expression. “Forget it.”

The windows are strewn shut, and the room is warm, two bodies sharing the same space.

“Bravo,” Mydei says, forcing the words out. “Should I clap for you, now that you’ve figured it out? Perhaps, a celebration is in order since you’ve finally grown a brain.”

The wide-eyed look Phainon gives—the audacity—has Mydei sneering.

His door is still ajar. His chest feels like it’s about to burst, and his vision streaks red. Why is Phainon even in his bedroom? How did he even get in? The nest was placed by someone else, that much rings clear, so someone must have led him here.

It’s inevitable, with so many alphas crowded about in the same space, spending day in and day out with little reprieve. The barracks get messy, especially when recruits become of age, their ruts making them more prone to aggression.

Mydei lets Krateros drag him off, his chest heaving with each breath. It’s a struggle to keep himself upright.

The grooves of Krateros’ lined face are more pronounced. He looks like he’s lost weight and gained years, not in wisdom but in stress. His beard is a lighter grey, no longer the dark brown it had once been. His left eye, blinded, looks milkier than it had been, the corners lined red.

Towering olive and oak trees cast speckled shadows on the grass. Mydei stands across from Krateros, keeping a distance. While Krateros doesn’t smell as offensive as the other alphas, his scent still has Mydei on edge.

Krateros says, voice low with urgency. “Mydeimos, you need to go.”

The spring air is fresh and free of pheromones. He can finally breathe again, taking in deep breaths to get rid of the alpha coating his lungs.

“It’s not safe for you here,” Krateros continues.

“It’s not safe for me here?” Mydei echos, crossing his arms. “Am I not the leader of the Kremnoans?”

“Don’t be daft.”

“I’m only getting started. Isn’t it your desire to have me more present?” Mydei says. He cracks his neck and rolls his shoulders. A part of him wants to continue with the spars, but he had left the challengers in rough shape, going too far in the blaze of battle. Phainon could easily match him, a voice whispers. He ignores it. “I have time today.”

“Are you looking to go into heat in front of everyone? If that is your choice, so be it. I won’t be able to rescue you if it comes to it.”

Mydei freezes.

“There are hundreds of alphas here. You may be strong, my young lord, but do not overestimate yourself when surrounded by this many pent-up soldiers.”

Mydei steadies his breathing. “I have no clue what you’re talking about.”

“You’re on the verge of collapse,” Krateros says. “And you’re agitating the soldiers. It won’t end well. Heed my warning, Mydeimos. I know you better than you think.”

“I don’t—I’ve never—I’m not an omega,” he chokes out. His words shake with a type of urgency, a need to convince, though he’s aware it’s futile.

Krateros knows and has known for a while now.

“I am aware of my limits,” Mydei says before turning and walking back into the training hall.

The mood of the soldiers has changed, even as they continue through structured training drills. Some soldiers eye him with disdain, while others turn away the moment Mydei looks in their direction.

His boots echo off the stone floor as he makes his way toward the omega recruits. He sticks with them. Every so often, his vision fades in and out, but it’s bearable. His thighs, however, are grossly wet, and he’s sure his pants have already soaked through.

“Lord Mydei—” Iavokos begins, noticing the lack of color in his face.

“I’m fine,” Mydei manages, staggering. “Continue with the drills.”

The atmosphere is stifling. Everywhere he turns, there’s another alpha soldier, eyeing him, watching him.

He feels exposed, naked. The scent patches  rub against his skin and he wants so badly to rip them off and rake his nails down his nape until liquid gold runs down his back. Anything to make the ache stop.

There’s a force pushing him down like hands gripping his throat.

When he’s with the omega recruits, it’s easier. They don’t eye him like they’re expecting something from him. He feels safer with them, less a fish out of water when once the training hall had been his safe place.

“My young lord,” Krateros says, approaching once more. The concern in his grey eyes has Mydei faltering. He hasn’t seen such an expression in years.

“I’ll go,” Mydei bites out. “Keep an eye out on the soldiers.”

In a daze, Mydei stumbles around the Kremnoan district, following the familiar stone paths he knows like the back of his hand.

He had been here for all of it, the construction of the temple of Nikador, a pathetic imitation of what they have in Castrum Kremnos but enough for his people to worship, the creation of the central plaza with the lionhead fountain, crafted by a now retired renowned Kremnoan craftsman.

The bustle of the plaza doesn’t match that of Mamorael Market, but the Kremnoans have carved out their own subset of the city for themselves.

Mydei stays in the shadows, walking through corridor after corridor. He doesn’t go into the light, unable to brave the dawn’s rays. There’s no need for the extra attention, not when his vision fades in and out every few seconds.

Vendors shout their wares. Kremnoan children laugh as they scurry around, wooden swords in hand.

“I want to be a big strong warrior! Like Lord Mydeimos!” a little boy says, waving his sword around.

His friend laughs and chases after him.

Mydei continues to walk, listless in his step. The walls are caving in on him. He stumbles through the alleyways until he lands in front of a familiar mural. He knows this as the decorated path of strife that goes straight to the main temple of Nikador. Various paintings of Castrum Kremnos through the ages line the stone walls, stories of the glorious triumphs of the once prosperous city state and of the celebrated violence that Kremnoans had inflicted on their path to glory.

King Gorgo stands atop a cliff, triumphant after slaying the feared Chryseus Leo with his bare hands. He dangles the beast’s head, a crown of gold and rubies atop his head, red cape fluttering in the breeze. The beast’s dead body is beside him and below are his subjects, cheering and offering up their praises. At the top of the mural, Nikador shines in a radiant light, the titan gazing down on the victorious king.

Mydei runs his hand over the painting, dust building on the leather of his gauntlets.

Castrum Kremnos had been founded by an alpha king, had been maintained by generation after generation of alpha rulers. There’s never been an omega on the throne, never a chance to allow what they deemed as weakness on the throne.

But he can’t change who he is. He can hide, yes. He can pretend all he wants, ignore the fire and ache brewing beneath his skin, the wetness between his legs, but the truth remains. He wonders how his mother must think of him, how disappointed she must be that her son is so weak. He’s never met her, never knew her before he had been thrown into the sea, even if her signet ring weighs in his pocket.

His countrymen are so blinded in their belief of him being an alpha when he had never proclaimed to be one. It was never a question of his secondary gender. Alpha or nothing. That’s how it was, and at the time, he hadn’t cared. It was no bother what his countrymen assumed as long as he was able to keep the peace.

His eyes burn, and before he knows it, a tear runs down his cheek and more follow. He leans his forehead against the stone wall, hiding his shame from view. He only hopes no one passes by, but that’s a tall order. It doesn’t matter.

A tear lands on the stone floor. A lily blooms, beautiful, fragile white petals, lightly pink in the center. He bends down and holds it, cradling it as if it were his child.

In a day's time, the lily will wilt and die. Its delicate beauty is fleeting, awash by the tides of time until only a memory remains. Softly sweet and delicate, many would view it as weakness.

He holds in a sob. His breaths come out shaky.

The flower crystallizes. His vision swirls.

Mydei blacks out.

The evernight is a wasteland of the broken.

Echoes of the past whisper for the times long lost, and the remnants of once powerful, vibrant city-states stand cloaked in darkness. There’s nothing here but the forces of nature that have wrangled back control. Curling vines crawl through decrepit buildings and tufts of grass burst through splintered tile floors.

Phainon treks up the winding stone path, careful not to stumble into any loose branches. It’s a windy night, the evergreen leaves rustle a gentle whisper in his ear. This is what is left of Amphoreus—ruins of civilizations that no longer stand, save for broken passages and crumbled tomes, unreadable from decay. Every time he ventures out, he’s struck with the reality that Okhema is all there is left of the once proud and lively Amphoreus. The last bastion of humanity.

Enchanted bronze braziers light his way, as if expecting his arrival. It’s a little eerie, but he’s glad for the light and the clear direction forward. His boots clack upon stone.

Titankin crawl in these sorts of areas, attracted to the energies of once sacred prayer grounds. The desecration of these one glorious temples by creatures of the night and the corruption that stains Amphoreus is a pity, but it does serve as great areas for testing his combat prowess.

Normally, he’d have Mydei here with him. They would compete over who could kill more titankin or who could reach the highest level of the temple first, all in the name of friendly rivalry. Grim situations are better with another, especially someone as effortlessly powerful and confident as Mydei.

Only now… Phainon forces a smile, if only to keep his morale up. He doesn’t want to think about it.

Combat comes easy for a warrior like him. His entrance into the temple is met with a hoard of monsters. Titankin after titankin fall. The veins in his arms bulge with each slash.

He loses himself to the rhythm of battle. Adrenaline lights up his body. He had forewent the patches and lotions completely, allowing his scent to flow free, unrestricted. Monsters grow vicious in his presence, attracted to the scent of death and destruction, the char of ash from smoking battlefields. It feels good letting loose and allowing his weapon to speak for him. The titankin stand no chance. He slices through them as if they were made of butter.

The mission Aglaea had given him had been simple—clear out as many monsters as possible and explore a recently discovered temple of Oronyx for any signs of the titan and coreflame. She had called him up for an impromptu meeting, a knowing look in her eye as she laid out the instruction. If she hadn’t given him the mission, more an excuse to get him out of Okhema than anything else, he would have left on his own. He’d rather brave the cold of the evernight than stay in Okhema amidst the shame and embarrassment and the realization that this entire time, he had been oblivious to what had been so obvious.

Because fuck.

He doesn’t think he can face Mydei ever again. Not after that.

It was as he had feared. There was a distance between them that couldn’t be breached. Mydei didn’t trust him, and he blew any chance of Mydei ever trusting him.

His movements are swift, precise. He lashes out, baring his canines as he slams through a hoard of monsters. He blows through an entire floor’s worth in less than an hour.

He had shed his ruined outercoat and armor long ago, leaving himself in only a high collared compression shirt. Not the best protection against the monster’s blades, he can admit. Aglaea is sure to give him an earful when he returns, but that’s the least of his worries. Normally, he’s particular about keeping his clothing and appearance as pristine as possible, but not this time.

There’s a light trickling of stale water from what was once a grandiose waterfall, the scent of mildew and dirt flourishing in the damp air. The statue of Oronyx in the center of the hall has eroded into nothing but a slab of cracked stone and the base it had been standing on.

Sweat beads his brow, and he wipes it away. He takes in the sight, at the staircase that beckons him upwards. There’s nothing here aside from monsters.

“So, how’d it go?” Cipher asks.

Phainon jolts and nearly swings his greatsword at her. Luckily, he catches himself in time and it embeds into the stone beside her feet.

He catches his breath and says, “How do you think it went?” He yanks his weapon out, causing a splintering in the already crumbling temple floor.

Cipher whistles. “Judging from the lack of Mydei and the atrocious alpha pheromones stinking up the place, I’m guessing not so great…”

Phainon stalks up the staircase. The last person he wants to see is Cipher, but once she’s sunk her claws into a victim, she doesn’t let go. He’s the latest in her games.

Somehow, she’s there when he makes it to the top. It’s darker up here. No flickering flames to light the way, no gleaming of magical runes carved into the temple wall. It’s also smaller, and his pheromones saturate the space with no path of escape. Cipher reacts, and Phainon holds himself back before he can ask her what’s wrong.

“I’ve never met an alpha who smells like you do,” Cipher says, wrinkling her nose. She fans the air, as if it would make a difference. “Emotional alphas smell musty and sour. It’s disgusting. But you… you smell like how Dolos did when it was destroyed.”

“I didn’t think I would have company,” Phainon grits his teeth. “Forgive me for not preparing ahead of time.”

It takes a few moments for her words to register. To other alphas, he’s been told he smells like an opponent, a foe to cut down, conquer. To betas, his scent is unpleasant and acrid, but to omegas, he smells like a calamity.

Omegas seek warmth and comfort, and Phainon is the very opposite. He’s taken solace in it. It’s night impossible to change his charred scent, nor remove the memories of the day his life as a simple village boy burned into ashes before his very eyes.

“Aren’t you an alpha?” he asks.

From the darkness, a titankin comes barreling at them. In one fluid motion, Cipher jumps to the side, the monster’s blade missing her by a mere centimeter. “Ouch! That one almost got to me!”

Phainon cuts it down.

The demigod of trickery has no scent. Tales spin her as an alpha, and it’s regarded as fact that she is indeed one, for how could the legendary cat thief be anything but an alpha? Either way, it doesn’t matter. Whatever she is, she’s still Cipher.

And by that, he means a nuisance. When he met her for the first time, many years ago, he wanted to be her friend. She looked rather lonely, hiding in the shadows as she stared at the laughing children. Her expression had been one of yearning, but she remained in the dark. It was as if there was a barrier that she couldn’t cross, unable to brave the dawn’s rays for longer than a moment’s notice. All it took was one look, and he knew they couldn’t be friends. He had been sneered at, mocked as Okhema’s darling. Aglaea’s new favorite.

The second floor is the same as the first, down to the decrepit waterfall and remains of the Oronyx statue. He takes little note of it. Many multifloored temples follow in a similar format.

The coreflame of Oronyx is a mystery. No one knows where the titan has gone. The discovery of this newly unearthed temple could give answers, or it could be yet another dead end. The trees had grown dense, covering it from view. For a temple to be in the middle of the forest, between large stretches of civilization, it left a less than stellar omen. But a clue is a clue, and Aglaea needed someone experienced to chase it down.

Cipher lets out a sigh of relief. “So, the cat’s out of the bag!”

“...” Phainon braces himself.

“Mydei is in heat,” Cipher continues.

His throat closes. Against common sense, he asks, “And how is that my problem?”

He doesn’t wait for her to answer. There are more titankin to kill. In one swift movement, he hacks through two more. They aren’t particularly difficult monsters to defeat, given their lack of self-awareness. The ones corrupted by the black tide are a great deal heartier, their touch corrosive, but, like the rest of the monsters that lurk in the evernight, they fall to his greatsword.

“He’s been calling for you in his sleep,” Cipher says, pouncing in front of him before leaning forward, beckoning him closer as if revealing a great secret. “Our little immortal prince has been murmuring Deliverer over and over in that mighty cute way of his. You know, the one where he sounds like a purring lion.”

“Probably because he’s thinking of strangling me. Thank you for that, by the way.”

Cipher has the audacity to laugh and clap him on the back, acting as if he’s told a great joke.

It’s not funny. His eye twitches, but he steadies himself. Cipher wants him to react, that much is true. He’s not giving it to her.

“Contrary to what you think, I’m not here to sabotage you,” she says. “I’ve been on your side since the beginning.”

In a flash, she’s gone and two nearby titankin slam onto the ground, kicking up a storm of dust. “I simply wanted you to confess.” She drags one dead titankin atop another and smushes them together. They fall in a tangled heap onto the floor. “Like that!”

Phainon grimaces. Not the greatest visual, but it does its job. If only it were that easy.

“A grand exchange of love and passion! The two of you falling into bed together and ending this whole tiresome situation. Mnestia must be in deep despair watching the two of you prance around each other like you’re both barefoot, stepping on hot coals.”

It sounds too idealistic to ever come true. Did she think it was that easy? Mydei doesn’t even desire him that way. He also doesn’t know where the signet ring went, considering Cipher had snatched it away from him again before he could even think of formulating a plan to confess.

“Where did you put the ring?” Phainon asks.

Cipher smiles. “Use that pretty little head of yours.”

“His nest,” Phainon states. Internally, he curses himself.

“Bingo!”

Of course it was in Mydei’s nest. Where else would it have been? No wonder he couldn’t find it. Entering Mydei’s room had been a bad decision all around. He shouldn’t have gone in, but he needed the ring back, and Cipher wouldn’t tell him where she hid it.

“If you want it, go and find it~” she had told him, gesturing to Mydei’s room, the door swung wide open. “Or he will. I’m sure you don’t want to ruin the surprise. It’d be a shame…”

She opened the door wider, giving Phainon a glimpse of Mydei’s bed and what looked to be… a nest?

It was a momentary impulse. His first instinct had been, was the omega there with him? Living with him? Jealousy curled in his gut, overtaking all reason. Yet, he remained planted, conflicted.

So, Cipher, legendary speed and all, disappeared then reappeared behind him and kicked him straight into the room. He tumbled and landed facefirst onto the floor, right in front of the impeccably prepared nest. His fate was sealed.

He should have left immediately. Had his brains not been a jumble and the flames of jealousy stoked in his chest, maybe he would have. Unfortunately, he stayed.

A mistake. A lapse in judgement. Mydei hates him now, and he deserves it.

“I was saving it,” Phainon says. “I wanted the perfect time to give it to him, to make my feelings known.”

“And that’s why you suck!” Cipher twirls her finger around in a spinning motion. “Mr. Boring! It’s always the same answer from you.”

Phainon frowns. His grip on his greatsword tightens.

“At the rate you were going, you would have never confessed if I didn’t throw you off the deep end. You keep second guessing yourself.”

“You’re having fun with this, aren’t you?”

“Maybe a little!” Cipher tries a grin, but her lips shake at the corners. She clears her throat and promptly steps on the wrong tile.

There’s a clicking noise, then silence.

“Oops,” Cipher says. “Wasn’t supposed to do that…”

“What did you do?”

The floor begins to rumble, and Cipher grabs him by the collar. In a flash, they land on a platform above, just in time to watch a trap door open from where they had just been standing. “These interruptions. Ugh. Anyways, you’re wasting your time, you know.”

Phainon yanks himself out of her grasp. His heart feels like it’s about to pop. “You set me up.”

“I did. Had I not done anything, would you have ever confessed to Mydei?”

“I was waiting for the right time.”

“And when would that be?”

“... I was working on it.”

Cipher’s eye twitches. It doesn’t escape Phainon’s notice of how she’s trying her best not to breathe in his presence.

“Do you want me to confess to him for you?” Cipher asks, venom dripping with each word. “You can take the spoils. That way you won’t fuck up again. Little lion will never know. I’m a great actress! The best, actually.” She sobers up at the end.

Phainon shakes his head. Nothing that comes out of her mouth can be trusted. What is her end goal? It’s nigh impossible to elucidate the strange workings of her mind nor does he want to try. If she were to pretend to be him, it’d be a great way to make an already precarious situation worse, especially if Mydei were to find out.

But that being said, how did he not notice it sooner? It was obvious by all means that Mydei wasn’t an alpha. Had he been so blindsided to believe in what Mydei, himself, had never confirmed?

Cipher remains a wide distance away from him, gaze studying the remnants of the Oronyx statue at the end of the hall.

They make it up the next staircase. Another dark, dusty hallway full of titankin and another main hall with the same waterfall and statue. Unfortunately, Phainon’s a little distracted to take note.

“He’s an omega,” Phainon says. By now, his compression shirt has started to shred, and his arms are littered with small cuts that drip gold.

Cipher remains unscathed save for the scrunching of her expression every so often. “Yes, he is. Very observant of you.”

“How did I not get it sooner?”

“It’s not all your fault,” Cipher says, and that rouses him more than any of her jabs. “Well, sort of. Eh, kind of?”

“What?” Phainon asks.

“Don’t worry your pretty little head about that,” Cipher waves him off. The cat-shaped accessory on her neck clacks as she turns back to stare at him. “Anyhow, this is where we’re at right now. The little lion is in heat. What will you do?”

“I—”

“Wrong.”

“I haven’t even said anything yet.”

“Yeah, because whatever nonsense comes out of that giant mouth of yours will only worsen the situation! So, I’m gonna tell you what to do.”

Phainon feels a headache incoming. “What makes you think I’ll trust you?”

“Considering the choices you have made thus far have led you nowhere, I would say you have a pretty good chance!”

“I don’t need your help.” He really doesn’t,

“The veil has been lifted, yet you still act like this…” Cipher sighs, shaking her head. She looks back at him, pity in her eyes, as if she’s staring at a helpless little puppy instead of a grown man.

He’s missing a big piece in the puzzle, he’s aware of that, but he also doesn’t expect to be given any answers. That’s how it’s been lately. Left in the dark.

Regardless, he asks, “What veil?”

As he expects, Cipher doesn’t respond. Instead, she hops off the platform and scurries around the hall, clicking all sorts of mechanisms, messing with runes, and toppling pillars. Loud thuds echo through the hall, creating enough of a ruckus to summon a hoard of titankin swarming in their direction.

“What are you doing?!” Phainon yells as he parries an attack. One of them manages to slice his cheek, dripping gold down his face.

“You piss me off,” Cipher says. “What can I say? It’s fun testing what goes on in these temples. Use that brain of yours. You have one, right? We’ve been stuck on this floor for a while now.”

“Oh.” He’s never been met with this sort of trap before, but he also doesn’t take to exploring temples of Oronyx. “Is that why you haven’t dragged me back to Okhema? We can’t leave.”

“You only noticed now?” Cipher says. “And you’re supposed to be the grand hero of deliverance, savior of Amphoreus, usherer of the Era Nova? Stupid alpha…”

He can’t argue, not when he’s slamming titankin into the ground and chasing after Cipher who’s somersaulting over the crumbling floors and monsters with ease, leaving Phainon to fend for himself.

She shouts at him, “Ever since we got to this floor, it’s been the same. This is why you don’t go into suspicious looking temples alone! Surely, that’s the first thing Aglaea taught you. Where’s your survival instinct, rascal?”

“This was a solo mission,” Phainon says, narrowly evading the swing of a blade. Sweat stings his eyes as he jumps onto another platform. He nearly slips on a puddle and falls on his face.

“See how frustrating this is?” Cipher continues, watching Phainon struggle to steady his breathing. “This is how I feel dealing with you.”

Phainon glares at her. His arms tremble from exertion, from killing what felt like a thousand titankin in the span of an hour.

“Ha! Finally!” Cipher grins, looking so proud of herself with her chest puffed out like she’s won a prize. “I didn’t know Okhema’s golden boy could glare like that! Oh, how scary!” She pouts and places a hand on her chest. “If only someone would come and save me! Princess Homebody, perhaps… Maybe I should call her, she would know how to deal with you.”

The reminder of Castorice lights an idea in his head. She had dealt with something like this before and had made haste to alert the other heirs about it. A time loop mechanism, she called it.

“The Oronyx statue,” Phainon says, pointing to it. “The enchantment is connected to the statue.”

“Bravo! Took you long enough!” Cipher exclaims, propelling herself forwards.

He only wishes he had her agility. What he lacks in speed, he matches in strength. His calf muscles burn, and his canines sink into his lip. His bangs fly in his face, but he can’t stall. They have to get out of here.

Cipher turns back and says, “You know, Cassie wanted you to confess on your own. She didn’t want me to step in. She’s been trying to nudge you two together for some time now.”

I know, Phainon wants to say. It’s rather obvious that she’s been trying to push them together, but Mydei isn’t moved in the slightest. Even after all the scenting, the touches in the baths…

Shouldn’t Mydei be aware of it? The boundaries that have been crossed.

When they make it to the statue, Phainon is heaving for air, hands on his knees. He’s sure that once this whole ordeal is over, he’ll be sore all over. Even his biceps are beginning to cramp.

Cipher places her hand on the Oronyx symbol carved at the base and whispers what sounds to be a prayer. Behind the statue, two pathways manifest, one carved with a symbol of the moon and the other the sun.

“Mmm, quite the sticky situation we’re in,” Cipher laughs. Her nose wrinkles. “Let’s split up.”

Phainon frowns. “Didn’t you say—”

“Let’s split up,” Cipher bites out. “You try your best to figure your way out, and I will too. We don’t have time. You want to get out of here or not? You have your omega waiting for you.”

“My omega?” Phainon echoes.

“Yes, you idiot,” Cipher hisses. “Now, get a move on.”

Against better judgement, he splits up with Cipher.

ོ༘₊⁺☀︎₊⁺⋆.˚

Water.

Everywhere.

In his lungs. Burning his eyes. Flooding his ears.

Each gulp is another mouthful. His lungs burn. The rest of his body is cold.

He tries to thrash, but there’s nothing to grab, only the silence of the water and the hideous monsters that lurk beneath its endless depths. The light grows dimmer, his struggles for naught. His limbs don’t respond to his commands like he’s been strapped down with lead weights.

Alarms blare in his head. Panic sets in.

Another gasp for air. Another flood of water.

It burns.

Mydei falls.

Weak. Why is he so weak? He should be stronger. He needs to be stronger—He needs… He— He…

Then nothing.

“It is not your time, my child,” a female voice whispers, gentle and warm. Once again, Mydei is greeted by the silhouette of a woman, the one that guides him towards the light, as she does, time and time again. He hasn’t met her in years, and it’s almost a comfort to see her.

He knows what’s coming next.

His eyes snap open, yet he’s still submerged by the tides. Once more, water floods his lungs, and he gasps and flails and struggles. The weight remains tied to his limbs, his movements weak, his body uncooperative, and he continues to sink.

His lungs give out. His heart stops. The cycle repeats.

Eventually, the monsters, jagged, vicious creatures that swarm the abyssal depths, find him, eager to take their meal. He’s torn to shreds. Stitched back together again. Then torn to shreds once more. The woman’s voice whispers in his ear, dragging him back to the world of the living. He sees her, and she always says the same, her presence familiar in a way that it shouldn't be but is.

He tries to reach for the light, the surface where stars meet the sky, but he’s dragged down before he can even hope to break the water.

This shouldn’t be happening. Panic burgeons. He’s not an infant anymore. He’s braved the sea of souls and left victorious. So, how? How is he back here? Even as he sinks, his arm shoots for the surface, pitiful and futile.

Time slows. The fever lessens, then stops. The weight upon his body is removed, and he has control once again. He tears the sea monsters into shreds with his bare hands, crimson blooming like lilies in the water.

He makes it to shore. The fire has long been quenched, and he remains as he had before, unscathed, save for the memories, hazy as they are. There’s no telling how long he’s been down there, and his body remains pristine, bearing no marks, no scars.

He kneels in the sand, the push of salty water against his knees. Crabs scuttle in the sand, and the crash of waves is loud in his ears.

Stars spot the night sky. Far away and out of reach. In a trance, he reaches out regardless, a cold breeze against his wet skin like a caress of the damned.
